open.full: prior art: foul play (pmariglia) — a singles mcts bot at top-100, and it has four things we have as open defects. it moved from expectiminimax (every possibility, ~5 turns, ran out of clock) to mcts (promising branches ~10+ turns, unpromising ones minimally) — which is the question #62 exists to answer, already answered by someone who shipped. its four techniques land on #24 (roll grouping), #32/#35 (likelihood-weighted chance nodes), xatu/slowking (hidden info as a filtered possibility set, not a point estimate — it keeps candidate sets per opposing pokémon and narrows them as the battle reveals things; we pick one most-likely set) and #43 (reverse damage-calc inference). positioning stays clean — singles, species clause, and the source says outright *"specifically in singles, it's not vgc"* — same inputs as our store, different game. and its fairness critique lands on us: a ladder bot is argued unfair rather than merely strong, because a human cannot process branches at that rate under a timer. the paper should meet that deliberately; note the premise is not yet true of us, since miltank needs 26s against a 20s budget (#61). everything here is a video narrator's paraphrase and must be verified against the source before it is cited

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE BLUEPRINT + LIVE RE-SOLVE ARCHITECTURE — WILL, 2026-08-11. *"you know how poker solvers have charts for every scenar
open.full: the blueprint + live re-solve architecture — will, 2026-08-11. *"you know how poker solvers have charts for every scenario that people try and memorize, i want that for us, so we can try searching for the most similar scenario from a repository as well as live rollout"*, alongside *"i dont want to behavior clone first i want to try our searching and poker like simulation"*. this is the architecture that beat humans at nlhe — libratus and pluribus do not play off charts, they compute a coarse blueprint offline and do real-time subgame re-solving at the table. blueprint + live search is exactly what he described, and it is a far better fit here than behaviour cloning: vgc-bench trains offline so inference is cheap, whereas search pays per turn on a clock. the endgame half is already scoped and small — #47 measures 1v1 at 16 cells, 2v1 at 96, 2v2 at ~1,296, with 2v1 alone reachable in 45.9% of games; retrograde analysis builds up from there (#30, #40, #41). the early game is the research problem and it is the abstraction, not the retrieval. poker charts work on isomorphism — a(s)k(s) and a(h)k(h) are one hand — and pokemon has no isomorphism that clean, because which species is on the field is the information content. so the repository needs a learned similarity metric. we have a candidate and it has been tested in the wrong direction: #23 gated porygon2 on whether it can separate positions two turns apart; retrieval needs the inverse, that genuinely similar positions land close. same encoder, opposite test, never run. the honest dependency: the re-solve half needs a fast simulator, which loops back to #62 and to the poke-env benchmark nobody has ever taken

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE END GOAL, STATED SO PRIORITIES CAN BE ARGUED AGAINST IT — WILL, 2026-08-11: *"the end goal is to beat closed team sh
open.full: the end goal, stated so priorities can be argued against it — will, 2026-08-11: *"the end goal is to beat closed team sheets and get to number 1 on the ladder but we are far off"*. it had never been written down, so every ordering argument in this register was being made against a target nobody had stated. it is a curriculum, not a mismatch — will corrected this the same day: *"once we solve open team sheets, we can think about the more difficult closed team sheets and adapt our models accordingly"*. i first filed the open-sheet corpus against a closed-sheet target as a violation of this file's *fitting environment must match playing environment* rule. that was an over-application. the rule governs fitting and playing in the same deployment; deliberately solving the fully-observable version first and adapting afterwards is staging, and staging is how you get a measurable baseline at all. what survives is narrower and still worth holding: a model fitted where every set is known must be able to accept uncertainty about sets later, and that is an architecture question better answered before everything is built assuming certainty — the same lesson as the focus sash drag, where replacing a hedge with a certainty inherited responsibility for every event that staled it. and it flips the poker argument the right way. open sheets strip out most hidden information and make our game easier than poker in the dimension poker is hardest; closed sheets put it back — unknown items, spreads, the fourth move, which four of six they brought — so information sets become the game and #163's blueprint+re-solve becomes the right primitive rather than a flourish. two things already built for other reasons are the closed-sheet machinery: #52 hypno (rate the opponent, decide how hard to exploit — deferred by will) and the prefer observed over declared rule with its knock off / trick / consumed-berry tracking, which is exactly the inference a closed-sheet bot needs. will's own farigiraf/cud chew read is the same idea from the player side: a bluff that exists only because sheets are closed, and that open sheets delete. "far off" is accurate — #62 unanswered, ~26 open rows in the medicham block, no search redesign started

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: ARGMAX IS UNSOUND IN A SIMULTANEOUS-MOVE GAME, AND OPEN TEAM SHEETS DO NOT RESCUE IT — CITED, 2026-08-11. Bosansky, Lisy
open.full: argmax is unsound in a simultaneous-move game, and open team sheets do not rescue it — cited, 2026-08-11. bosansky, lisy, lanctot, cermak & winands, *algorithms for computing strategies in two-player simultaneous move games*, artificial intelligence 237 (2016) 1-40: agents *"may need to use randomized (or mixed) strategies in order to play optimally ... even though the only information that is hidden is each player's action as they play it"*. simultaneity alone forces mixing. i had told will the opposite — that open sheets make our game easier than poker in poker's hardest dimension. on this axis they do not. what medicham is: `miltank.js:1315` is `if (v > bestval) { bestval = v; bestpair = [ia, ib]; }` and `:1384` clicks it — a plain argmax, deterministic by construction, answerable for free by anyone who knows the scorer. magnemite underneath it does sample (`magnemite.js:954`, `:1154`, a softmax its own header calls *"the single biggest measured lever"* and which argues *"taking the argmax would be the obvious thing and it is wrong here"*), so the bot gets less mixed as it gets smarter — the 31.6% of turns miltank defers are the only ones that come out mixed, which inverts #62: more compute means fewer deferrals means more predictable. duct is not the fix — i had it in the fix list and the paper reports it *"also might not converge to a nash equilibrium"*, even the mixed variant; uct's failure is shown on biased rock-paper-scissors (shafiei, sturtevant & schaeffer, giga 2009). what is sound, three tiers from that paper: exact backward induction solving the matrix game per node, which *"outputs a subgame perfect ne"*; sm-oos, which *"guarantee[s] to closely approximate the optimal strategies given enough time"*; and sm-mcts-rm (regret matching at simultaneous nodes) as the practical middle. so roadmap #41's python equilibrium solver is the textbook-correct primitive for this game class, currently filed as *"the equilibrium answer exists and cannot play"*. and unlike pluribus we are 1v1 zero-sum, so the *"equilibrium is not the right goal"* retreat does not apply to us — equilibrium is the target here. phase 3, not now: medicham is phase 1 and a correct simulator is a prerequisite under every version of this. registered so it is not rediscovered

open.title: SITRUS BERRY FIRES ON THE WRONG SIDE OF ITS OWN THRESHOLD, BOTH DIRECTIONS. `test-tag-wire`: *"at 40% it eats the berry
open.full: sitrus berry fires on the wrong side of its own threshold, both directions. `test-tag-wire`: *"at 40% it eats the berry and heals exactly 1/4"* fails at 18/170 with item `''`, and *"at 80% the berry stays in the pocket — the threshold is the tag's, not a vibe"* fails too. failing in both directions means the threshold is not being read at all rather than being read wrongly. the artifact is proven correct in the same run (*"sitrus declares its own threshold and restore (was a name check in the residual loop)"*), so this is a consumer gap. note for whoever takes it: the berry work closed earlier in this sprint reported `sitrus 118`, so a live counter may be firing while this fixture is not — establish which is wrong before editing the engine, because a broken probe has already cost this project a session (`docs/lessons.md` §5) | closed 2026-08-11 — the engine was never broken and this row misdiagnosed it. one defect explains all four: `_chooseaction`'s last fallback clicked struggle past a legal button (the #152 block, whose own comment stated the bug in place — *"a body with legal status moves left is not on struggle"* — and filed it as the lesser evil). struggle is a 50 bp attack with 1/4-max recoil, so every fixture body holding a single protect or roost was hitting the thing under test and paying for it. heat wave never touched the partner: the trace reads `|move|p2b: whimsicott|struggle

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: TWENTY ARTIFACTS WERE NEITHER CLEARED NOR WITHHELD, AND THE SENTENCE EXPLAINING WHY HAD BEEN FALSE FOR TWO DAYS — DONE (
open.full: twenty artifacts were neither cleared nor withheld, and the sentence explaining why had been false for two days — done (discovery), open (re-run). `engine/quarantine.js` printed *"provenance.js finds a writer only in engine/ and build/"* beside twenty files. `gen_dirs` has held `tests/` since 2026-08-09 (#105) and the stated reason applied to none of them. it survived because the set was computed by subtraction — list `data/`, remove what has a row — and a subtraction returns the same list whatever the cause, so nothing could contradict the caption. an unknown is a row now: `provenance.js` emits `unknown: true`, `by: null` and a derived reason for every file in `data/`, `--graph --json` carries them, and `quarantine.js` reads that set instead of growing its own. one of the twenty was a real miss and it was the release pointer — `data/engine-release.json`, the file every frozen measurement resolves through, written via a same-file helper and one hop of object-property indirection. 181 -> 182 rows, `path variable` 64 -> 65, no existing attribution moved; 19 explicit unknowns from 5 derived causes. shown red three times: against the old code (3 of 5 assertions fail), with the scratch-tree guard disabled (the pointer misattributes to `tests/test-miltank-release.js`, which writes that basename into a temp dir as a fixture), and with `provenance.js` blinded to one file (`quarantine.js` still names it, with `no reason recorded`). the fix would have introduced the same class of failure: unknown rows fed into the classification loop come out `quarantined: false` because no clause fires on a null writer, and `web/build-quarantine.js` asks only whether a row exists — twenty artifacts would have moved from `unclassified` to `clear` on the site, in the permissive direction, through a change to the one thing that exists to refuse to default. split out before classification. still open — no staleness verdict was published: engine was rewriting `tag_dex.js`, `tags.json` and `medicham2-browser.js` throughout and a release was cut mid-run, so every provenance verdict beside this must be re-run on a settled tree; `data/quarantine-stamp.json` is unsafe by construction (it digests both edited files); and `node engine/quarantine.js --check` was deliberately not run, because with the gate transiently open it rewrites `citation_sites` to `[]` and a gate that closes again would then flag every existing citation as new

open.full: a green census count cannot detect an over-match, and the working rule would have passed one — 2026-08-11. while splitting the protection counter the first shield dispatch matched on `stallcounterchecks`, and endure is a `stallingmove` that rolls the same die and blocks nothing. it became a shield and broke both endure probes. `live` read 444 before and 444 after — two probes broke and two arrived, and the count is a net. only `missing` moving 0 -> 2 caught it. the working practice "confirm `live` went up" is therefore not a check at all against this failure mode, and it is the practice most often used, because it is the number printed largest. fixed with a sixth tag, `shieldsuser`, derived from `checkmovebypassesprotect` on the volatile\'s own condition — 5 members, endure correctly absent. the row is the rule change, not the bug: a census movement must be reported as arrived/broke/net, never as a net alone, and `missing` must be read beside `live` every time

open.title: THE EFFECTIVE-IDENTITY RATCHET WAS RESTAMPED WHOLESALE, ON WILL'S INSTRUCTION, AND 964 READS WENT IN UNREVIEWED — 2026-0
open.full: the effective-identity ratchet was restamped wholesale, on will's instruction, and 964 reads went in unreviewed — 2026-08-11. will, asked whether to walk the reads or reset the reference point: *"restamp i guess"*. recorded as a row rather than done quietly, because this is the exact move the repo has been burned by — *"the gate went green after somebody re-stamped it"* — and the difference between a legitimate re-baseline and laundering is whether anybody can later see what was swallowed. baseline 2026-08-02, count 234 -> 2026-08-11, count 1,198: 964 reads adopted across 46 files. largest: `tests/roster.js` 247 (new), `tests/test-mechanics.js` 226 (new), `engine/medicham2-browser.js` 59 -> 215, `tests/probe_red_demo.js` 123 (new). the simulator entry is the one that matters — the other large entries are harnesses that legitimately construct bodies, but 156 new raw reads inside the engine itself are exactly where a declared-versus-effective ability confusion would do damage, and nobody read them. the restamp was timed after the tree settled (doing it mid-run is what put this red in the first place, per claude.md on a measuring agent beside a writing one) and the adoption was diffed rather than assumed. what is owed: a walk of the 156 simulator reads specifically, routing the ones that want the live value and declaring the ones that legitimately want the declaration. the other 808 can stay adopted re-scoped 2026-08-23 — the count this row is denominated in no longer exists, so the debt had to be restated or it would have gone quiet. the raw-count ratchet was retired (#411) and the 2026-08-11 baseline of 1,198 is kept under `last_count_baseline` as history. "964 reads adopted" is therefore no longer a live quantity, and this row must not be read as though 808 of them are still sitting in a floor somewhere. what is still owed is narrower and is stated in the new gate’s own terms: the replacement asserts a runtime property and is execution coverage only — it is blind to a sheet value copied off a body before a `board` ever existed, and it says so on every run. the 156 simulator reads this row named are covered exactly to the extent that the driven path reaches them, and nothing measures which of them it does not reach. what would decide it: a coverage read of which of those 156 sites the gate’s driven board actually executes, so the uncovered remainder is a list rather than a worry. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-identity-gate-permanent.md`. instrument owed

open.full: the runner's loudest number was its own bug, and that is the row. the ohko arm read 34.40% against a declared 30 on 7,005 trials, z = +8.0 — bonferroni-surviving, and a clean false accusation against the engine. a raw probe over 25,000 games counting only `|-miss|` and `|-damage|` inside an ohko block, with no eligibility rules at all, reads 1,081/3,622 = 29.85% [28.4, 31.4], and `hitchance` returns exactly 30 for fissure. the family is now tallied and not scored — withheld rather than captioned, per claude.md. three further instrument denominator defects were found and fixed as controlled before/afters (same seed, same release, one change each): silently-refused secondary stat drops (z −6.157 -> −4.60), `[from]` residual lines counting as connections, and an explicit miss being overridden (accuracy z +2.53 -> +1.52, ohko 34.40 -> 32.89). two hypotheses were measured and rejected before becoming prose — ally veils/safeguard (`allyveilrefused=1`, `sidebuffrefused=0`) and mid-turn replacements (moved z by 0.000). owed: the ohko denominator must be reconciled with the rule-free count before that arm is scored again

open.title: FIVE ABILITIES RECORD CORPUS USES THAT THE CARRIER DERIVATION SAYS ARE IMPOSSIBLE — AND THE CAUSE IS ALREADY KNOWN: THE
open.full: five abilities record corpus uses that the carrier derivation says are impossible — and the cause is already known: the corpus is contaminated. `serenegrace` 5, `stormdrain` 3, `psychicsurge` 2, `tintedlens` 2, `steelyspirit` 1, all sitting in the 93 abilities derived as having no legal carrier in reg m-b. will, 2026-08-11: *"i think the corpus is contaminated and people uploaded games with custom rules, weve been over this bro in the last session"*. the row was filed as an open either/or — contaminated corpus or incomplete legality read — and that framing was the defect: it had been established in a prior session and was recorded nowhere a later session would find it. not in `docs/`, not in this register, not in memory. so it was re-derived from scratch, at the owner's expense, and he had to say so. the answer: a replay carrying the format name is not proof the game was played under the regulation's rules. the legality derivation is fine; the corpus is the suspect. consequence, and it is wider than these five: every usage-weighted figure inherits this, including the 99%-of-usage coverage bar the medicham gate is defined against. the fix is a corpus filter that validates each stored game against the regulation — not a loosening of the legality read, and not a per-ability exception. until it exists, a usage count is a lower bound on legal usage and an unknown mixture otherwise

open.title: OUR MOVE RULEBOOK IS GENERATED FROM MAINLINE, NOT FROM THE CHAMPIONS MOD — and 22 values differ. THE 22 ARE MOOT; THE GE
open.full: our move rulebook is generated from mainline, not from the champions mod — and 22 values differ. the 22 are moot; the generator is not. `data/move-effects.js` is generated from `chomp/data/move-effects.json`, built by `chomp/build/build_move_effects.js`, which contains zero references to `forformat`, `mods/champions` or the champions dex. its own header claims the values come *"straight from showdown's moves.json - the same server data that runs the format"* — that sentence is false: `moves.json` is mainline, the format runs the mod. `tests/test-mod-conformance.js` (new) asks the two dexes which fields differ rather than comparing a chosen list, because the hand-written first version compared six fields, found 24, and missed 42 pp differences, 6 flag changes and salt cure's halved residual — the exact failure `mod_audit.js`'s own header warns about, read on the same night it was repeated. the 22 were then falsified rather than assumed live: driving the rulebook's `bp` to 999 moves a real turn by nothing (56 -> 56) while `engine-data.js` moves it (56 -> 647); forcing its `type` moves nothing (155 -> 155) while forcing engine-data's does (155 -> 78). base power, type and accuracy all come from format-derived surfaces; the only field the engine reads out of that file is the secondary, and after #187 none is unguarded. so this row is about the generator, not the values. repoint it at the mod. cross-checked independently against bulbapedia's champions section, which confirms dire claw 50% -> 30% + slicing, and freeze-dry losing freeze

open.full: the speed claim the whole engine programme rests on, measured for the first time: c/b = 7.82x. `engine/speed_vs_pokeenv.js` had never been executed. 200 games, same teams, same random policy, quiet machine: showdown in-process 28.7 games/sec; medicham 224.5 games/sec. adr-003's feared null result — *"if c/b is near 1 the programme's justification is transport avoidance, which driving battlestream in-process already gave us for free"* — did not happen. three defects were found by running it, each invisible to inspection: (1) it loaded the engine wrong, copying `game_differential.js:147` and not `:128`, so the data tables were never loaded and the first call died on `mc is not defined`; (2) it handed showdown-shaped sets to a medicham-shaped builder and got 0 usable bodies from 6 — fixed with the repo's existing `buildpair`, as its own header instructed, rather than a third implementation; (3) an uncaught throw in one arm destroyed the other arm's measurement, because the artifact is written after both — arm b, the honest baseline, was computed and discarded every time. arms are isolated now. taken under `--anyway` with the gate closed and 5 uncommitted engine files, both stamped into the artifact. arm a (poke-env) remains unwritten and will has declared it out of scope — it measures a network round trip

open.full: miltank and mag are both owned by will and are being reworked by him — declared 2026-08-11. will: *"im gonna rework miltank so dont spend too much time on it"*, then *"same with mag"*. this extends #26, which already put the mag weights in his hands, to the search itself. consequences, so nobody spends a night on a number that is about to be replaced: do not refit the weights, do not restamp the feature fixture, and do not re-run the miltank timing — `data/miltank-timing-r6.json` is 7 days old and describes a superseded engine build (`medicham2-browser.js b1b3ea94d5c3`), and re-running it costs ~8 minutes of quiet machine to characterise something being rewritten. the invocation is recorded in `docs/search.md` if it is ever wanted: `miltank_timing=… engine/mew.js --miltank --miltank-n 200 --miltank-preview-n 40 --seed 90001`, then `engine/miltank.js --reduce`. what is still worth knowing and is not his: #62's gate — miltank untimed against miltank on the clock — because `clock_observations` reads 0 in that artifact, so the clocked arm has never once been observed, and that is a fact about the harness rather than about any particular miltank

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: STALL IS IN THE CLOSET — DECLARED 2026-08-11, TEMPORARY BY DECISION. Will: *"bro put stall in the quarantine closet aint
open.full: stall is in the closet — declared 2026-08-11, temporary by decision. will: *"bro put stall in the quarantine closet aint nobody using dat"*. measured before closeting, not asserted: `stall` records zero uses in the corpus, and its only legal carrier in reg m-b is sableye. it sat could-not-stage with the reason `no handler` — the effect (always move last inside the priority bracket) lives in an engine table, so nothing in the ability text suggests a board, and the harness separately reports that a priority bracket is only observable when the order decides the final board, which is the same wall that holds extreme speed, ice shard and jet punch. closeted the same way illusion was (#160): declared, counted, named, and reversible — not quietly dropped. it is excluded from the staging backlog and must not be counted as a coverage gap while it is in here. re-admit when either its usage stops being zero or the priority-bracket harness learns to build a board where going last changes the outcome — that second one is shared with the three moves above, so this row reopens for free when they are solved. zero usage is the reason and the reason is measured, so if the corpus ever shows a sableye this row is wrong and should be reopened on that evidence alone

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE RATE RUNNER MUST PLAY THE STAGED SCENARIOS, NOT RANDOM SELF-PLAY — WILL'S DESIGN, 2026-08-11. Will: *"the million ga
open.full: the rate runner must play the staged scenarios, not random self-play — will's design, 2026-08-11. will: *"the million game run will be all these staging scenarios right, just with normal accuracy, proc chances, crit chances, etc"*, then *"so those will have to be in the million game run"*. one set of fixtures at two dice settings: the roster plays a staged board with the dice pinned and asks *does it do the right thing when it fires*; the rate runner plays the same board with the dice free and asks *does it fire at the right rate*. the runner already names this as its missing piece — `engine/million_run.js` marks the whole `proc` family `observable: false` because *"an ability/item proc needs the trigger to be reached … the trace does not say whether the trigger was reached, only whether it fired, so the denominator would be invented. needs a staged arm, not a bigger corpus."* that is the whole argument: on a staged board you know the trigger was reached, so the denominator is real rather than invented, and more random games never fixes an invented denominator — it only makes it bigger. today the runner is self-play over random teams (211 rows) and coverage is whatever the games happen to produce. what this reclassifies, and it is most of the remaining backlog: the 17 pinned-dice rows (static, effect spore, flame body, poison point, poison touch, cute charm, shed skin, stench, harvest, healer, cursed body, quick draw, king's rock, quick claw, focus band, aspear berry, rawst berry), early bird as a sleep-duration row, and the modifier abilities that need a real roll — sniper and merciless, because no sniper or merciless carrier learns flower trick (verified: beedrill, ariados, barbaracle, toxapex; only meowscarada learns it), plus compound eyes, no guard and tangled feet as accuracy rows. none of these is unstageable. every one is in the wrong instrument | closed 2026-08-11 — the staged arm shipped and the proc sampler is right. `engine/million_run.js --staged` -> `data/million-run-staged.json`, release `eafb0abb9736`, free-running dice. 17 fixtures covering all 12 proc target rows plus 5 the target list does not carry. pooled over every row that fires: 58,738 of 176,209 against 58,613.76 expected, z = +0.64, every row powered to one point. denominator known by construction and proved so by a trigger-control arm that must record zero trials — `millionrun_sabotage=staged-precondition` shows it red (13 of 17 controls went 0 -> 60 trials, refused). will's stopping rule, and it answers the question nobody could: 241,525 staged battles / 63 seconds for 1-point resolution; 78,494 / 21 s for 2 points; 19,758 / 6 s for 5. a staged battle is one constructed four-body board played for one turn at 0.26 ms — not comparable to a self-play game, which is why 'a million games' was always the wrong unit. the rule earned itself immediately: at 2 points effect spore read 31.90% and diverged at 95%, with a split-half spread of 1.97 against an effect of 1.90 — not an effect (lessons §9) — and at the powered n it reads 30.34%. a row stopped early is not a smaller answer, it is a different one. and the instrument's own three bugs were found before publication: the first version matched the tag's status word against the engine's and read flame body 0/40 and poison point 0/40 — a headline that would have been filed against engine — because the tag speaks `burn`/`poison`/`sleep` and the engine speaks `brn`/`psn`/`slp`, and static passed by pure accident on three shared letters; the filler pool was `attackers.slice()` over a three-body pool, so six fixtures reported zero trials; and one refusal rate conflated by-design refusals with construction failures, silently dropping harvest and both berries | closed — measure

open.full: three formes have no body to become, and it is a data gap rather than an engine one. `data/engine-data.js` carries no row for `mimikyu-busted`, `morpeko-hangry` or `castform-sunny/rainy/snowy`, so disguise, hunger switch and forecast cannot be asserted at all — there is no target forme to compare against. the new forme instrument prints this on every run and never as a pass, which is the correct handling of an absence (an unprinted gap reads exactly like an agreeing one). `engine/engine-data.js` was not regenerated — a previous agent hit the same wall wiring `formefollowsweather` and it is explicitly not to be rebuilt. and the sprint notes' table of nine forme-changers is wrong for this regulation: derived from `dex.forformat`, exactly five `formechange(`-calling abilities have a legal carrier. ice face, shields down, schooling, power construct, zen mode, gulp missile, flower gift and tera shift have none, and mimicry changes type, not forme. `refusescopy` holds ten members, not the 34/37 the spec quotes — that count predates the carrier toss and is stale. the five rows landed 2026-08-22 (engine) and the instrument moved from 5 uncoverable to 0: `disguise` and `hungerswitch` now agree with the authority on all four assertions, `forecast` is declared known-open on a1 alone. every field derived from `dex.forformat` and spliced in beside its base row by brace-matching — not a regeneration; the field-by-field diff reads `rows lost 0 | rows changed 0 | rows added 5`. the builder that owns these rows skipped them for a reason its own comment says should not apply: `merge_mega_into_engine.js`'s `addableforme` gates on `bodydiffers` (base stats only) while its comment claims *“a forme whose stats and types match its base needs no row”* — castform-sunny/rainy/snowy differ in type and the predicate never looks. three of the five rows are inert to the simulator and that is measured, not assumed: against a control release with the rows excised, `disguise` moves `formerenamednorow` → `formeswapped` while `hungerswitch` (rename branch first, deliberately) and `forecast` (`syncweatherformes` never calls `formeswap`) are byte-identical. a fourth assertion a4 — the type line was added because castform's formes move no stat and a1/a2/a3 are blind to it; shown red by its own plant with no leak. remaining: a1 for forecast — `syncweatherformes` can become a `formeswap` now the rows exist, which is an edit to `engine/medicham2-browser.js`. full account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-formes.md`

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A BASELINED-AS-LEGITIMATE FILE GREW AND THE RATCHET COUNTS LINES, SO IT FIRED ON GROWTH THAT CARRIES NO RISK — 2026-08-1
open.full: a baselined-as-legitimate file grew and the ratchet counts lines, so it fired on growth that carries no risk — 2026-08-11, raised with the audit on record. `engine/merge_mega_into_engine.js` went 14 -> 23 hits. its exemption is categorical, not budgetary: the file builds `mc.mons`, so it cannot ask an index of a table it has not finished writing — and `mckey` caches its index against the table's object identity, which the merge mutates in place, so the index would go stale mid-run even if it could. all 23 sites were read individually before the number moved: membership during construction, base-row reads during construction, the `bynorm` map the ratchet's own header names as legitimate, and the post-merge audit walk. none resolves an external name. the re-baseline was taken and diffed to prove it laundered nothing else: exactly one number changed, `14 -> 23`, with the other fifteen files byte-identical. recorded rather than done quietly, because 'we re-baselined the ratchet' is indistinguishable from 'we loosened the gate to make it green' unless the audit is written down. the residual weakness is real and stated: for a file whose every hit is table construction the count carries no information, so this clause will fire again on the next honest growth. the structural answer — a categorical exemption for the two files whose reason is categorical (`medicham2-browser.js` cannot `require`; this one builds the table) — is deliberately not taken tonight, because it would also stop catching a genuine hand-rolled resolution inside those two, and that trade needs measuring rather than assuming. and this row closed the gate on its first run, which is a second finding and is kept here rather than quietly edited away. `quarantine.js`'s defect clause is a `defect` token in the status cell plus a backstop list of phrases for rows written before the token existed — and one of those phrases appeared inside a sentence explaining why a file is exempt, in a row that describes a test's design and asserts nothing about the simulator at all. the wording was changed to a synonym and the gate reopened. that is the cheap fix, not the right one: a vocabulary backstop cannot tell a claim from a quotation, and an over-firing gate is the one people learn to ignore (#148). the row is left open on that ground

open.title: A DATA-ONLY COMMIT CAN ORPHAN EVERY FIGURE IN A LIVING DOC, AND THE HOOK THAT WATCHES FOR THAT SKIPS DATA-ONLY COMMITS —
open.full: a data-only commit can orphan every figure in a living doc, and the hook that watches for that skips data-only commits — 2026-08-11. `tests/test-docs-current.js` calls a figure traceable when some artifact contains it. `docs/medicham-sprint-notes.md` recorded the first rate run — 16,575 trials, 30.42%, the confidence intervals — and every one was traceable because `data/million-run.json` held it. re-running the same instrument overwrote the artifact with new numbers and orphaned nineteen figures at a stroke. nothing was typed and nothing became false; the doc still describes what was measured, and the artifact that proved it no longer exists. isolated rather than assumed: at head with none of the evening's doc edits applied the count already read 47 against a baseline of 28, so only one of the twenty came from the pass being committed. the reason it went unseen is the hole: `.githooks/pre-commit` skips data-only commits, so the run that rewrote the artifact was exactly the commit the gate did not inspect. baseline raised 28 -> 48 with the diff shown (two lines, the count and the timestamp, nothing else laundered). the structural weakness is real and is not fixed by this row: the check cannot tell 'a figure nobody measured' from 'a figure whose instrument has since been re-run', and it will fire again on every re-run. the candidate repair is to make a re-run stamp the figures it supersedes — a doc figure would then cite a run rather than a value, which is the same lesson as the frozen release and is a bigger job than a baseline bump. recorded now because the alternative is that the next person raises the number again and the ratchet quietly becomes decoration

open.title: THE WEATHER RESIDUAL RAN IN SLOT ORDER WHILE THE CLOCK RESIDUAL HAD BEEN SPEED-SORTED SINCE #115 — CLOSED 2026-08-11. Th
open.full: the weather residual ran in slot order while the clock residual had been speed-sorted since #115 — closed 2026-08-11. the largest single family in the whole-game differential: 80 games across 6 causes, every one identical in shape and differing only in which body is chipped first. read from the authority rather than inferred from the traces: the sand chip is not in the clock pass at all — `sandstorm.onfieldresidual` calls `this.eachevent('weather')` and `battle.ts:465` speed-sorts descending. this engine had it right in one pass and wrong in the other, which is why nobody saw it. #115 speed-sorted the clock loop — perish, yawn, status chip, leftovers — when will asked whether bodies faint in speed order; the weather loop one screen above kept iterating `[...acta, ...actb]`. nothing could have caught it: every body takes the same 1/16, so every total agreed and a damage differential is structurally blind to an ordering defect. fixed as one `residualorder(acta, actb, field)` that both passes ask, with #115's three inline lines deleted rather than left beside it — re-sorting the weather loop in place would have written the fact twice with the same chance of drifting apart again. probe `move/weathersetter`, four bodies at speed 205/101/80, and the trick room arm is the discriminator: `getactionspeed` returns `10000 - speed`, so the inversion is already inside the number both passes sort on and no second branch exists — an engine sorting by raw speed passes arm 1 and fails arm 2, slot order fails both. garchomp on the board takes no chip, the control that says this is the sand. verified independently of the agent's report: the both-sides family reads 3 causes / 4 games against 6 / 80 | reopened 2026-08-12 — the explanation was wrong and the 32 games are unexplained again. this row said protect's divergences were an instrument artefact: our stall counter shares the scalar die, so mode a's corner forces every consecutive protect to fail. the coupling is real and the first protect is clean under both pins — but that cannot be the cause, because showdown's stall check is pinned to refuse at the same corner (#222, measured). both engines refuse; they were agreeing for that reason. so a trace showing the authority emit `-singleturn|protect` where we emit `-fail` is not a disagreement about the roll — it is a disagreement about the counter's value, theirs short-circuiting at `_ctr <= 1` while ours is at 2 or more. that is a rule about when the stall counter resets, which is exactly what mode a exists to find. 32 games, 94,313 corpus clicks, the most-played move in the format. recorded as reopened rather than quietly re-scoped, because the tidier story is the one that got believed twice

open.title: THE DIFFERENTIAL RAN BLANK SPREADS AND A MOVING TEAM POOL, SO IT WAS TESTING TURN ORDER IN THE ONE CONFIGURATION WHERE T
open.full: the differential ran blank spreads and a moving team pool, so it was testing turn order in the one configuration where turn order cannot be got wrong — will, 2026-08-12. he asked *"how much of the divergence is us not knowing the sps"*, then *"i thought the whole point was we invent teams that we know every stat of so nothing can drift"*, then *"we can yoink moves, we just need to give them our stat spreads"*. builds every body with — not a guessed spread, no spread. an open team sheet reveals species, item, ability, moves, nature, gender and level and not the spread; every stored sheet reads `evs: null`, 173,784 of 173,784 bodies. neither the blank spread nor the speed ties cause a single divergence — both are applied identically to both engines — they hide errors instead, and the file already said so in a comment nobody had acted on: *"with every body flat and serious, 91.4% of legal species share a base speed with some other species, so the rig manufactured speed ties"*. the prediction is recorded before the fact: adding spreads should make the number worse and `ordering` should grow; an unmoved rate is the suspicious outcome. second unfrozen input named the same day: the team pool is read live from stores ops appends to continuously, which is why three runs of one instrument reported 1,556, 1,213 and 983 — a measurement that freezes the engine and pins every die took its sample from a moving file. frozen on will's instruction to `data/team-pool-frozen` (bo3 13,214 lines sha 5e10d7ba991f, ots 4,167 lines sha cd21077a4578) and the first pinned baseline is 327/983 (33.3%) top-tie-first and 377/983 (38.4%) bottom-tie-first — the first whole-game figure in this project whose counts are comparable run to run. that five-point arm gap also weakens a claim i made to will off the unpinned run — i said the two corners agreed to within half a point and therefore the divergences were rules rather than dice; on a pinned pool they are five apart and the higher one is the tie-sensitive arm

open.title: MEDICHAM HAS NO GENDER AT ALL, SO TWO ABILITIES CANNOT BE TESTED AND ONE OF THEM IS A LIVE BLUFF — 2026-08-12. `game_dif
open.full: medicham has no gender at all, so two abilities cannot be tested and one of them is a live bluff — 2026-08-12. `game_differential.js` hard-codes `gender: 'n'` on every body of both sides and its own comment gives the reason: *"medicham2 has no gender at all, so a declared gender would part the streams on line one of every game."* that is a correct decision for the differential and a dead end for the mechanics runner: cute charm and rivalry can never fire in any fixture this harness builds, and no amount of preflight repair changes it — the preflight now labels them cannot-fire-in-this-fixture with the clause named, which is the honest state rather than a fix. cute charm was separately measured at 30.92% once a staged fixture did carry genders, against 0 of 4,166 read as "absent" before — so the mechanic works and only this harness cannot reach it. the cost is not theoretical: `rivalry` is one of the 13 roster rows whose control arm is itself a live ability, and it came back fired on a genderless board, which its own guard makes impossible — an over-match that turned out to be control-not-quiet arriving through a new door rather than a broken clause. fixing this needs gender in `medicham2-browser.js` first and then in `game_differential.js`; doing the second without the first is what the hard-coded `n` is protecting against

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: SOME MECHANICS ARE HARDCODED EXCEPTIONS IN THE SIMULATOR, NOT HANDLERS, AND EVERY DERIVATION BUILT TODAY IS BLIND TO THE
open.full: some mechanics are hardcoded exceptions in the simulator, not handlers, and every derivation built today is blind to them — will, 2026-08-13. he asked whether the ability that poisons steel types is even in the regulation. it is: corrosion, legal, carriers salazzle and glimmora, 36 corpus uses — and it has zero `on*` handlers. it is not an ability hook at all. it is a name written into the immunity check itself, `pokemon.js:1257`: `!(source?.hasability("corrosion") && ["tox","psn"].includes(status.id))`. this is a class, not a curiosity. ten abilities are named directly in `dist/sim/*.js` rather than reached through a handler — sheerforce, klutz, prankster, multitype, megasol, levitate, guts, eelevate, dancer, corrosion — and three carry no handlers whatever. levitate is the expensive one: 3,186 corpus uses and 0 handlers. every derivation this project built on 2026-08-12 reads handlers — the per-ability trigger derivation (`pre.moveneeds`), the preflight trigger clauses, the accmod conformance sweep, the residual-order table. all of them are structurally blind to this shape, so the abilities arm cannot stage levitate or corrosion from a handler read, and a sweep that reports "no handler, nothing to check" is reporting its own blind spot as a clean bill. `data/tags.json` does carry rows for both, so `tag_dex` reached them by another route — but that is a second derivation happening to cover the gap, not coverage by design, and nothing checks that the two agree about which abilities exist. the concrete cost, measured the same night: a diverging game showed toxic into a steel scizor — the authority emits `-immune`, we emit `-miss`, because our poison immunity check runs after the accuracy roll instead of before it. fixing that as an absolute immunity would have been wrong in the opposite direction, since a salazzle toxic into a steel body lands. will caught that before it shipped. the ordering fix and the corrosion exemption went to the agent already in `hitchance`; the general sweep — which mechanics in this format are hardcoded exceptions, and does anything verify our tags cover them — is not started

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: MAG BECOMES A FUTILITY GATE AND STOPS BEING A LEARNED SCORER — WILL, 2026-08-13. *"im thinking of cutting mag back in si
open.full: mag becomes a futility gate and stops being a learned scorer — will, 2026-08-13. *"im thinking of cutting mag back in size to say, no fake out after turn 1, no poison on steel, no status moves into gholdengo, no prio moves when farig is on the board... just very simple rules and not the whole convoluted, protect and let my partner ko the threat."* this fixes an ordering fault and is not merely a simplification. a learned mag prunes what is bad on average and runs before doduo, so it deletes precisely the actions that are bad alone and good in combination — fake out into a spread, follow me covering a setup turn, a weak click that baits a protect — which is the entire class doduo exists to find. the safe line is futile (no other action rescues it) versus bad (conditional, must survive to doduo). the gate must be derived, not written, and all four example rules are wrong as typed: fake out is `activemoveactions > 1` — first turn out, not turn 1 of the game, so a fake out user switching in on turn 6 may still use it; corrosion (salazzle, glimmora) poisons steel; good as gold is `breakable` and refuses only when `target !== source`; armor tail is one of farigiraf's three abilities and exempts perish song, flower shield and rototiller. category right every time, hand-written form wrong every time — the ban-list-of-four shape, and a prune list is worse than a ban list because it fails silently: a deleted option leaves no trace in any output. so the gate asks the engine "does this action produce any effect on this board" rather than holding rules. open sheets do not remove the need: fake out's condition is battle state and appears on no sheet, and the sheet stops being true — six legal moves change an ability mid-battle plus 11 mold breaker carriers and a mummy, and knock off has 4,078 corpus uses. it reads the live board, which on turn one is the same object and by turn four is not. buildable now — the only stage of the pipeline with no fitted parameters, so the quarantine does not block it. needs a counter for what it pruned and a check that a pruned action really was a no-op: an over-pruning gate deletes a good play and nothing catches it, because both sides of every comparison share the blind spot

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE FUTILITY GATE CARRIES A DECLARED PREDICTION, AND WILL BROKE THE SAFETY ARGUMENT THE SAME NIGHT — 2026-08-13. *"of co
open.full: the futility gate carries a declared prediction, and will broke the safety argument the same night — 2026-08-13. *"of course there is forbidden tech of clicking a prio move when farig is on the board because youre making a prediction of it switching out."* the rule in #251 was stated as "no action rescues it", and that quantified over my partner's actions only. quantified over the opponent's as well, most of the gate's membership stops being unconditional: a move follows the slot, so switching the slot rescues it. priority into an armor tail farigiraf is dead only while that farigiraf is still there when the move resolves; the same holds for toxic into a steel and any status into gholdengo. two halves, one assumption-free: the unconditional half fails on the user's own state (fake out out of position, a choice lock, no pp) and asserts nothing; the occupant-dependent half asserts *"they will not switch"*. three of the four original examples are in the second half. the gate may still cut them — it is usually right and the expected cost is small in a format where the read is rare — but it is a prediction and must be recorded as one. deferred by will's decision, not missed: *"id rather not engage with those type of scenarios at the moment but make a note of it for things to possibly adjust much much later into the project."* when taken up, the home is not the gate: an action that is dead under one opponent action and live under another is a column of the equilibrium matrix, not a row to delete before coordination

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE WORD "ENDGAME" IS CLAIMED BY TWO MODELS IN OUR OWN LEDGER, AND THAT IS WHY THE ARCHITECTURE WAS HARD TO HOLD — WILL,
open.full: the word "endgame" is claimed by two models in our own ledger, and that is why the architecture was hard to hold — will, 2026-08-13. *"wait didnt we have dusknoir as the endgame guy? its hard to keep track."* he is right and the confusion is ours, not his memory. `docs/models.md:1451` scopes dusk as the endgame tablebase — exact, precomputed offline, shipped as a lookup because it cannot be solved under a turn timer. slowking's job: line in the same file reads *"the endgame — tell you the equilibrium-best move (and win %) on a live position"*, which is not distinguishable in wording. the split, now written down: dusk is small endgames, exact, offline then looked up; slowking is any position, approximate (an equilibrium over estimated values), live per turn; hypno is about the opponent rather than the position and is a deliberate deviation from slowking. only dusk can say "guaranteed" — which means will's own description of the late-game stage (*"which ones lead to a guaranteed win... hand these scenarios to miltank"*) is dusk's job and was filed under hypno. fixed in `docs/models.md` and `docs/alakazam-v2-spec.md`. and the matrix is kept even if greedy wins: *"id still want slowking matrix even if greedy wins right? because then if we play opponents regularly we can adapt and become unexploitable."* keeping it is right and is already adr-003's position — vgc-bench's policy beats a worlds competitor and is ~100% exploitable, so winning on average and being safe are different axes. one correction to the reasoning: adapting to an opponent makes you more exploitable, not less. nash never adapts and cannot be beaten in the long run; deviating to punish a habit opens a hole in you. what repeated play actually buys is the other direction — a fixed policy degrades because they learn you, and greedy is a fixed mapping. the matrix is not the adaptation mechanism; it is the floor you measure your deviations against, and hypno is the deviation

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: EVERY HAZARD LANDS ON THE SIDE THAT LAID IT IN THE OFFLINE BOARD, AND THE LIVE PATH IS RIGHT — SO THE FIT AND THE GAME D
open.full: every hazard lands on the side that laid it in the offline board, and the live path is right — so the fit and the game disagree. found by search 2026-08-13 while chasing #249; split out and verified independently. `engine/board.js` `notemove` ends with `if (move.sidecondition) board.startside(side, move.sidecondition, ...)` — `side` is the mover's, unconditionally. derived from the format, not recalled: of the 11 legal side-condition moves in this regulation, seven are `target: allyside` and four are `target: foeside` — stealth rock, spikes, sticky web, toxic spikes. the seven (reflect, light screen, aurora veil, safeguard, tailwind, quick guard, wide guard) are correct by accident, because the mover's side is the right answer for them. the four hazards are recorded on the layer's own side, which is the side they can never be on. this is not #249 and must not be closed with it. that row is the seed carrying no hazards into a playout — a missing feature, and a rollout that ignores hazards is merely blind. this is a feature that is present and inverted, and it sits in the board the fit reads: `engine/board.js` is the offline board, the live path reads showdown's `|-sidestart|` and gets it right. that is fitting environment and playing environment must match, broken in a new place — the same shape as mag fitted with the sheet visible and played without it, and machamp trained under broken mega. a model fitted on a board where stealth rock hurts its own team learned something about a game nobody plays. size, and it is small and that is not the argument: 259 corpus uses across the four (stealth rock 168, sticky web 42, toxic spikes 34, spikes 15) against 16,074 for tailwind alone. a wrong value is worse than a missing one at equal volume, because nothing downstream can tell it is wrong. the fix is derived, not a list of four: read `move.target` and place the condition on the far side when it is `foeside`. a hand-written hazard list here would be the ban-list-of-four shape a third time, and a hazard added next regulation would silently land on the wrong side again. three sites, not one, and they are currently wrong together — which is the only reason nothing has broken. read 2026-08-13 before anyone touches it: `engine/board.js:2675` writes with `board.startside(side, ...)`; `:3311` reads with `board.hasside(side, m.sidecondition)` to set `deadside` ("this move cannot work, it is already up"); `:3343` reads the same way for `alreadyup`, which gates `setupturns`. all three take the mover's side, so today they are self-consistent and the error cancels — a hazard is written to the wrong side and then looked for on that same wrong side. fixing the write alone produces a worse bug than the one it fixes: the hazard would land on the foe's side while both readers keep looking at the mover's, so `deadside` would never fire for a hazard and the model would re-lay stealth rock every turn believing it was not up, crediting itself `setupturns` each time. so it is one helper, not three edits — a single `sidefor(board, side, move)` that answers "whose side does this condition live on" from `move.target`, called by the write and by both reads. whose side a condition lands on is a fact, and three call sites must not each decide it independently; that is the rule this repo has broken most expensively. `const foeside = side === 'p1' ? open.title: "EVERY SECONDARY FIRES" SELF-CANCELS FOR ANY EFFECT WITH AN ESCAPE ROLL, SO THE BOTTOM ARM GUARANTEES FREEZE AND GUARANT
open.full: "every secondary fires" self-cancels for any effect with an escape roll, so the bottom arm guarantees freeze and guarantees thaw — will, 2026-08-13. *"bro guaranteed freeze in the lower bound is so broken"*, then, one message later, *"but i guess we get guaranteed thaw?"* — both right, and together they name a property of the instrument nobody had stated. `makearm` pins `random(den)` to 0 in the bottom arm, and `chance = (num, den) => random(den) < num`, so every `randomchance` returns true. the freeze secondary (`randomchance(1,10)`) fires and the thaw check inside `frz.onbeforemove` (`randomchance(1,4)`) also fires, so a body is frozen and cures on its very next move without ever losing a turn. the bottom arm therefore never exercises frozen-turn behaviour at all, while appearing to guarantee it. the effect is not uniform and that is the point: an effect with one roll compounds (paralysis is applied and fully paralyses every turn; confusion is applied and self-hits), an effect with an escape roll cancels (freeze). *"the worst corner"* is therefore the wrong mental model for this arm — it is *"every branch taken"*, which is the worst case only when there is one branch. not a defect in the pin, which is doing exactly what it says; it is a coverage claim that needs narrowing, and the arm's own description (*"every secondary fires"*) is what misleads. and a latent collision found while checking it: `random(m)` returns the damage index when `m === damage_roll_sides` (16), so any `randomchance(x, 16)` would be read as a damage roll rather than a chance. derived: no legal move in this regulation has a 1-in-16 secondary, so it is latent today and would surface silently the day one is added

open.title: A MIDDLE ARM WITH EVENT-ADDRESSED DICE, BECAUSE BOTH PINNED CORNERS PRODUCE GAMES NOBODY PLAYS — WILL, 2026-08-13. *"is
open.full: a middle arm with event-addressed dice, because both pinned corners produce games nobody plays — will, 2026-08-13. *"is it possible at all for us to run a middle bound? where things can miss, and secondary chances have a chance to proc? to get some more realistic scenarios to test... otherwise paralysis ends the mons usefulness... thats why games take years."* he is right about the mechanism and it is measurable: the bottom arm pins every `randomchance` true (see #260), so the full-paralysis roll fires every turn and a paralysed body never moves again — which is a large part of why the median game hits the 12-turn cap when a real one ends at 7. why random dice are not the answer, and this is the whole design problem: the arms are pinned for synchronisation, not caution. both engines must give the same answer to the same question or a divergence is a dice disagreement rather than a rule disagreement, and they make different numbers of draws in different orders, so a shared seeded stream desynchronises on turn one. a constant is the only mapping that survives that. the way out is to address the die by the event rather than by position in a sequence: `hash(turn, attacker slot, move id, effect name) % 100 < chance`. order-independent, so the engines agree without being in lockstep; some rock slides miss and some flinch; paralysis fires near 1-in-4 instead of every turn; games end. across thousands of events the observed rates approach the printed ones, which also makes it the natural home for the rate work in #196/#28. the cost, stated: the two engines must name the event identically — same move id, same turn, same target — or the hashes differ and every roll disagrees. the normaliser already maps ids, so it is checkable, and it must be asserted rather than assumed: a probe that plants a known event on both sides and compares the drawn value. and it inherits #260: an effect with an escape roll must not get "true" for both the apply and the escape, which a hash gives for free and a constant never can | engine half landed 2026-08-13 — the engine names the event; the authority half is still unwired and measures 0.0%. medicham2 now carries a module-level event address written at four sites (top of the turn, top of the action, the announcement, the step driver) and `mideventdice`/`mideventlog` export it; `tests/test-middle-identity.js` diffs the two engines' address logs over 900 real games. measured, medicham2-matched: acc 99.7%, dmg 98.8%, crit 98.5%, sec 91.0% — 98.3% pooled over 1,058 events, floored per category (pooling hid a break: deleting the per-target write left the pool at 91.2% over a floor of 90). four deliberate breaks, three red, and the fourth green is itself the finding — the announcement-site write is redundant over 900 games and is now counted rather than trusted. the row cannot close on engine's side alone. `game_differential.js` builds its address inside the function it installs as `battle.prng.random`, and `battle#random` is `this.prng.random(m,n)` — so `this` there is the prng and every authority address is `<seed>|undefined|<cat>|-|-|<nth>`. the test computes both streams on every draw and asserts the degenerate one stays under 5%, so the arm cannot be switched on by mistake. owed in that file: capture `this.battle` in `midwrapshowdown`'s `around()`, and clear `mid_nth` per game beside the existing `midreset()`. three category mislabels fell out of the diff by counting, one of them a standing roadmap #222 gap: the move's own secondaries loop was on the generic stream (28 authority `sec` draws against zero from us), and king's rock and dire claw likewise. what is not solved and is not claimed: `nth` is a repeat counter, so a differing draw count at one address still parts after entry 0 — 457 of 2,029 events are `nth > 0` and that is printed every run

open.title: THE STORE HAS NO SPREADS AT ALL, SO A REPLAY DIFFERENTIAL CANNOT ADJUDICATE DAMAGE OR SPEED — WILL, 2026-08-13, AND HE T
open.full: the store has no spreads at all, so a replay differential cannot adjudicate damage or speed — will, 2026-08-13, and he talked me out of leading with it. i proposed running `engine/replay_differential.js` against real games as the realistic instrument. *"we dont know the sps on games that actually happened tho"*, then *"so the damage and speed would be off."* measured on `data/games.bo3.jsonl`: 4,001 games, 47,856 sheet bodies, every one `"evs": null`, zero with a real spread. an open team sheet shows species, ability, item, moves and nature — never the stat points. speed is the worse half and that is the part i missed: damage being off produces a wrong number, but speed being off produces a wrong turn order, which is categorical — every line after it diverges for a reason that is not a rule. `replay_differential.js`'s own header already makes this argument about reconstructing choices (*"a reconstruction that guesses is worse than no test, because a guess that happens to be wrong looks exactly like an engine defect"*) and does not apply it to the spreads. the distinction that matters is control, not realism: the synthetic differential's spreads are unknown and identical on both sides, so a divergence can only be a rule; a replay's spreads are unknown and different from whatever the player actually brought, so a divergence may be either. unknown-but-identical is fine; unknown-and-wrong is not. so the replay differential keeps a narrower job — sequences and categorical facts independent of exact numbers (did that ability fire, did that switch happen, was that move legal) — and cannot arbitrate a ko or a speed tie, which is most of what a game turns on. this is roadmap #68 restated with its consequence: it is narrowed by the nature and can never be closed by it. do not lead with replay; build #262 instead, which is synthetic and therefore controls its own spreads

open.full: three moves always crit in this format and we roll a die for them, and on an ordinary move the authority rolls where we do not — 2026-08-14. found by the middle arm before the middle arm works, which is the argument for building it. its address dump on a voided game: the authority draws `dmg|flowertrick` and no crit; we draw `dmg|flowertrick` and `crit|flowertrick`. on the next move it inverts — the authority draws `acc|lowkick`, `crit|lowkick`, `dmg|lowkick` and we draw `acc` and `dmg` with no crit at all. derived and filtered to the regulation: exactly three legal moves carry `willcrit: true` — storm throw, flower trick, frost breath. wicked blow and surging strikes carry it and are `isnonstandard` here. a guaranteed crit that rolls is wrong on every use — sometimes we do not crit on a move that always does, which is a damage error rather than a narration one, and it is invisible to the pinned corners because both arms force the crit die to a constant. the second half is the more interesting one and is not diagnosed: low kick has `willcrit: false` and `critratio: 1`, so the authority rolls an ordinary 1-in-24 and we appear to skip it entirely. either our crit is computed somewhere the address does not see, or a class of moves never rolls one. also derived, and unchecked here: 14 legal moves carry `critratio: 2` — crabhammer, night slash, shadow claw, air cutter, aqua cutter, blaze kick, cross chop, cross poison, drill run, leaf blade, psycho cut, sky attack, stone edge, triple arrows — and nobody has confirmed we double their rate. probe all three shapes: a guaranteed crit must crit 100/100 with no draw; sprt accepts h0 against arm 1 after 30 decisive pairs. this number must be read with run 1 in hand — forcing switching on to make the comparison fair did not remove a confound, it crippled the mag arm, so 94.3% is an upper bound and not the honest margin. run 3, as shipped (in flight): mag switching-off vs miltank switching-on, each player in its best configuration. at 200 games the raw split was 136–64, a visibly smaller margin, which is the direction run 1 predicts. the decisive-pair rate is its own finding: 34.2% in run 1 against 60.2% in run 2 — with miltank on the board the policy decides the game roughly twice as often as it otherwise does, and nothing about that was implied by "search beats score". affordability, which is the question r4 does not ask: 9,655 logged decisions, mean 48.9 options and 3,859 ms per decision (max 24,299 ms), ~4 s on the bring. at 20–30 turns that is 80–200 s against a 7-minute clock, so the search fits. both readers agree on every count (`--verify`: 2-0 259/259, 0-2 139/139, 15/15, 250/250). quarantined on arrival and the figure travels with the stamp, not a caption: medicham has not passed its gate, so the magnitudes are provisional; open.title: THE DOCS-CURRENCY CENSUS WAS EXEMPTING FIGURES ON THE STRENGTH OF ITS OWN COMPLAINT ABOUT THEM, AND `--update` WAS THE #
open.full: the docs-currency census was exempting figures on the strength of its own complaint about them, and `--update` was the #258 laundering button a second time — filed and fixed 2026-08-15 by measure. three defects in one gate, found while chasing `docs/abra-whitepaper.md: 12 untraceable figures, was 11` — a red search correctly refused to file as known. (1) self-reference. `engine/docs_scan.js#allartifactnumbers` unions every `data/*.json`, and `data/docs-currency-baseline.json` is one: it records the census's own findings as strings (`"docs/abra-whitepaper.md|0.073|data/slowking-eval.json"`), and `artifactnumbers` walks strings, so writing a figure down as an offender made it traceable next run. demonstrated by building it worse — recording the untraceable set took the whitepaper from 12 to 5 in one run, seven figures 'traced' to the file that had just called them untraceable. the loop was live through `citation_mismatches` since the day it was written. `not_an_artifact` now excludes it: a gate may not satisfy itself. (1b) and the same loop arrives through the register, caught in the act within the hour. `data/open-work.json` is `engine/open_work.js`'s copy of roadmap.md's prose, so any figure quoted in a register row becomes traceable. this row quoted the offending identifier while describing it; `open_work.js` copied the row into the artifact; the census read the complaint as evidence for the figure and the clause went green with the real regression still underneath. writing down 'this number has no source' must never become that number's source. excluded too, and the sweep for other prose-copying artifacts came back with exactly one — this file. it was masking nine figures across three documents: closing it takes `docs/medicham-sprint-notes.md` from 25 to 32, restores `docs/role-family.md`'s 2 (a green run had already dropped that document from the baseline when the register laundered it to zero), and puts the whitepaper's arxiv identifier back on the list. those seven are a discovery, not a regression — roadmap #188 is the row about a ratchet with no split between the two, and this is that row happening. the recorded counts were not raised to match. (2) `--update` did both jobs at once, exactly as `tests/test-no-silent-failure.js` did before #258: `ok(added.length === 0 || update)` turned a failing clause green and `next: added.length && !update ? base : cur` adopted every new offender. one command locked in a fix and laundered tonight's regression. it is monotone now — retires and lowers only, never adopts, never raises, never passes a red clause — and `if (f === 0 || update)` is `if (f === 0)`, because a run that found a regression must not record it. proved: `--update` leaves the artifact byte-identical (md5 unchanged) and exits 1. (3) it ratchets a count it cannot explain. the baseline held `docs/abra-whitepaper.md: 11` and not which eleven, so the twelfth is not recoverable from the tree — sixteen `data/*.json` artifacts were rewritten in the 47 minutes between the two runs. a count also launders by swap: fix one figure, add another, count unchanged, gate green. the figure set is recorded beside it now (green runs only). the twelve, characterised: two are untraceable only by sign (the doc writes u+2212 and the matcher demands the sign — the absolute values occur in 1 and 23 artifacts), one is `arxiv 2304.08272`, an identifier the scanner counts as a measurement, and seven occur in no artifact at any sign. deliberately not fixed: removing the arxiv false positive alone would take 12 to 11 and turn the gate green while the real regression sat underneath, which is 'known failure' in a new coat

ceruledge` → `sd \|-unboost\|p1a: ceruledge\|atk\|0` where we emit nothing at all. the authority's branch is the one this row already derived: `sim/battle.ts:2076-2077` — for an effect that is a move open.full: the accuracy roll was one per move where the game rolls one per target, so rock slide could not hit one and miss the other — fixed 2026-08-18 by engine. will: *"rock slide and heat wave can hit one and miss the other."* `engine/medicham2-browser.js` declared the divergence at its own roll site — *"one roll per move, not per target… a spread move rolls once, against no defender, and gets the attacker's modifiers only"* — and the authority is `hitstepaccuracy(targets: pokemon[], pokemon, move)` (sim/battle-actions.ts:690-692), which takes an array, sets `this.battle.activetarget = target` per iteration and ends each one in `randomchance(accuracy, 100)` at :737. the distribution was wrong, not only the variance: a 90-accuracy spread move into two live bodies is 81 / 18 / 1 in the authority and was 90 / 0 / 10 here, so the eighteen-percent middle case did not exist in this engine at all. reach: rock slide 18,122 clicks, heat wave 11,121, plus dazzling gleam, hyper voice, matcha gotcha, eruption — every sub-100-accuracy spread move in the format. the stated objection was obsolete and that is why it landed now: *"it would change how much rng every existing seeded run consumes"* was true of a sequence; open.title: THE WHOLE-GAME HEADLINE IS COMPUTED OVER A DENOMINATOR THAT INCLUDES 350 VOID GAMES, AND THE ARTIFACT DOES NOT CARRY THE
open.full: the whole-game headline is computed over a denominator that includes 350 void games, and the artifact does not carry the number that would fix it — found 2026-08-18 by measure while re-running the differential. `engine/game_differential.js` declares its own rule in the middle arm's description: *a game whose draw counts diverge is void, not a divergence*. its stdout reports all three figures — `diverged (primary arm middle): 700 of 995`, `void (instrument desync): 350 of 995`, `diverged among the 645 usable games: 628 (97.4%)` — and the artifact persists only `games: 995` and `diverged: 700`. so `wholegameclause` publishes 700 (less declared) over 995, and by the run's own arithmetic 72 of those 700 diverged games are themselves void: 700 — 628 = 72, and 995 — 350 = 645. the honest figure is worse, not better. on the games where the instrument is valid the engines disagree about 628 of 645 = 97.4%, where the clause's own ratio is 69.9%. neither number can be published by the clause today, because the void count exists only in a console line nobody parses. this is not a request to change the bar: the clause is green only at zero either way. it is that the most-quoted number in this project is a ratio of two quantities that do not describe the same population, and a reader cannot tell from the artifact. measured on release `978ca8fe72c9`, 995 games, arm a/middle, census `2e3953f1f882`, pool `631d4ea60a80`; the identical split appears on release `6875c8ace00e` under the same steering. instrument owed: the artifact must persist `void` and `usable` beside `games` and `diverged`, and then `wholegameclause` must publish the usable rate — a clause cannot derive a denominator that was never written down. landed 2026-08-18 by engine, and the population was not what the void rule said it was. `mid_void` is now in the artifact — `void_games`, `usable_games`, `diverged_among_usable`, `diverged_rate_over_usable`, and every verdict the check reached by cause. printing the causes killed the headline: 340 of 350 voided games had drawn no comparable address at all, 275 of them because neither engine rolled a die in the whole game (median 12 turns, the cap). under the count-based check an empty side meant the streams had parted; under shared-address identity there is nothing to disagree about, and the rule already said so two clauses down for the outcome log while contradicting itself for the full one. a dice-free game is the most trustworthy evidence in the run, not the least. and the real desync was #302, one file over. void on the same 797-game sample: 350 (old rule) -> 11 (rule corrected) -> 8 (#302 fixed). verified by tests/test-middle-draw-scope.js, whose §6 re-runs itself with `--mid-carry-nth` and fails if the broken arm passes

open.title: THE CATCH BLOCK THAT REPORTS A FAILED SHOWDOWN WRAP CANNOT RUN, SO A BAD `SHOWDOWN_PATH` KILLS THE DIFFERENTIAL WITH A T
open.full: the catch block that reports a failed showdown wrap cannot run, so a bad `showdown_path` kills the differential with a temporal-dead-zone error naming neither cause nor cure — found 2026-08-18 by measure, by walking into it. `engine/game_differential.js:244` assigns `mid_wrap_error = e.message` inside the catch that guards the middle-arm wrapper; `mid_wrap_error` is declared `let` at :743, five hundred lines below. the assignment is therefore in the variable's temporal dead zone and throws. reproduced: a `showdown_path` carrying one trailing space (`set var=x && ...` in cmd keeps it) makes the `require` fail, and the process dies with `referenceerror: cannot access 'mid_wrap_error' before initialization` at line 244 — which names the reporting variable and says nothing about the path, the require, or the wrapper. the error path is the part that does not work, which is this repository's founding shape pointed the other way: not a capability absent and everything reporting success, but a capability whose failure report is the thing that is broken. it is latent while the wrap succeeds, so no run that worked has ever touched it, and `mid_wrap_error === null` is asserted by a pin claim that can never see this branch. cost measured at one wasted run and about ten minutes of looking for an engine bug that was a shell quoting mistake. the repair is to hoist the declaration above the try. instrument owed: an arm that loads the driver with a deliberately wrong `showdown_path` and asserts the process reports the require failure rather than a `referenceerror`

open.title: `switch lookups that MISSED: medicham 22, showdown 0` ON A LINE THE RUN ITSELF MARKS `MUST READ 0`, AND NOTHING GATES IT
open.full: `switch lookups that missed: medicham 22, showdown 0` on a line the run itself marks `must read 0`, and nothing gates it — found 2026-08-18 by measure. the whole-game differential prints this counter with its own bar attached and its own consequence spelled out beside it: *a miss means that side passed while the other switched*. so on those lookups the two engines are not playing the same game at all — one body left the field and the other did not — and every line after it is compared across two different positions. measured: 22 misses on the medicham side and 0 on the authority's, on release `978ca8fe72c9` over 995 games, and the identical 22/0 on release `6875c8ace00e` under the same steering, so it is not a regression from either of today's landings. it is reported here rather than repaired because `engine/game_differential.js` and the simulator are engine's and were live while this ran. the counter is not persisted in the artifact either, so nothing downstream can read it. instrument owed: the miss count published in the artifact and a clause that fails while it is non-zero, since a run marked must read 0 that reads 22 is currently caught only by a human reading stdout

open.title: THE AUTHORITY'S REPEAT INDEX SURVIVED THE GAME BOUNDARY, SO THE TWO ENGINES DREW DIFFERENT VALUES FOR THE SAME EVENT IN
open.full: the authority's repeat index survived the game boundary, so the two engines drew different values for the same event in every measured game — found and fixed 2026-08-18 by engine. the middle arm's die is `fnv1a(seed|turn|category|move|target|nth)`, and `nth` — the repeat index — is a field of the hash. medicham2 clears its map once per game inside `mideventdice`. the driver's `mid_nth` and its authority address log were cleared by the void check instead, which runs once per pair — after both the stones-removed control game and the measured one. so every address the control game touched was left at nth=1,2,3..., the measured game's authority draws continued from there, and medicham2 started at 0. 846 of 878 unshared addresses in a 260-game run differed in `nth` and in nothing else. the log half made the check too lenient rather than too harsh, which is why nothing noticed: `shared` is `meo.filter(a => sdset.has(a))`, so an address the authority only asked in the control game counted as agreement — measured on game one as `sd=1075 me=11`. same shape as #220 and larger: #220 mis-addressed the draws made outside three `battleactions` methods, this mis-addressed every authority draw in every game that had a control in front of it. fix is the reset moved to the top of `playgame`, beside `arm.medirng()`, which is the one place that already knows a game is starting. paired on 797 games, release `978ca8fe72c9`, census and pool pinned, the driver the only file that moved: diverged 487 -> 452, void 11 -> 8, games positively verified as naming the same events 208 -> 231. verified by tests/test-middle-draw-scope.js — the same staged game played twice must produce the same addresses and the same trace; `--mid-carry-nth` restores the leak and the file fails if that arm does not go red
