open.title: THE LARGEST CLASS IN THE WHOLE-GAME DIFFERENTIAL WAS A SHARED DIE READ BACKWARDS ON ONE SIDE — FOUND AND FIXED 2026-08-1
open.full: the largest class in the whole-game differential was a shared die read backwards on one side — found and fixed 2026-08-18 by engine. `-damage field 3` was 226 of 491 diverging games while `tests/test-engine-diff.js` reads 0 of 6000 at each corner and `game_differential.js`'s own header says *"the engines agree about damage"*. both were true: the corner is exactly where the defect cannot show. showdown's `random(16)` is an index and `randomizer` is `tr(tr(d*(100-i))/100)`, so i=0 is the maximum; medicham2 draws a position in its span, `d.min + floor(u*(d.max-d.min+1))`, increasing in u. the pinned arms already encode the correspondence — `corner_top` sits beside `damageindex: 0`, `corner_bottom` beside `damageindex: 15` — and the middle arm handed showdown `floor(u*16)`, the inverse. a shared die read backwards on one side is anti-correlated, which is worse than two independent dice. arm split, one 969-game run, complete populations: 226 in `middle`, 2 of 155 in `top-tie-first`, 0 of 183 in `bottom-tie-first`; sampled hp deltas both signs to +/-18, median 5 — the span, not a rounding step. fix narrowed to `mid_cat === 'dmg' && m === damage_roll_sides` because `random(16)` elsewhere is a 1-in-16 chance (#260). paired on 797 games, the mapping the only thing that moved: `-damage field 3` 204 -> 137, diverged 452 -> 409, void 8 -> 4. two thirds of the family survives and is not explained — the standing candidate is a real medicham2 defect, `damage_interior`: 20 producible hp values against the authority's 14 on one staged hit, 6 of them the authority can never emit. verified by tests/test-middle-damage-roll.js, which derives the mapping from the pinned arms' own declarations and re-runs itself with `--mid-damage-uninverted`

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: medicham2's DAMAGE ROLL IS A UNIFORM DRAW OVER THE INTEGER SPAN; SHOWDOWN'S IS ONE OF SIXTEEN FLOORED INDICES — FOUND 20
open.full: medicham2's damage roll is a uniform draw over the integer span; showdown's is one of sixteen floored indices — found 2026-08-18 by engine, not fixed. showdown computes `tr(tr(d*(100-i))/100)` for i in 0..15, so its support has holes and repeats; medicham2 computes `d.min + floor(u*(d.max-d.min+1))` (`medicham2-browser.js:18336`), which is every integer in the span. measured by the driver's own `damage_interior` block and published in `data/game-differential.json`: on one staged hit showdown 14 distinct values, medicham 20, six of which — 110, 113, 116, 119, 122, 125 — the authority can never emit, worst per-value probability gap 7.5 points. every corner instrument is blind to it by construction (the endpoints agree), which is why `test-engine-diff` reads 0/6000. `dmgrangeonehit` already takes a `rolls` out parameter *"in showdown's own `random(16)` index order"* with exactly one caller, so the fix is to select `rolls[index]` instead of interpolating. it moves every damage number in every rollout and wants its own pass and its own probe. fixed 2026-08-18 by engine. it is the support that is wrong, not a rounding stage: 16 indices is a hard ceiling, the randomizer's own floor creates repeats below it (`basedamage/100` per step) and every stage after it — stab `:262`, the type chart `:270-284`, burn `:285`, `modifydamage` `:293` — scales the survivors apart into holes. the loop now selects `rolls[damagerollindex(u)]`. the 14/20 shape holds across a widened fixture of nine staged hits (both categories, a resist, a 4x, an item after the die, two spreads, bp 40-120): ice shard reads 5 authority values against 25, ice beam 9 against 33 — and the two rows whose supports matched still failed the paired clause, so a support count alone understates it. paired, 797 games, `medi_damage_span_draw=1` the only difference: `-damage field 3` 137 -> 8, diverged 409 -> 330, 51.1% -> 41.1%, and both corner arms unmoved at 163/191 — which is the prediction, since `rolls[0]` is `d.max`. the pre arm reproduces #303's published post exactly. standing artifact republished: 969 games, 344 diverged, 2 void, 35.4%. landing it exposed two census probes and one gate clause that were pinning the defect — `spreadfoes` demanded 51, a value the authority cannot emit at any roll; part 3b of `tests/test-game-differential.js` failed if the interior was identical. verified by tests/test-damage-roll-support.js

open.title: TEN MECHANICS PARTED THE BOARD AND FOUR MORE WROTE A LEAF NOTHING COMPARED — FOUND BY `engine/all_mechanics_fire.js`'s b
open.full: ten mechanics parted the board and four more wrote a leaf nothing compared — found by `engine/all_mechanics_fire.js`'s board arm, fixed 2026-08-19 by engine. ten rows came back state: `spite` removed no pp at all, `syrupbomb` applied no speed drop, `corrosivegas` / `stuffcheeks` / `teatime` all left a berry the authority had taken, `berserk` paid +3 off a three-hit move, `sleeptalk` and `snore` were refused by the sleep gate in the one state they exist for, `focuspunch` wrote a `|move|` line the authority never writes and spent pp for it, and `fling` left the target 8 hp down. the `fling` diagnosis in the work order was wrong and the correction is the useful part: the damage lines are identical on both engines (`952/960`) and the authority then writes `|-heal|…|[from] item: sitrus berry|[of] p1a: abomasnow` — `fling.onpreparehit` replaces `move.onhit` for a berry so the target eats it, threshold bypassed. the three berry rows did not share a cause (a spread-targeting failure, a self-eat gated on a boost, and an `onhitfield` walk). four leaves wired into `board_state.js` — `vol.trapped`, `vol.uproar`, `vol.charge`, `field.fairylock_turns` — each shown red first by a plant in `all_mechanics_fire.js --red` that moves state and writes no protocol line; two of the four turned out to be unimplemented moves rather than unread leaves (fairy lock was a whole no-op turn; spirit shackle's trap is a `secondary.onhit` the derivation could not see). wiring `vol.trapped` immediately exposed magic bounce trapping the wrong body. five new tags, every membership printed first — and `sleepmove`'s first predicate caught rest, which asks the same question with the opposite sign. census 603 -> 618 live / 0 missing; gate 4 of 8 failing -> 3; mechanics 47 -> 34 diverging, whole-game 35.9% -> 35.2%, both re-run on release `926e810dd8a0`. verified by tests/test-mechanics.js (fifteen probes) and engine/all_mechanics_fire.js --red

open.full: three damage rows root-caused and unfixed, and two of them want the same consumer. all three survived #304 and are byte-identical to the pre-#304 artifact, so they are not roll-index residue. shell side arm (`data/moves.ts:16223`): `onmodifymove` recomputes physical against special from raw stats and flips `move.category`, also setting `flags.contact` — the authority emits `[anim] shell side arm physical` and deals 99 where we deal 88 off the declared `"special"`, and no tag exists for this shape. sand force (`data/abilities.ts:3950`): the handler is a disjunction (rock or ground or steel) and `engine/tag_dex.js`'s `ontype` regex takes the first alternative only, so the artifact says `"rock"` and a bulldoze fixture never matches — while `engine/fixture_preflight.js` derives all three off the same handler, two producers of one fact disagreeing, the `artifact_audit` shape in a new place. metronome (item) (`data/items.ts:4023`): the tag `damagemultonrepeat` is complete and correct and grep finds no consumer in `medicham2-browser.js`. hustle is diagnosed and deliberately unfixed because it needs the same consumer sand force does — base-power stage plus type plus weather, which no branch of `dmgrange` serves today. land that consumer once and measure both; landing them separately makes a bad result unattributable

open.title: `slushrush` LOOKS LIKE A GENUINE ENGINE GAP AND IS THE ONLY ONE OF THE TWENTY UNEXPLAINED ABILITIES THAT DOES. Beartic a
open.full: `slushrush` looks like a genuine engine gap and is the only one of the twenty unexplained abilities that does. beartic at 50 x 2 = 100 clears feraligatr's 78, so the turn order genuinely should change once snow is up, and the harness cannot currently show it. twenty abilities still cannot say why they did not fire (down from 98 across both legs); the largest coherent group is ally mechanics — `friendguard`, `telepathy`, `hospitality`, `curiousmedicine` — which need a rung where the partner is a live participant rather than another explanation, not a new predicate. do not re-derive `ally-only` by the `isally` route: it matched 26 abilities and most mean the opposite (competitive's `if (!source || target.isally(source)) return;` excludes an ally), and that line has been held twice. a wrong explanation is worse than none and both look like coverage

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: `STATE_PLANTS` AIMS AT SLOTS WITHOUT CHECKING ANYBODY IS STANDING THERE, AND `applied` MEANS THE CALLBACK RETURNED TRUTH
open.full: `state_plants` aims at slots without checking anybody is standing there, and `applied` means the callback returned truthy. two separate holes in the board comparator's own proof, filed by measure 2026-08-20 and not fixed. 22 instances across 18 plants land on a corpse at a late boundary and now prove nothing, because the post-faint group is held on both sides after the corpse-asymmetry fix. and `applied` records only that the plant callback returned truthy, not that the board moved — the bench-hp plant takes `t[t.length-1]`, which is a fainted body, and `math.max(0, 0 - 1)` changes nothing. the driver's own comments already document that exact hazard for the active-hp plant. a plant that cannot move the board is a test that cannot fail, and this one gates the number the whole medicham finish line now rests on | open — instrument defect. measured 2026-08-21, so this row is no longer debt: `tests/probe_bench_plants.js` over 8 pairs reports 19 plants applied and not caught, 0 never applied. the six bench plants this row was filed about are now proven 5/5 (item, status, toxic stage, typing, stat stage, ability) — that half is fixed. `docs/engine.md` still says "41 of 42 are caught, the one hole is the benched-hp plant"; that sentence is contradicted by its own instrument and must not be read as current. the 19 are indeterminate rather than confirmed blind, because this row's own second hole — `applied` means the callback returned truthy, not that the board moved — makes the label unreliable. consequence: `planted_state_proof_ok` is false in every `--state` / `--end-state` artifact, so different-end-state is a lower bound wherever it is quoted, including the 83 published in changelog 5.54.0, which did not disclose it. artifact `data/verification/bench-plants-309.json`

open.title: A FAINTED MEGA'S FORME REGRESSES IN SHOWDOWN AND NOT HERE. `sim/battle.ts:2554-2557` and `:2568-2571` return a fainted m
open.full: a fainted mega's forme regresses in showdown and not here. `sim/battle.ts:2554-2557` and `:2568-2571` return a fainted mega to its base forme; `medicham2-browser.js` leaves it evolved. measured in the 797-game end-state run: 3 `species`, 2 `maxhp` and 2 `types` leaves differ on bodies both engines call dead. these were deliberately not held by the post-faint skip (changelog 5.54.0) precisely because they are the one thing about a corpse a later board can still be wrong about — a re-entry, a party-wide effect or a count over living formes can read them. small, real, and cheap

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE MOVE STAGE HANDS EVERY MOVE IN THE FORMAT TO ONE CARRIER THAT CANNOT LEARN 331 OF THEM — MEASURED 2026-08-21, NOT FI
open.full: the move stage hands every move in the format to one carrier that cannot learn 331 of them — measured 2026-08-21, not fixed. with roadmap #316's control-click exemption applied, 632 learnset refusals remain across the three roster stages and 87% sit on four fixed cast bodies: goodra-hisui 349, dragapult 106, weavile 77, torterra 26. it is not 421 accidents, it is two design decisions seen many times — `move/*` rules stage the move under test on one bulky quiet body so the comparison is about the move rather than the body, and `delivery` picks one boring vehicle per type without asking who is throwing it. the clause is report-only for the roster as of #316, declared with its reason and its concentration printed on every run: the roster does not build teams, it builds boards — `scaffold()` multiplies hp by 4, 6 or 8 and `buildpair()` constructs bodies directly in both engines, so the rig is already a position no validator would pass. the cost is stated: a shape rule that derives a carrier which cannot legally hold the entity is no longer refused. the repair is to derive the move stage's carrier from the move's own learnset and the delivery vehicle from the thrower's — which changes the carrier's types, bulk and speed and therefore changes what every move scenario measures, so it is its own batch, in the same words `data/fixture-learnset-baseline.json`'s header uses about the eight pairs that preceded it. this count must reach zero and the clause must then go back to fail marker not machine-runnable — noted 2026-08-23 by measure, row otherwise untouched. this row’s `verified by` carries an environment prefix and a literal placeholder, so `engine/register_reality.js` refuses it rather than shell-executing it, and the row files as instrument unrunnable — which is not agreement and is not evidence either. the command is a correct instruction to a human; it is not an instrument. see #381. and it cannot be decided from disk either — noted 2026-08-23 by measure. the learnset-refusal count this row is scored on is printed to stdout and written to no artifact: `data/roster.moves.json` carries `counts`, `scope`, `reds`, `mirror` and `results`, and no refusal figure at all, so the 632 can be re-read only by a human watching a run go past. instrument owed: the `learnset clause is report-only` count published into the roster artifact, so this row can be decided by a file rather than by a person.

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: 157 OF 500 MOVES PART FROM THE AUTHORITY BY 1–4 HP, AND NOTHING HAS SEEN IT SINCE 2026-08-11. The roster's move stage, r
open.full: 157 of 500 moves part from the authority by 1–4 hp, and nothing has seen it since 2026-08-11. the roster's move stage, runnable again after roadmap #316, reports 157 fired-and-boards-differ / 0 did-not-fire / 306 fired-and-boards-match on release `b240433ae8af`, against the last artifact anybody could read (2026-08-11, release `96361d523e20`) which said 0 differ. it is almost certainly one defect family, not 157: 217 of the 240 parted leaves are `hp` or `party.hp` (`torterra 1334 vs 1333`, `goodra-hisui 1215 vs 1218`, `sceptile 79 vs 75`), and 97 of the 157 entities are staged by the single rule `move/plain-attack` — a plain hit into the punching bag. the tail is 21 `status / present-in-one-engine-only` and 11 `boosts.*` off-by-one. do not read this as 157 broken moves, and do not compare it to the 2026-08-11 figure as a regression: those are different bytes, which is exactly what #316's withhold now enforces. it needs the damage arithmetic diffed on one staged hit against the authority before anything is attributed marker not machine-runnable — noted 2026-08-23 by measure, row otherwise untouched. this row’s `verified by` carries an environment prefix and a literal placeholder, so `engine/register_reality.js` refuses it rather than shell-executing it, and the row files as instrument unrunnable — which is not agreement and is not evidence either. the command is a correct instruction to a human; it is not an instrument. see #381. re-scoped 2026-08-23 by measure — it is 5, not 157, and the five are named. `data/roster.moves.json` on release `c36782953dee` (generated 2026-08-23t06:06:12z) reads 5 fired-and-boards-differ / 0 did-not-fire / 470 fired-and-boards-match / 22 could-not-stage / 3 deferred-by-owner out of 500 in scope. this is not a before/after with the 157 and may not be quoted as one — different release, and #316’s withhold rule exists precisely so that a roster count is never compared across bytes. what it does establish is that this row’s scope is now five named entities, each with its own home: `dragoncheer`, `fakeout`, `psychup` and `transform` are one fact about the `vol.focusenergy` leaf (#384), and `matchagotcha` is a drain heal one hp short (#339). the items stage carries the other two — `bigroot` (#385) and `greninjite` (#356). when those four rows close this one has nothing left to describe and closes with them.

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: KINGAMBIT ANNOUNCES THE END OF ITS FALLEN COUNTER AND THIS ENGINE DOES NOT — 5 GAMES, 31.4% OF REAL GAMES, AND IT IS PUR
open.full: kingambit announces the end of its fallen counter and this engine does not — 5 games, 31.4% of real games, and it is pure commentary. filed 2026-08-21, not fixed. `|-end|p2b: kingambit|fallenundefined|[silent]` fires on every switch-out of a supreme overlord carrier (mainline `data/abilities.ts:4732`, not overridden by `/data/mods/champions/`; the literal `fallenundefined` is the authority own quirk — `onend` runs unconditionally while `effectstate.fallen` is set only once an ally has died). the differential compares it because its `display-flags` rule drops the `[silent]` flag and keeps the line. medicham2 already holds the state correctly — `_fallenstuck`, stamped at `bringin` and frozen for the stay, exactly as the handler freezes `effectstate.fallen` — so emitting the line clears 5 games and changes nothing about the game being played. it outranks every other family in this class on corpus exposure (kingambit is brought in 26,113 of 83,125 stored games) and was deliberately not taken, because the bar is state and not protocol. the decision this row wants is a general one: does this engine mirror announcements that carry no board? answer it once rather than five games at a time

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: CLASS A OF `data/mutation-coverage.json` SAYS "NOTHING IN THE SIMULATOR IMPLEMENTS THIS FACT" AND IT IS WRONG ON AT LEAS
open.full: class a of `data/mutation-coverage.json` says "nothing in the simulator implements this fact" and it is wrong on at least one row i checked by hand — measured 2026-08-22 on release `6fb9ebd3b704`. the a/b/c/d classifier decides a from exactly two things: no `tags.param/has/withtag/reactorsto` call names the tag, and no name branch names the carrier. it does not look at the other tags on the same carrier, and a sibling tag is a third route it cannot see. `move:leechseed / immunitygate` is graded a with the string *"nothing in the simulator implements this fact"*, and the grass immunity is implemented — `medicham2-browser.js:18616` reads `perturnhp.immunetype` and refuses the seed on a grass body. the same shape covers most of the class: `move:lowkick / weightbased` sits beside a read `variablepower {kind:'targetweightkg'}`, `move:acrobatics / readsownitem` beside a read `variablepower {kind:'usernoitem'}`, `move:heatwave / inflictsburn` beside a read `statusinflict`, `move:closecombat / lowersuser` beside a read `statchange`. 31 of the 36 class-a carrier x tag rows carry an armed census probe that proves the mechanic works, which is the artifact telling you the same thing from the other side. the file's own `cannotsee` block says a third route exists; the per-row `defectwhy` contradicts it, and the per-row string is the one that gets read into a report. that is the caption-is-not-a-quarantine failure at row scale. the fix is to the string and to the ranking, not to the rule: a means "this tag is a second, unread copy of the fact", never "this mechanic is missing", and a sibling-tag column belongs in `defectevidence` beside `namebranchat`

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: 119 VALUES IN `data/tags.json` ARE READ BY NOTHING, AND THAT — NOT CLASS A — IS WHAT THE MUTATION ARTIFACT HAS BEEN HOLD
open.full: 119 values in `data/tags.json` are read by nothing, and that — not class a — is what the mutation artifact has been holding. measured 2026-08-22, release `6fb9ebd3b704`, 198,840 sheet entries. classes b and c of the sweep name a param the artifact carries and the simulator dereferences nowhere: it consumes the tag's membership and substitutes its own number. 130 carrier x tag x param rows, of which 11 are provenance metadata (see #325) and 119 are facts. ranked by share of corpus sheet entries: `move:protect / shieldsuser.{volatile,duration,bypassable}` and `stallcounterchecks.{counter,duration,deletesonfailure}` and `targetclass.{target,mustpressure}` at 67.75%; `move:fakeout / firstturnonly.{menudisable,whileactivemoveactions}` and `targetclass.*` at 12.44%; `item:lifeorb / damagemultall.costsperattack` at 10.69% — the row rediscovered the expensive way on 2026-08-21 after sitting here for sixteen days; `move:suckerpunch / needstargettoattack.needs` 7.11%; `move:flareblitz|wavecrash / recoil.readfrom` 6.42% and 5.74%; `move:matchagotcha / drain.{num,den}` 4.36% and `move:gigadrain / drain.{num,den}` 1.22%; `move:knockoff / readstargetitem.mult = 1.5` 2.65%; `move:lightscreen|reflect / halvesdamage.mult = 0.5` (deliberate and documented — the doubles engine uses 2732/4096); `item:lightclay|damprock / extendsduration.insteadof = 5`; `ability:regenerator / switchouttrigger.heal = 0.333`; `move:infestation / partialtrap.durationrange = [5,6]`. none of these is a behavioural defect on its own — the mutation moved nothing, so the engine's number currently agrees or does not matter — and that is exactly the problem: this is claude.md's *a derived artifact is not a fact until something compares it to its source* at 119 live sites, with no comparison anywhere. life orb is the proof that the failure mode is real rather than theoretical. the unit of work is a comparator, not 119 fixes: something that reads each of these params and asserts the engine's constant equals it, with a declared exception list carrying a reason (light screen's is written down already)

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE MUTATION BATTERY PERTURBS PROVENANCE FIELDS AND SCORES THE RESULT AS `READ-AND-IGNORED`, WHICH IS PURE NOISE IN THE
open.full: the mutation battery perturbs provenance fields and scores the result as `read-and-ignored`, which is pure noise in the defect count — measured 2026-08-22. 11 of the 130 shadowed-param rows mutate a field that is not a fact about the game at all: `move:toxic / nevermissesfromusertype.from = "derived:battleactions.prototype.hitstepaccuracy"`, `move:feint|phantomforce / breaksprotect.from`, `move:solarbeam|knockoff / conditionalpower.note = "condition not derivable here -- carried by another tag"`, `ability:levitate / typeimmunity.via = "not derivable -- no handler"`, `ability:earlybird / nameimplementedbysim.{what,cite}`. a `from`/`note`/`cite` field is the tag_dex citation required by the no-typing-from-memory rule; nothing should ever read it, so "mutating it changed nothing" carries no information and inflates read-and-ignored by 11. small, but it is the same class of error as counting a corpse's bookkeeping: the denominator has rows in it that cannot be anything else. skip param names in the provenance set the way `nestedparamsskipped` and `nullparamsskipped` are already skipped — counted, not silent

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THREE MECHANICS ARE GENUINELY ABSENT FROM medicham2 AND ALL THREE ARE WORTH LESS THAN 0.3% OF THE CORPUS — MEASURED 2026
open.full: three mechanics are genuinely absent from medicham2 and all three are worth less than 0.3% of the corpus — measured 2026-08-22, filed so they are not re-discovered, not so they are fixed. after hand-reading every class-a row of `data/mutation-coverage.json` that the census cannot prove (5 of 36), exactly three survive as real gaps and one — `move:leechseed / immunitygate` — is a false positive (see #323). what is real: (a) `immunitygate` on `move:trick` — the simulator contains no lookup for the tag and the string `stickyhold` appears nowhere in it, so trick succeeds against sticky hold; sticky hold has 0 uses in 198,840 corpus sheet entries, and `refusesitemloss`, the other tag that would carry it, is also unread. (b) `punishesminimize` on `move:heavyslam` (467 uses) and `move:bodyslam` (215) — neither the tag nor the string `minimize` appears in the simulator, so the never-miss and the x2 into a minimized body are both absent; minimize is 32 sheet entries, 0.016%, and the mechanic only fires against one. (c) `damagemultonrepeat` on `item:metronome` — the escalating `[4096,4915,5734,6553,7372,8192]` table is unread; 27 sheet entries. the carrier's own usage is the wrong ruler here and it is the trap this row exists to name: heavy slam is clicked 467 times, but the mechanic's reach is minimize's 32, not heavy slam's 467. do not schedule these against #324, which is worth two orders of magnitude more

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE MORPEKO SWITCH DIVERGENCE IS NOT A FORME-DATA GAP AND NOT AN ORDERING ONE — REFUTED WITH A CONTROL, AND THE REAL CAU
open.full: the morpeko switch divergence is not a forme-data gap and not an ordering one — refuted with a control, and the real cause is three defects on one shape. 2026-08-22, engine. #204 was routed on the premise that ten `event missing from medicham2` games name morpeko and that the missing forme rows caused them. three of the 40 cards in `data/divergence-turns.json` mention morpeko and one is the switch case, and it is not a switch order divergence at all: medicham2 emits no line for that slot, which is why the class is `event missing from medicham2`. speed, `comparepriority`, `switchin_order.js` and `data/switchin-order.json` are all irrelevant — those govern the order entry abilities resolve in, not which `|switch|` lines are emitted. refuted: the same board played against two releases identical but for the five forme rows gives byte-identical output. c1, engine — a non-permanent forme change is not reverted when the body leaves the field; measured off the bench, `ours morpeko-hangry` against `the authority morpeko`. showdown's `formechange` takes an `ispermanent` flag, hunger switch passes nothing, `clearvolatile` puts it back. c2, instrument — `game_differential.js` stamps `_switchkey` in `buildpair` (:2213) *precisely* so a rename cannot orphan a body (*“that body can never be switched to again”*), and `freshbodies` (:2362) — what every played game is built from — drops it: `buildpair ["morpeko","dragonite","espathra","garchomp"]` against `freshbodies [null,null,null,null]`. the resolver falls to `id(x.name)`, misses, answers `pass`. one fact, two construction paths, one of them fixed. sufficiency proved without editing the file: restamping from `onboundary` one boundary before the ask brings the subject back. c3, a different defect and said so — a mega is a permanent rename, so both engines hold `abomasnow-mega` while the ask still says `abomasnow`; the showdown branch (:3436) matches on `id(q.species.id)` and misses too, and the game throws rather than diverging. restamping does not clear it. over-fire control: the identical board asked as `{sw:'abomasnowmega'}` completes on both engines. nothing was fixed here on purpose — c1 is in `medicham2-browser.js` (owned by the damage-die agent that day) and c2/c3 are in `game_differential.js`, which is not in `sources` and is therefore read live by every run, so editing it moves a file under a measuring agent. full account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-formes.md`

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: TESTING READS A CORPUS THAT MOVES UNDER IT, AND AN ARTIFACT RECORDS WHICH BYTES OF CODE MADE IT BUT NOT WHICH GAMES — WI
open.full: testing reads a corpus that moves under it, and an artifact records which bytes of code made it but not which games — will, 2026-08-17: "lets keep scraping games but for our testing purposes i just want a frozen corpus so it doesnt move". ops appends continuously and should keep doing so — `data/games.bo3.jsonl` and `data/games.ladder.jsonl` both moved at 21:01 on the day this was filed. what must stop moving is what testing reads. two channels leak today. (1) the differential's team pool, already filed as #81 wire 5 and stated in `engine/game_differential.js:4037` in its own words: *"`buildswarm` reads data/games.bo3.jsonl and data/games.ots.jsonl live, dedupes to distinct teams and picks by a stride over the matching set — so one appended game shifts the stride and changes which teams get played"*, with the note that both files moved during that wire's own test runs. the mitigation there asserts which team keys were picked, so a moved pool is visible afterwards; it does not stop the pool moving. `data/team-pool-frozen` already exists and is half the mechanism. (2) every `uses` count, which lives in `data/tags.json` and is regenerated from the live store — two divisions reported it independently on 2026-08-15 as *"~3,271 moved lines are `uses` counts following the store"*. the cost is measured, not hypothetical and not large: the metronome closet entry states 19 uses and the artifact reads 25, with nobody having edited either — the corpus grew underneath a typed number, which is this repository's signature failure in miniature. every impact ranking built on `uses` — the divergence work order, the bring guide, the mechanics priority — is therefore against a moving target at the margin. the second half is the provenance gap and it is the reason nobody noticed: an artifact carries an `engine_release` id saying which bytes of code produced it and nothing saying which games, so two runs can differ entirely in corpus and look identical in provenance. a corpus snapshot id belongs beside the release id in every artifact that reads a game file. not a freeze of the store. ingest keeps running; testing reads a stamped snapshot. sequencing, deliberate: this lands before the mag refit and after the medicham gate closes. the refit is the run that most needs a stable corpus and is the one place where fitting against a moving target would be invisible; doing it before the gate closes would change the corpus definition under an in-flight measurement, which is the failure this row exists to prevent, committed while building the fix

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: FUR COAT CARRIES NO DEFENCE MULTIPLIER, SO medicham2 DEALS DOUBLE PHYSICAL DAMAGE THROUGH IT — FOUND 2026-08-21 BY ENGIN
open.full: fur coat carries no defence multiplier, so medicham2 deals double physical damage through it — found 2026-08-21 by engine, by accident, not fixed. furfrou was the first draft of `tests/test-bracket-regain.js`'s second foe and the board parted on the very first physical hit: `p2.party.furfrou.hp medicham 90 showdown 120` on a talonflame facade, medicham dealing exactly double. `data/abra-tags.js` gives `furcoat` a single tag, `breakable`, with no multiplier param at all, so the halving never reaches `dmgrange` — this is a `engine/tag_dex.js` derivation gap and not a missing branch in the simulator, the same shape as #312's sand force, where the derivation read one alternative of a disjunction and the artifact then looked complete. it appeared in all three arms of that file including both controls, so it could not have flipped that verdict, and the cast was changed to a body with an inert ability so `statediv === null` could be asserted rather than excused. 8 corpus sheets, so it is small — and small is exactly the size at which a defect survives, since nothing in the ranked queues will ever surface it. the derivation must be shown its own membership before it is wired: `breakable` is carried by a large family and the multiplier is not, so a predicate that over-matches here would silently halve damage through abilities that do no such thing

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE OPEN-DEFECT CLAUSE CALLS A ROW "NO INSTRUMENT DECIDES IT" WHEN WHAT IT MEANS IS "MY VERDICT ARTIFACT IS OLDER THAN T
open.full: the open-defect clause calls a row "no instrument decides it" when what it means is "my verdict artifact is older than that row" — measured 2026-08-22 on #318 and #319. `engine/where.js --gates` reads `docs/roadmap.md` live and reports that both rows name an instrument. `opendefectclause` in `engine/quarantine.js` reads `data/register-reality.json` and reports both under `debt`, whose line reads *"open row(s) assert breakage with no instrument that decides them"*. both tools are computing the right answer to their own question and one of the two sentences is false. `data/register-reality.json` was generated 2026-08-22t01:55:12z; commit `76e4a67` put the #318 row into the register at 02:33z, thirty-eight minutes later, so the clause has no verdict for a row that has carried a `verified by` marker since it was written. a second, independent cause sits under it: `register_reality.js`'s `safe` guard accepts only a plain `node <repo script>.js [--flags]`, and the marker on both rows begins `showdown_path=... node tests/roster.js --stage moves`, so a fresh run would classify them `instrument unrunnable` rather than giving them a verdict — moving them out of `debt` into the clause's third bucket, never into `withred`. neither reading changes the gate: `ok` is `withred.length === 0`, currently 3 rows (#218, #241, #258) out of 16 open-and-asserting-breakage, and `debt` has never held the clause shut. the defect is the bookkeeping, and `where.js` already does its half: since commit `cac12fa` it prints *"naming a gate is not having a verdict"*, names the artifact's age, and lists the rows with no verdict. the quarantine side says nothing. what would decide it: `opendefectclause` reads the row it is already parsing for a `verified by` marker and splits `debt` into "names nothing" and "names an instrument, no verdict recorded", and compares `register-reality.json`'s `generated` against the mtime of `docs/roadmap.md`, printing stale when the artifact is older. related and not the same row: #108 is `status.js` against `provenance.js` over artifact safety; this is the open-defect clause against `where.js` over the register's own coverage. same shape, second pair — which is itself the argument for fixing the shape rather than the instance. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-register-reconciliation.md`

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE DIVERGENCE ROLLUP'S RANKING CAN NAME THE LINE WE EMITTED RATHER THAN THE ONE THAT DIFFERS, AND A HUMAN READING 40 CA
open.full: the divergence rollup's ranking can name the line we emitted rather than the one that differs, and a human reading 40 cards found ~20 root causes where the rollup over the same run found none — measured 2026-08-22. the class name describes the comparator, not the defect. `event missing from medicham2` means "the authority emitted a line and we did not", which is a property of the diff and is the same sentence whether the cause is encore's failure condition, imposter's transform announcement or a life orb recoil. two defects with nothing in common land in one bucket and one defect lands in several depending on which line differed first, so the rollup can only ever report how the comparator classified things. over the same 961-game run its buckets were *"`-fail` 7 games"* and *"ordering 29 games"*; will grouped by mechanism instead and recognised encore, roost, toxic debris and matcha gotcha on sight. two concrete ranking defects. (1) `max_uses` is `math.max` over the entities named by both lines of a pair, so the head of a usage-ordered list can name the line we emitted: the report's own head read *"126,170 clicks, protect"* when the differing line was `-start|typechange|[from] protean`. that half is confirmed against the current file — `entitystanding` collects mentions from both sides and `max_uses` is a max over all of them. (2) the card review also records a species carrying `uses: null` printed as 0, putting the kingambit `fallen` family at the bottom of a usage-ordered list while covering 31.4% of games; that half is not confirmed against the current file — a `species_uses` block reading `data/meta-usage.json` exists and may already supply it, and the observation may predate it or belong to a different renderer. recorded as observed-and-unconfirmed rather than asserted. the action will asked for is cheaper than either fix: dump far more cards. `--dump-games 40` sampled 40 of 378 diverging games; a card costs a few hundred bytes and a missed root cause costs an evening. raise it to the low hundreds and render with `engine/divergence_cards.js`. what would decide it: print the ranking key beside each cause — which entity, from which side's line — so a reader can see whether the head names the divergent line or ours

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE ROSTER CREDITS SPIKY SHIELD ON A SCENARIO THAT CANNOT FAIL — OBSERVED 2026-08-22, INSTRUMENT WEAKNESS, MECHANIC BELI
open.full: the roster credits spiky shield on a scenario that cannot fail — observed 2026-08-22, instrument weakness, mechanic believed covered elsewhere. `all_mechanics_fire` reports `spikyshield` as resolved / no-divergence with `setup: []` — nothing attacks into it — and marks both `volatile:spikyshield` and `volatile:stall` uncomparable. so `punishescontact` (`oncontact: true, fraction: 8`, correctly derived) never fires in that row, and a green there is a green about nothing. the mechanic itself is well covered and this row is not a claim that it is broken: 40 census rows touch protect/shield/stall, including *"spiky shield hurts the attacker it blocked"* with a protect control that must toll 0 while spiky shield tolls 22, *"a spiky shield answers before the type chart"*, and *"spiky shield and baneful bunker refuse encore exactly as protect does"* for the status half (#238). the census is the strong instrument; the roster row is the weak one. note also that the authority itself announces spiky shield as `move: protect` on both `-singleturn` and `-activate`, so our naming there is correct and the renderer is faithful — that is not a defect and is recorded here so it is not filed as one later. what would decide it: the roster's scenario builder must refuse to credit a mechanic whose `setup` is empty, or must stage a contact attacker into the shield; a row that cannot fail is a test that cannot fail, which is #314's lesson applied to a different instrument. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §f2

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: `tools/lownode.cmd` IS SOUND AND ITS ARGUMENT QUOTING IS A LIVE HAZARD THAT HAS ALREADY TRUNCATED A RELEASE REASON — OBS
open.full: `tools/lownode.cmd` is sound and its argument quoting is a live hazard that has already truncated a release reason — observed 2026-08-22. the wrapper itself passes: `tests/test-lownode.js` is 4/4 including exit-code propagation, and measured directly it returned 7 for `process.exit(7)` and 1 for a module-not-found with stdout and stderr intact. the hazard is the arguments. an absolute windows path splits on its drive colon across the bash-to-`cmd` boundary, and `start` mis-parses a quoted argument containing spaces — `--seed "a vs b"` launches `cmd` rather than `node`. it has already cost something: a quoted `--why` string was truncated to a fragment on an engine-release cut, so a release carries a reason that is not the reason anybody typed. the workaround is repo-relative paths and no spaces in a quoted argument, and that is a rule somebody has to remember, which is what this register exists to replace. what would decide it: an arm in `tests/test-lownode.js` that passes an argument containing a space and an argument containing a drive-letter path and asserts the child received them byte-identically — shown red against the current wrapper before any change. related and not the same: #300, the differential's unreachable catch block on a bad `showdown_path`. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §f3

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE AUTHORITY ANNOUNCES A VOLATILE COUNTER'S EXPIRY AND WE ARE SILENT, AND NOTHING PROVES THE TWO ENGINES END ON THE SAM
open.full: the authority announces a volatile counter's expiry and we are silent, and nothing proves the two engines end on the same turn — observed 2026-08-22 by will across three cards. three cards, three counters, one question: do they tick and expire on the same turn? showdown emits `-end ... infestation [partiallytrapped] [silent]` twice and `-end ... throat chop` once, and we emit nothing. the state behind them is compared — `board_state.js:661` reads `trapped_by_move`, and the file notes the victim's half is *"the half that decides whether a switch is legal"* — but the comparator's own proof is not clean: `probe_bench_plants.js` lists a move trap counter off by one among its 19 applied-and-not-caught plants (7 of 8 pairs catch it), which is #314's second hole. so the field is read, a lie about it is mostly detected, and the instrument cannot say so with authority. an unannounced expiry at the right moment is cosmetic; one a turn late is a body that cannot switch when it should. infestation blocks switching, and perish song's last tick kills — `duration: 4`, the cast-time `perish3` is `[silent]`, and the residual prints whatever the counter now reads, one step per end of turn. not covered by #242, which is closed and settled the residual order and which of 90 walk participants announce; and not covered by #234, closed, which fixed the `[from]` attribution naming the condition where showdown names the move. neither asserts that a counter expires on the same turn. what would decide it: stage infestation, throat chop and perish song separately, run each to expiry on both engines, and assert both end on the same turn and emit the same `-end` line — with perish song's arm asserting the body dies on the same turn, since that is the one where a tick off by one is a game

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A FAILED ROOST LEAVES THE USER STILL FLYING ON THE AUTHORITY AND GROUNDED HERE, AND IT IS BOARD-MATERIAL — STAGED AND DE
open.full: a failed roost leaves the user still flying on the authority and grounded here, and it is board-material — staged and deliberately not fixed 2026-08-22. found while landing #342's `null`-against-`false` classification and stated in that commit's own account, with no register row until now. we emit the `-fail ... heal` line correctly and then also the `-singleturn`; the authority emits neither, because `runmoveeffects` marks the target `false` and `selfdrops` skips false targets. the consequence is not the two lines: it is that the roost user's flying type is suppressed here on a turn the authority leaves it flying, so a ground move that should be refused connects, and every damage and speed read for that turn is taken against the wrong type. left undone on purpose — the rule in this repository is one family per pass, and the roost family wants its own hand list rather than a free ride inside the encore/yawn batch. what would decide it: stage a roost that fails (a user already at full hp) on both engines and assert (a) neither line is emitted and (b) a ground move into that user is refused on both. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §e3 and commit `11bab14`. adjacent: #147 wired roost's grounding in the first place; #242 records that roost is residual order 25, announces nothing, and gives its type back twenty orders above the grassy terrain heal

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A FAINTED BODY STAYS IN ONE OF OUR ACTIVE SLOTS WHERE SHOWDOWN CLEARS IT INSIDE `faintMessages` — OBSERVED 2026-08-22, C
open.full: a fainted body stays in one of our active slots where showdown clears it inside `faintmessages` — observed 2026-08-22, confirmed as real state, consequence unmeasured. a dragonite read `fainted=true` together with `where=active`. showdown sets `pokemon.isactive = false` inside `faintmessages` (`sim/battle.ts:2563`); we leave the body in the active array until something replaces it. confirmed to be real state rather than a labelling artifact — `rostersnapshot` reads membership of the active array itself, not a flag. it is not the cause of card 25 (see #346, which was entirely the harness) and in the repaired game it produced zero divergent lines, so it is recorded as an observation and not asserted as a defect. it is nevertheless the same `faintmessages` region as #331 (the batching) and #315 (a fainted mega's forme), and `isactive = false` at `:2563` is what makes the authority's `tostring()` print a bare side id — so if #331 is fixed this may fall out with it. what would decide it: a boundary comparison asserting no body with `fainted=true` is a member of either active array at the moment the authority has already cleared it, plus a search for a read path (`bringin`, targeting, spread-move target selection) that would behave differently with a corpse in the slot. until one of those produces a consequence this row makes no claim about a mechanic. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §e4

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: DRAGON TAIL AND CIRCLE THROW IGNORE SUCTION CUPS — CONFIRMED, PROBED RED 2026-08-22. The phaze branch reads `refusesForc
open.full: dragon tail and circle throw ignore suction cups — confirmed, probed red 2026-08-22. the phaze branch reads `refusesforcedswitch`; the damaging branch does not, so a damaging phaze move drags a body the authority refuses to move. staged: tyranitar's dragon tail into malamar — the authority emits `-activate p2a: malamar / ability: suction cups` and nobody moves; we emit a `drag` of snorlax. malamar is the only legal carrier of suction cups in reg m-b and is brought 1,340 times across the two human stores. the membership is derived and small, which is why it can be closed cleanly: exactly two abilities and one move carry `ondragout` in the whole authority — suction cups (legal, one carrier), guard dog (zero legal carriers) and ingrain (a legal move that zero legal species can learn here). champions overrides none of the three. that is why this is the only member of the family that can fire, and it is why #175's rule holds: do not add a guard dog row by hand — `tests/test-tag-params-derived.js` proves the predicate already covers it, its absence is the legality filter, and a regulation that brings a carrier would pick it up with no edit. what would decide it: the staged tyranitar-into-malamar pair above, asserting no body moves and the `-activate` line is present, with a non-carrier control that must still be dragged

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE BENCH IS IN A DIFFERENT ORDER FROM THE AUTHORITY'S, AND BOTH OF OUR INSTRUMENTS ARE BLIND TO IT BY CONSTRUCTION — DI
open.full: the bench is in a different order from the authority's, and both of our instruments are blind to it by construction — diagnosed 2026-08-22, die hypothesis refuted, landed as a diagnosis with no row until now. the drag divergence was hypothesised to be the die and it is not: both engines roll a uniform die, consume exactly one draw, and under pinned dice draw the same value at the same address. what differs is the order of the list the die indexes into. `sim/battle-actions.ts:125-132` swaps the outgoing body into the arriving body's party slot; we remove-and-append. measured: 34.8% of side-boundaries hold the same bench in a different order, and 0 of 3,118 index positions map to the same body — zero fixed points, so a uniform index disagrees with probability 1. invisible to both instruments, and that is the important part: the protocol comparison sees no line, and `board_state.js`'s `partymap` keys the party by species — correctly, because index-keying manufactured a divergence in 123 of 179 games — and the same correct choice makes it blind to where a body is standing. blast radius is larger than the drag: `bringin`'s default replacement is `_live(bench)[0]`, so a reordered bench moves every faint replacement and every pivot with no explicit target, in rollouts and in `board.js` features. measure it; do not assume it neutral. what would decide it: a boundary-by-boundary comparison of the two party arrays by index (not by species) on a pinned run, asserting the same body stands at the same index, with the 3,118 positions as the denominator. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §e1; the diagnosis landed in commit `11bab14` and carried no register row

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: LIFE ORB RECOIL DID NOT FIRE FOR A WHOLE TURN IN A REAL GAME, WHICH IS THE BEHAVIOURAL HALF #324 EXPLICITLY EXCLUDES — O
open.full: life orb recoil did not fire for a whole turn in a real game, which is the behavioural half #324 explicitly excludes — observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 24 (index 37); not probed since. `data/tags.json` gives `lifeorb` a `damagemultall` of `mult 1.3` plus `costsperattack: "1/10 max hp"` — the multiplier is machine-readable and the cost is an english string, so nothing can derive the recoil from the tag and whatever applies it is hardcoded elsewhere, which is why it fires in two cards and not in a third. on this card gholdengo landed a resisted shadow ball and never paid its 16 hp; the stream runs to the `upkeep` marker with no life orb line at all, so it is absent for the turn, not merely late. life orb appears in 17,168 of 19,401 bo3 games and the roster credits it `fired / diverged false`, so two live instruments both call it clean. not covered by #324, and the distinction is the point: #324 registers `item:lifeorb / damagemultall.costsperattack` as one of 119 tag values read by nothing and says in its own words that *"none of these is a behavioural defect on its own — the mutation moved nothing"*. this row is the counterexample to that sentence for one member of the 119. what would decide it: replay card 24's index 37 on both engines and assert the recoil line is present, then stage a resisted hit, a super-effective hit and a hit that would leave the holder at 1 hp — a recoil applied conditionally is what the two-of-three card pattern suggests

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A SPREAD DRAIN HEALS ONCE OVER THE SUMMED DAMAGE WHERE THE AUTHORITY HEALS AND ROUNDS PER TARGET, SO WE HEAL 1 HP LESS O
open.full: a spread drain heals once over the summed damage where the authority heals and rounds per target, so we heal 1 hp less on a quarter of them — observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 1 (index 0). showdown heals per target, interleaved, with an `[of]` attribution on each; we heal once at the end and drop the attribution. the arithmetic is merged too, and that half is not narration: `dealt` accumulates across targets and the drain heals half of the accumulated total once, where the authority rounds per target (`battle.ts:2168`). the two disagree exactly when both hits deal odd damage — 25.0% of two-target spread drains — and we heal 1 hp less. legal spread-drain moves in this regulation: matcha gotcha (8,182 uses) and parabolic charge (151); parabolic charge is `alladjacent`, so up to three drains and three roundings. partially adjacent to #324, which lists `move:matchagotcha / drain.{num,den}` at 4.36% of corpus sheet entries as a param the simulator dereferences nowhere — that is the derivation half; this is the arithmetic half and #324 asserts nothing about it. what would decide it: a staged two-target matcha gotcha whose per-target damage is odd on both bodies, asserting the healer's hp matches the authority to the point, with an even-damage control that must agree both before and after the fix corroborated by the roster 2026-08-23 on release `c36782953dee`: `data/roster.moves.json` (generated 2026-08-23t06:06:12z) reads `matchagotcha` fired-and-boards-differ, and every parted leaf is the healer short by one — `goodrahisui party.hp showdown 583 ours 582` at turn 3, `592 / 591` at turn 4 — which is the direction and the magnitude this row predicts. it is corroboration and not a second measurement of the 25.0%: the roster stages one scenario, so it says the arithmetic parts and says nothing about how often.

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: `onTryImmunity` IS NOT DERIVED, SO SIX LEGAL MOVES CARRY NO IMMUNITY GATE AT ALL — OBSERVED 2026-08-22 BY WILL READING C
open.full: `ontryimmunity` is not derived, so six legal moves carry no immunity gate at all — observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 35. endeavor's gate is `ontryimmunity(target, pokemon) { return pokemon.hp < target.hp; }`, and returning false produces a type-immunity-style block (`-immune`), not `-fail`. on card 35 both bodies were at 135/135 — whimsicott and raichu share max hp at l50 and 0 ev — so `135 < 135` is false and the authority answered `-immune`; we ran the `damagecallback` (`target.hp - pokemon.hp` = 0) and announced a zero-damage line reading "drops to 100%". our tags for `endeavor` carry no immunity condition at all. legal moves on this hook: attract, endeavor, leech seed, switcheroo, trick, worry seed. trick and switcheroo matter most — a missing immunity gate means an item swap that should be blocked goes through, which is board-material. recurring shape: a fact that lives in a handler rather than a declarative field is not picked up by `tag_dex`, and the roster then credits the entity clean because nothing staged the condition — joins #317 (fur coat) and #312 (sand force). adjacent and not the same rows: #327 covers `immunitygate` on `move:trick` against sticky hold specifically (0 corpus uses), and #323 records `move:leechseed / immunitygate` as a classifier false positive because the grass immunity is implemented through a sibling tag. neither covers the hook. will's requirement, and it is the discipline that got the last `-fail` attempt retracted: stage the positive arm too. three cases, all three asserted: user hp greater than target hp gives `-immune` with no damage line; user hp equal to target hp gives `-immune` as well, because the gate is a strict less-than (the 135/135 case, easy to miss); user hp less than target hp works, the target drops to exactly the user's hp with a real `-damage` line. a test that only proves the immunity is a test that ships an endeavor which never works

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: SLEEP: THE DISTRIBUTION IS MODELLED CORRECTLY AND WHETHER THE DRAW IS ADDRESSED IDENTICALLY HAS NEVER BEEN CHECKED — RAI
open.full: sleep: the distribution is modelled correctly and whether the draw is addressed identically has never been checked — raised 2026-08-22, verification owed, no claim of breakage made. champions overrides `slp` and uses `this.sample([2, 3, 3])` (*"1/3 chance for a pokemon to wake up on turn 2"*) where mainline uses `this.random(2, 5)` giving 2, 3 or 4 — a different distribution and a different draw shape, since `sample` calls `random(3)`. our `sleep_turns_lost = 1 + 2/3` is exactly the expected value of `sample([2,3,3])`, one third times one plus two thirds times two, so the distribution half is right. what is unverified is the address: whether both engines consume the same number of draws at the same point, which is what decides every later die in a pinned game. reading mainline here is the documented way to be wrong. what would decide it: a pinned staged sleep on both engines printing the draw count and the address consumed, against the champions override read from the mod and cited by line. this row asserts nothing about a mechanic being wrong and deliberately carries no defect token in its cell: a row that overstates its scope costs a whole agent, which is more than the defect it names

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE CONFUSION SELF-HIT DRAWS A DIFFERENT INDEX FROM THE AUTHORITY, AND THE FORMULA IS RULED OUT AS THE CAUSE — OBSERVED
open.full: the confusion self-hit draws a different index from the authority, and the formula is ruled out as the cause — observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 36; root cause unprobed. our formula is correct and documented: no stab, no type chart, no crit, no screen, no burn, sixteen sides at `85+r`, matching `getconfusiondamage` (`battle-actions.ts:1850`), with one gap declared rather than hidden — an `onmodifyatk` ability, so a burned guts body hits itself harder. the move is typed with the wildcard category, so no item or type boost can reach it; that hypothesis is ruled out. authority `108 -> 75` against our `108 -> 78` is 33 against 30, and `30/33 = 0.909` sits inside the 85-100% band, so it is a different index, not a different multiplier. note the authority takes two draws here — `randomchance(33,100)` for whether to self-hit, then `randomizer(damage)` — so a different order or category shifts every later die address too, and this may be an addressing defect rather than a damage one. what would decide it: pin the dice and print the index each engine selected for the same staged self-hit, plus the draw count consumed at that address. do not fold this into #333 until the index is read: one is a scheme and the other is an address

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A PER-TARGET SECONDARY LANDS ON THE WRONG BODY — #294 FIXED THE ACCURACY ROLL AND NOT THE SECONDARY ROLL. OBSERVED 2026-
open.full: a per-target secondary lands on the wrong body — #294 fixed the accuracy roll and not the secondary roll. observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 40; not probed since. muddy water is a spread move with a 30% accuracy-drop secondary that the authority rolls per target. showdown dropped spiritomb's accuracy; we dropped snorlax's. same shape as #294 — *"the accuracy roll was one per move where the game rolls one per target"* — one hook over, and #294 is closed, so its row must not be read as covering this. the sleep difference in the same card is probably downstream of this: once a secondary fires on a different body every later die address shifts, so it must not be treated as an independent defect until this is fixed. what would decide it: a scripted per-target secondary stream on a spread move with a sub-100% secondary, asserting all four outcomes (neither, first only, second only, both) are reachable — the exact discriminator #294 used for the accuracy roll, shown red on the pre-fix tree there, and never run for secondaries

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE MULTI-HIT DAMAGE PATH WAS NEVER CONVERTED TO THE SIXTEEN-INDEX ROLL, SO #304'S FIX COVERS SINGLE HITS ONLY — PROVED
open.full: the multi-hit damage path was never converted to the sixteen-index roll, so #304's fix covers single hits only — proved by arithmetic 2026-08-22 from cards 38 and 39. `battle#randomizer` is `tr(tr(base * (100 - random(16))) / 100)`: sixteen discrete values between 85% and 100% of the base. twin beam is the clean case because both hits are 40 bp, so the base is identical for both. authority `185 -> 130 -> 75`, hits of 55 and 55 — one base, the same index twice. medicham2 `185 -> 125 -> 75`, hits of 60 and 50. no single base can produce both under that scheme: 60 requires `b >= 60` and 50 requires `trunc(b x 0.85) <= 50`, i.e. `b < 60`. contradiction. so either our base changes between hits of a constant-bp move or our draw is not the sixteen-index one. this is the unconverted residue of #304, whose own status cell already names it — *"8 games survive, candidate is the declared per-hit multi-hit randomizer"* — and a uniform draw would produce 60 and 50 from one base because it can hit any integer in the interval. it also explains will's observation that multi-hit damage "evens out": a uniform draw is unbiased about the same mean, so totals converge while individual hits scatter. what would decide it: a staged constant-bp two-hit move on both engines under pinned dice, asserting the two hits are equal whenever the authority's two are equal, plus a per-hit support count in the style of #304's `damage_interior` block

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: `onDamagingHit` IS WRONG TWICE ON ONE HOOK — IT RESOLVES BEFORE THE MOVE'S OWN SECONDARIES WHERE THE AUTHORITY RESOLVES
open.full: `ondamaginghit` is wrong twice on one hook — it resolves before the move's own secondaries where the authority resolves it after, and it fires once per move where the authority fires once per hit. observed 2026-08-22 by will reading divergence cards 29 and 37; not probed since. two defects, filed as one row because they are one derivation. order: `sim/battle-actions.ts:1099` runs `secondaries()` and `:1121` runs `runevent('damaginghit')`, so secondaries resolve first; card 29 is flare blitz's burn against a stamina defense boost in the opposite order here. frequency: card 37 has the authority laying one toxic debris layer per hit of dual wingbeat where we lay one after the move completes. twenty legal abilities ride this hook — aftermath, cursed body, cute charm, effect spore, electromorphosis, flame body, gooey, illusion, innards out, justified, mummy, poison point, rough skin, sand spit, spicy spray, stamina, static, toxic debris, wandering spirit, weak armor — and several are board-material rather than cosmetic: aftermath and innards out deal damage, so the attacker's hp when the secondary lands differs; weak armor changes speed and therefore turn order; cursed body disables a move; and mummy overwrites the attacker's ability, so running it before a secondary the new ability would have modified resolves that secondary under the wrong ability entirely. what would decide it: two staged pairs run on both engines — (a) a contact flare blitz into a stamina carrier, asserting the same relative order of the burn and the boost, and (b) a two-hit contact move into a toxic debris carrier, asserting two layers rather than one. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §a1, release `6a05dd9ad60d`, census pin `2cab3179f5fc`, 961 games / 133 diverged

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: WE ANNOUNCE A FAINT AT THE MOMENT OF LETHAL DAMAGE AND THE AUTHORITY BATCHES IT UNTIL THE ACTION COMPLETES. OBSERVED 202
open.full: we announce a faint at the moment of lethal damage and the authority batches it until the action completes. observed 2026-08-22 by will reading cards 28 and 34; not probed since. `this.add('faint', pokemon)` lives inside `faintmessages()` (`sim/battle.ts:2549`), which `runaction` calls at `:2832` after the action finishes, so showdown completes the move's own consequences — the recharge flag, stone axe's hazard, fling's item — and announces deaths afterwards. two consequences beyond the ordering itself. (1) `faintmessages(lastfirst = false, …)`: the `lastfirst` argument is why final gambit faints the user before the target on the authority and the reverse here. (2) it also explains a wording difference for free — `pokemon#tostring()` returns `p2a: name` while active and bare `p2: name` once not, and `faintmessages` sets `isactive = false` at `:2563`, so the authority's `-hitcount` names an already-dead body (`p2: azumarill`) where ours names a live one (`p2a: azumarill`). one root, two visible symptoms. likely worth more than its card count: a faint announced early shifts every line after it, so games currently filed under other classes may be downstream of this one. imposter (#320) predicted ~10 and delivered 13 for exactly that reason. what would decide it: stage a lethal stone axe and a lethal final gambit on both engines and assert the `|faint|` line's position relative to the hazard line and to the target's faint. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §a3. adjacent and not the same row: #315, a fainted mega's forme regression, which is the other half of the same `faintmessages` region

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A BERRY IS EATEN BEFORE the `upkeep` MARKER AND\|upkeep` AND BEFORE FAINT PROCESSING HERE, AND AFTER BOTH IN THE AUTHORI
open.full: a berry is eaten before the `upkeep` marker and\|upkeep` and before faint processing here, and after both in the authority — this one changes who survives. observed 2026-08-22 by will reading card 30; not probed since. the authority's residual case runs `fieldevent('residual')`, then `add('upkeep')`, then `faintmessages()`, and only then `eachevent('update')` — and sitrus hooks `onupdate`, so it eats after the turn-end marker and after deaths are processed. we eat during the residual sequence. two ways that moves the board rather than the narration. (a) a body that residual damage would kill is dead before the berry can be eaten on the authority; eating mid-sequence heals it above zero and it lives. (b) with several residuals in sequence, eating mid-sequence gives a larger hp pool to every residual that follows — body at 20, poison 15 then sandstorm 7: authority 20 -> 5 -> 0 dead, ours 20 -> 5 -> berry 36 -> 29 alive. the residual order itself is checked and correct and is not part of this row: `data/residual-order.json` carries sandstorm at order 1 / `onfieldresidual` and leftovers at order 5 / suborder 4, derived from the authority, and the simulator reads the numbers from that file rather than hardcoding them (#221, #242). will raised this as the ko-flipping hazard; the residual half is sound and the berry half is where it bites. what would decide it: stage a sitrus holder at an hp the residual chain exactly kills, on both engines, and assert the body is dead on both. source `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md` §a4
