open.title: MOODY RAISES AND DROPS DIFFERENT STATS FROM THE AUTHORITY IN 8 OF THE 121 WHOLE-GAME DIVERGENCES, AND THE INSTRUMENT CAN
open.full: moody raises and drops different stats from the authority in 8 of the 121 whole-game divergences, and the instrument cannot say whether the two engines even share the die — filed 2026-08-22 by measure with no verdict. observed on `data/game-differential.json`, release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z: six causes in `-boost field 3` and two in `-unboost field 3`, e.g. `\|-boost\|p2a\|spa\|2 <> \|-boost\|p2a\|def\|2` and `\|-unboost\|p1a\|spa\|1 <> \|-unboost\|p1a\|spe\|1`. the magnitudes agree on every one — both sides chose a raise and a drop and only the stat identity parts — so this is selection, not clamping. both selection rules were read and they agree, which is what makes the draw the live question. the authority is `data/abilities.ts:2691-2719` (champions does not override `moody`): two `this.sample` draws, the first over boosts `< 6`, the second over boosts `> -6` excluding the stat just raised, both skipping accuracy and evasion, iterating `pokemon.boosts` in key order atk, def, spa, spd, spe. ours is `engine/medicham2-browser.js:23030-23042`: `_st=['at','df','sa','sd','sp']`, the same two predicates, `math.floor(rng()*l.length)`. same membership, same order, same number of draws, same mapping. two claims the wire-queue triage made for this mechanic did not survive a check. (1) its corroboration was the roster reading `fired-and-boards-differ`; `data/roster.abilities.json`, generated 2026-08-22t19:08:07z on the same release as the differential, now reads `fired-and-boards-match` with a second control (ice body) that found *"the two deltas differ on 28 leaf/leaves, which means at least one control is live on this fixture … 24 of 38 leaf/leaves survive both controls and the verdict is computed on those alone."* the differ was a live control. (2) *"under the middle arm's pinned dice both engines draw the same value at the same address"* is not supported: `engine/game_differential.js` wraps exactly three authority methods to derive a category — `hitstepaccuracy` → `acc`, `secondaries` → `sec`, `getdamage` → `dmg` — and a residual ability draw executes in none of them. the artifact agrees from its own side: every entry of `mid_void.unshared_address_shapes` is `acc`, `crit` or `dmg`. so this may be the instrument rather than the engine, which is the morpeko shape (#328, two of three causes were the harness), and no verdict is filed. what would decide it: print the address each side uses for the moody residual draw on one staged residual and compare — extend the category wrapper past the three `battleactions` methods, or publish that a residual draw is unshared. a stat-selection probe means nothing until that is answered settled 2026-08-23 by measure — it is the instrument, by construction, and nobody should touch the engine for it. the question this row asked (*does the residual draw share an address*) is answered inside `engine/game_differential.js` itself, read tonight: `mid_cats = ['acc', 'crit', 'sec', 'dmg', 'stall']` at :699, restated as the `out` set at :872, and the comment above it names what is deliberately excluded — *"the `any` bucket is every draw with no move in scope — target selection, sleep timers, multihit counts"* — with the measurement that justified the exclusion quoted beside it (95.2% identity on one sample and 37.0% on another from the same engine). moody's stat pick is `this.sample(stats)` on a residual (`data/abilities.ts:2704`) and is exactly that class, so the two engines draw independently and cannot agree except by luck. the signature agrees with the construction rather than merely being consistent with it: across all 8 games of the 2026-08-23 run the body, the protocol index and the magnitude are identical and only the stat name differs, over 5 distinct stat pairs with no repeated pattern — a rule defect picks the same wrong stat repeatedly. six of the 8 are carded and all six name scovillain; the two `-unboost field 3` members are inferred from shape, so if they are something else the instrument count is 6, not 8. the decision is `game_differential.js`'s, not engine's: either a new shared dice category, or a permanent and published exclusion from the rate. the original what-would-decide-it stands as confirmation and is still owed — print the address each side uses on one staged residual; the verdict above is a construction argument plus a signature, and not that print. declared 2026-08-24 by measure — `impossible to compare`, 8 games, and the scope is the pick and nothing else. the declaration is landed in `engine/quarantine.js` as kind `incomparable` under its own heading (*"the authority makes a random draw at an address this harness does not share … no defect, nothing to fix"*), printed with its own count and never summed with the `authority-wrong` kind. the clause moved `declared 5 → 13`, `undeclared 43 → 35` on 48 raw over 961 games; `diverged` and `declared` both still print, so the allowance is legible rather than absorbed. it is still red and nothing here could have opened it. the negative cases are the proof, not the positive one: nine mutations of this cause — each a real defect wearing the same shape — were injected through the shipping clause and every one fell through to undeclared: accuracy in the pool, evasion in the pool, `+3` instead of `+2`, `-2` instead of `-1`, our line unattributed, one of two occurrences unattributed, the authority attributing the boost elsewhere, the boost following that slot clicking a move, and a different slot on each side. selftest 108 passed / 0 failed. so a wrong magnitude, a wrong trigger rate or a pool containing accuracy or evasion is still a defect and is still counted — only which stat the die names is declared. the row is revisitable and says so: give the residual pick a named stream on both sides the way #290 did for `tie`, and this row must be deleted, not kept. still owed as confirmation: print the address each side uses on one staged residual — the verdict rests on a construction argument plus a signature (body, protocol index and magnitude identical across all 8, only the stat name differing, over 5 distinct stat pairs with no repeated pattern), and not on that print. the corner-arm half (*8 in `middle`, zero in either corner*) is derived from the pin code on this artifact and was measured independently on an earlier run. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-declared-moody-ties.md` declaration withdrawn 2026-08-25 by measure — the premise was refuted by measurement, and the thing this row called uncomparable was our own wrong address. nothing above is rewritten; it is dated and it stands as what was believed. what the declaration claimed: that a residual `sample()` "belongs to no named category on either side, so both engines take it off the generic `any` stream at an occurrence index each engine populates with its own unrelated draws" — therefore no shared address, therefore disagreement by construction, therefore nothing to fix. what was actually wrong: the `any` stream is shared; our half of the address was stale. the middle arm keys both engines' dice on `seed\|turn\|category\|move\|target\|nth`; the authority's `move`/`target` come off `battle.activemove`/`battle.activetarget` and it nulls both after every action (`sim/battle.ts:2828`) and again at the top of the residual (`:2810`, `clearactivemove(true)`, which runs before `fieldevent('residual')` and therefore before moody draws — both call sites read at the line, 2026-08-25). `engine/medicham2-browser.js` wrote `mid_move`/`mid_tgt` at the top of each action and never cleared them, so every end-of-turn die was addressed with a move name that had already finished: `authority 20260813\|1\|any\|-\|-\|0` against `this engine 20260813\|1\|any\|curse\|p20\|0`. two addresses that cannot match are two independent dice — a private coin because the address was ours and it was wrong, not because the authority's draw is unaddressable. the evidence, derived from the committed artifacts rather than recalled — same 961 games, same frozen pool, `wholegameclause` run over each with only the staleness stamp normalised: `0447cd1` (pre-fix, release `ffdec64bed0c`) 35 raw, declared 13 = incomparable 8 + authority-wrong 5, undeclared 22; `382e998` (post-fix, release `cbf345e56bc0`) 28 raw, declared 5 = incomparable 0 + authority-wrong 5, undeclared 23; `65a9c5c` (head, release `359b51b61d83`) identical to the post-fix figures. the eight games were seven causes — 6 x `-boost field 3`, 2 x `-unboost field 3` — and after the address fix zero games carry either shape. six stopped diverging outright; two now part on a different cause (`\|-immune\|p1a <> \|-miss\|p2b\|p1a`, and `\|switch\|p1a\|krookodile <> \|detailschange\|p1b\|charizardmegay`), so the exemption had been sheltering two real divergences that nothing could see while it stood. the engine change is engine's, in `midclearactivemove()`, with `medi_active_move_sticky=1` restoring the leak and stamping `medfails.activemovestickyrestored` so the red is reproducible rather than remembered. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-25-board-material-3.md` (engine) and `docs/_reports/2026-08-25-moody-undeclared.md` (this withdrawal). the row's own owed item is what killed it. this row said twice, in its own words, that the address print was *"still owed as confirmation"* and that the verdict rested on *"a construction argument plus a signature, and not on that print"*. the print was finally taken, and it refuted the verdict rather than confirming it. it also said the row must be deleted, not kept if the residual draw were ever given a shared stream; the stream was already shared and the row is duly withdrawn. what is not in dispute and never was: moody's rule. the authority takes two `sample()` draws over the five main stats only (`data/abilities.ts:2691-2716`, both loops `continue` on accuracy and evasion) and this engine implements that. what landed in code: the `incomparable` row is removed from `declared_divergence` in `engine/quarantine.js`, together with the two helpers that had no other caller, and replaced by a withdrawal note where the row stood. the nine negative mutations it used to be proven against are now simply the default — every one of them is undeclared — and a red ratchet asserts that a moody-shaped stat-pick divergence is undeclared and holds the gate shut, so re-adding the exemption goes red. the `incomparable` kind survives with no live row, and the two kinds are still proven to print apart on a synthetic pushed row rather than a shipping one. selftest 100 passed, 0 failed. the pattern, which is the part worth keeping: this is the fourth "nothing to fix here" in three days that turned out to be real — speed ties, tailwind twice, now moody's stat pick. in every case the reasoning was plausible and cited a line, and in every case the mechanism itself was never independently checked. a declaration is only as good as its mechanism, and a mechanism nobody re-derived is a guess wearing a citation.

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A `\|switch\|` LINE IS ORDERED BY THE DEPARTING BODY'S SPEED IN THE AUTHORITY, AND NOTHING PUBLISHES WHETHER WE AGREE —
open.full: a `\|switch\|` line is ordered by the departing body's speed in the authority, and nothing publishes whether we agree — 3 of the 121, filed 2026-08-22 by measure with no verdict. causes (release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z): `ordering :: \|switch\|p1b\|whimsicott,l50\|h/h <> \|switch\|p1a\|alakazam,l50\|h/h` (turn 2, a same-side double switch), `\|switch\|p1a\|staraptor <> \|switch\|p2a\|incineroar`, `\|switch\|p1a\|palafin <> \|move\|p2b\|helpinghand`. the authority's key is derived and verified line by line: `sim/battle-queue.ts:270` `if (!deferpriority) this.battle.getactionspeed(action);` → `sim/battle.ts:2657` `action.speed = action.pokemon.getactionspeed();`, and `switchaction` documents its own fields at `sim/battle-queue.ts:56-69` — `pokemon` is *"the pokemon doing the switch"* (the outgoing body) and `target` is *"pokemon to switch to"*. not covered by #330: #328 says in as many words that `switchin_order.js` governs entry ability order and not which `\|switch\|` lines are emitted. and an instrument gap found while looking, which is why no verdict is filed: this engine already declares an approximation on exactly this axis — `medfails.entryordertie` and `medfails.replaceordertie` (`medicham2-browser.js:1866-1874`), *"showdown shuffles the instaswitch pair; this engine keeps side order and counts the event, because drawing a number here would move the rng stream of every seeded run in the repo"* — and neither counter is published in `data/game-differential.json`, so the artifact cannot tell a declared tie from an ordering defect. what would decide it: publish the two counters in the run, then stage two double-switches with a known speed spread and assert the `\|switch\|` line order extended 2026-08-23 onto the settled artifact: on release `c66976713feb` (961 games, generated 2026-08-23t02:40:37z, triage `ea26208`) this class is 5, not 3. the two new causes — `ordering :: \|switch\|p1a\|garchomp <> \|switch\|p2b\|blastoise` and `\|switch\|p1a\|swampert <> \|switch\|p2a\|delphox` — are both post-faint replacements, and the second refutes a naive reading from inside the file: the authority moved the slower side first, so replacements do not go in speed order of the incoming body. four of the five carry `max_uses: null` — the mentions are species and species have no `uses` — so a usage-ordered head buries this group while it fires on every double switch and every post-faint replacement. the unpublished-counter ask above is still unmet and is now carried by #375 as well.

open.title: WE FLINCH WHERE THE AUTHORITY MOVES — 2 OF THE 121, AND THIS ONE IS INSIDE THE ARM'S ADDRESSED SET. FILED 2026-08-22 BY
open.full: we flinch where the authority moves — 2 of the 121, and this one is inside the arm's addressed set. filed 2026-08-22 by measure with no verdict. two causes (release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z): `\|-immune\|p1b <> \|cant\|p2a\|flinch` and `unrelated event mismatch :: \|move\|p2a\|psychicfangs <> \|cant\|p2a\|flinch`. in the second the authority's metagross uses psychic fangs and ours cannot act, so it is board-material in both directions — a turn of damage that does or does not happen. unlike #351 a shared-die argument is available here: the flinch chance is rolled in `secondaries`, which is one of the three methods `engine/game_differential.js` wraps for its address (`sec`), so the two engines are drawing at an addressed site and identity is measurable. #84 is not this — that is the `false`-against-`null` question and it is closed. what would decide it: fake out into a body under the same pinned `sec` stream, and assert `\|cant\|…\|flinch` fires on both engines or on neither

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: TWO TAILWINDS EXPIRING ON THE SAME TURN COME OUT IN THE OPPOSITE ORDER, AND #242 SETTLED WHERE IN THE WALK RATHER THAN W
open.full: two tailwinds expiring on the same turn come out in the opposite order, and #242 settled where in the walk rather than which side — 2 of the 121, filed 2026-08-22 by measure. one cause with `n=2` (release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z): `ordering :: \|-sideend\|p2:\|tailwind <> \|-sideend\|p1:\|tailwind`. #242 is closed and does not cover it: it placed tailwind at `onsideresidualorder 26 / onsideresidualsuborder 5` and landed ten clocks inside the residual walk, on both sides — an order that is by construction identical for the two sides, so it cannot decide which of them announces first. it is not a die. `engine/game_differential.js:2854` installs `battle.prng.shuffle = arm.shuffle`, the identity, in every arm, so the authority's `speedsort` tie resolution is deterministic on input order here and the two `-sideend` lines are directly comparable. a side holder has no speed, so `comparepriority`'s middle term cannot separate them either and the answer is whatever order `findsideeventhandlers` collects the two sides in. what would decide it: tailwind up on both sides with the same expiry turn, assert which `-sideend` lands first, and read the authority's collector order rather than inferring it derived 2026-08-24 by engine, and it needs a ruling rather than a fix — card 1 of `docs/_reports/2026-08-24-ordering-cards.md`. the two `-sideend` lines are tied on all five of the authority’s sort keys: `resolvepriority` (`sim/battle.ts:993-999`) fills the fifth key, `effectorder`, only for `switchin` and `redirecttarget` — an end-of-turn side clock never gets one — so `speedsort` hands the pair to `prng.shuffle` (`:456`) and a coin decides on the authority. staged both ways: with the shuffle pinned to the identity the authority says p1 first, reversed it says p2 first, and both tailwinds end in both arms. our side is `residualorder` (`engine/medicham2-browser.js:5487`), a stable sort, which always says p1. it is narration, and that was checked rather than assumed: the residual handler list is speed-sorted once before the walk (`sim/battle.ts:505`), so a tailwind ending cannot reorder anything after it; nothing between the two lines reads side state; and the speed consequence is not applied until the next turn’s `commitchoices`. 2 games of 961. the question for will: declare this pair impossible to compare (the authority itself is flipping a coin), or leave it undeclared and red. this is not the same question as #376 — there the tie device is pinned on both sides and must therefore agree; here the authority’s fifth key is genuinely absent. see also #422, the residual sort’s own defect, which is a different claim the card's derivation was verified 2026-08-24 and the row still waits on one word from will — measure. both halves of the card were checked rather than accepted. (1) the authority's fifth sort key really is absent here: `resolvepriority` fills `effectorder` only for `switchin` and `redirecttarget`, so an end-of-turn side clock never gets one and the tied pair really does reach `prng.shuffle` — staged both ways, identity says p1 first and reversed says p2 first, and both tailwinds end in both arms. (2) the consequence really is narration: the residual handler list is speed-sorted once before the walk (`sim/battle.ts:505`), so a tailwind ending cannot reorder anything after it; nothing between the two lines reads side state; and the speed consequence is not applied until the next turn's `commitchoices`. nobody here may declare it, and that is the point of leaving it open. a declaration subtracts a row from the open-defect clause, and this project has already had a live turn-order defect sitting under a heading reading "nothing to fix" — the withdrawal recorded in #376. the two options stay exactly as the card put them: declare the pair incomparable because the authority itself is flipping a coin, or leave it undeclared and red. 2 games of 961. shelved 2026-08-24 on will's ruling — deferred, not declared. will: *"tailwind coming out in the wrong order doesnt matter, put it into the closet with that note and move on."* his reasoning, checked against the derived residual order rather than accepted: tailwind resolves at order 26, after weather (1), poison (9), burn (10) and perish song (24), so no damage remains to land; the two tailwind handlers are adjacent in the list, so nothing runs between them that could read the difference; the handler list is speed-sorted once before the walk (`sim/battle.ts:507`), so an expiry inside the walk cannot reorder anything after it; and the speed consequence is not applied until the next turn's choices, identically on both sides. which tailwind ends first therefore cannot affect a game. this is a deferral and not a declaration, which is the whole point. it remains a real, deterministic narration divergence that we have chosen not to fix, quoted and dated above. it is deliberately not added to the declared kinds in `engine/quarantine.js` — a deferred row asserts that something is wrong, so it must never be subtracted from the divergence count; it stays undeclared, red, and named on every run, which is exactly the behaviour that stops a chosen deferral becoming a quiet pass. it is narration, so it already sits outside the board-material bar will set on 2026-08-22, and shelving it moves no gate figure. two corrections to this row's own derivation — 2026-08-24 by measure. the text above is left standing as dated history and is wrong on both points. (1) a coin does not decide it. the account above ends *"a coin decides on the authority"*. it does not: with `prng.shuffle` held at the identity — which is what `game_differential.js` installs in every arm — the authority still reverses the pair on the right board. the reversal is deterministic, so the pair is comparable, and impossible to compare was correctly refused as a filing for it. (2) the remaining cause is the handler list, not the sort. the speed sort is now correct at all four sites (#422). what our walk cannot reproduce is the authority's full residual handler list: the authority's selection sort swaps rather than shifts, so sorting the front of the list displaces the tail, and every held item adds a handler that participates in that displacement. the same cause covers two screens expiring on both sides in one turn.

open.title: PROTEAN DOES NOT FIRE ON A MEGA FORME, SO GRENINJA-MEGA KEEPS THE WRONG TYPES FOR THE REST OF THE GAME — TWO INSTRUMENTS
open.full: protean does not fire on a mega forme, so greninja-mega keeps the wrong types for the rest of the game — two instruments on one release, filed 2026-08-22 by measure. differential (release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z): `event missing from medicham2 :: \|-start\|p1b\|typechange\|normal\|[from]protean <> \|-singleturn\|p1b\|protect`. roster (`data/roster.items.json`, generated 2026-08-22t19:07:58z, the same release `13ba05093aa3`): `greninjite` is `fired-and-boards-differ` and its `diffs` are four leaves that are all one fact — `turn 1 party.types showdown normal ours dark/water`, `turn 1 p2a types normal / dark/water`, and the same pair again at turn 2. the facts are derived from the format, not typed: `d.species.get('greninjamega').abilities` is `{"0":"protean"}` and `d.moves.get('protect')` is type normal, category status — which is why the authority retypes the user to normal on a protect click and only then writes `-singleturn`. this is not an announcement. the body's types are wrong from that click onward, so every damage calculation, every immunity gate and every resistance read after it is taken against a body the authority does not have. related but not this: #49 (delete the 77 hand-typed mega abilities) and #204 (forme data); this row is about the ability firing on the evolved forme corroborated again 2026-08-23 on release `c36782953dee`, and this row’s mechanism is under re-derivation. `data/roster.items.json` (generated 2026-08-23t06:05:47z) still reads `greninjite` fired-and-boards-differ with the same four leaves — `turn 1 party.types showdown normal ours dark/water`, `turn 1 p2a types normal / dark/water`, and the pair again at turn 2 — on a control click that is now focus energy, itself a normal move, so the symptom reproduces under a different click. what is under re-derivation is the latch, not the symptom. will says protean is once-per-switch-in rather than once-per-move, and the source agrees: read: `pokemon-showdown/data/abilities.ts:3489` opens `onpreparehit` with `if (this.effectstate.protean) return;` and sets `this.effectstate.protean = true` at `:3494`, and `data/mods/champions/abilities.ts` carries no `protean` key, so champions does not override it. this row’s title says only that the ability fails to act on the mega forme; it says nothing about the latch, and a fix written from the title alone could retype on every click — wrong from turn 2 onward, and green on the one staged turn. the row is not rewritten here: engine owns the mechanism and proposes the text. measure’s note is only that the fix must be scored against the once-per-switch-in reading, with a second click in the same staged pair.

open.title: TELEPATHY ANNOUNCES AN ACTIVATION AND WE ANNOUNCE AN IMMUNITY — THE RIGHT BOARD, THE WRONG LINE TYPE. FILED 2026-08-22 B
open.full: telepathy announces an activation and we announce an immunity — the right board, the wrong line type. filed 2026-08-22 by measure. cause (release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z): `unrelated event mismatch :: \|-activate\|p2a\|telepathy <> \|-immune\|p2a\|[from]telepathy`, read off a real turn as `sd \|-activate\|p2a: oranguru\|ability: telepathy` against `med \|-immune\|p2a: oranguru\|[from] ability: telepathy`. derived from the format, `data/abilities.ts:4923-4929` and not overridden by champions: `ontryhit(target, source, move) { if (target !== source && target.isally(source) && move.category !== 'status') { this.add('-activate', target, 'ability: telepathy'); return null; } }`. `return null` is #342's four-valued result — *handled, stay silent* — so the ally hit is cancelled with an `-activate` and never with an `-immune`; ours picks the failure vocabulary for a refusal the authority does not call one. 0.91% of teams. what would decide the fix: one staged ally-aimed spread hit into a telepathy body, asserting the line type and not only that the damage was blocked

open.title: THE MULTI-HIT COUNT DIVERGENCE DOES NOT REPRODUCE, AND THE ROW EXISTS SO IT IS NOT RE-DISCOVERED AS NEWS — FILED 2026-08
open.full: the multi-hit count divergence does not reproduce, and the row exists so it is not re-discovered as news — filed 2026-08-22 by measure with no verdict. the wire-queue triage read one game on `data/game-differential.json` release `603d9a69d5a3` (generated 2026-08-22t06:47z) where showdown's scale shot hit 4 times and ours hit 5. on the current artifact (release `13ba05093aa3`, 961 games, generated 2026-08-22t19:15z) `scaleshot` occurs twice and both are coverage lists — it is not in the cause table at all. three explanations and nothing separates them: it was fixed between the two releases; the game that carried it now stops at an earlier divergence (the differential records only the first divergence per game); or the pool moved. #103 is not this defect — that one answered the mean 3.1 to every question and is done, and a constant 3.1 cannot produce a 5 — and #333 is multi-hit damage, whose fix does not touch the count. the count's draw carries #351's caveat: `sim/battle-actions.ts` draws a non-2-5 count as `random(h[0], h[1]+1)`, which executes in none of the three methods `game_differential.js` wraps to derive a die address, so whether the two engines share that draw is not established by this run either. what would decide it: stage scale shot under a pinned die and assert the same number of `-damage` lines on both engines. at 1 game it does not earn an evening; the row is here so the next reader knows it was looked at

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A SIMULTANEOUS DOUBLE WIPE IS A WIN ON THE AUTHORITY AND A DRAW HERE — WINNER-DECIDING, AND INVISIBLE TO EVERY PROTOCOL
open.full: a simultaneous double wipe is a win on the authority and a draw here — winner-deciding, and invisible to every protocol comparison we run. filed 2026-08-23 by measure. the authority, read in the checkout tonight: `sim/battle.ts:2605` — `this.win(faintdata && this.gen > 4 ? faintdata.target.side : null)` inside `checkwin`'s `if (this.sides.every(side => !side.pokemonleft))`, and `faintdata` is the last entry `faintmessages()` shifted off the queue at `:2546`. so in gen 5+ both sides emptying is not a draw: the side whose body fainted last wins — the cartridge rule that the self-destructing player loses, written as a queue position. *(the citation carried in was `:2603`; that is where the `checkwin(` signature sits in this checkout and the `win()` call is two lines below. stated so the next reader does not re-derive it.)* ours has no such rule: `battleresult(s)` in `engine/medicham2-browser.js` (`:24478` when read at 2026-08-23t01:40z; that file is under active engine edit and the number had already moved to `:24529` by 02:00 — grep the symbol, never this line) compares live-body counts, falls through to total hp fraction, and returns 0.5 for 0-against-0 four lines below — its own header calls that *"dead-even hp tie at the 20-turn horizon"*, which a mutual wipe is not. measured, not argued: `tests/probe_selfdestruct_winner.js` board `w3-simultaneous` — one boom on turn two takes all four remaining bodies — reads showdown `winner="b"` with `pokemonleft p1=0 p2=0` against medicham2's draw. it is declared known-open in that file and reported rather than swept in, and the disagreement is identical clean and under that file's surgical revert, so it is not the self-ko faint position (#331's region) and not the arm. why no instrument we own can see it: every whole-game comparison here compares protocol lines or boards. two engines can emit identical lines to the character and still disagree about who won, so `engine/game_differential.js` has no class for this and never will until a winner is compared. the blast radius is the leaf, not the narration — `battleresult` is what the sealed rollout and the tower end screen read, so every mutual wipe in every rollout is scored half a win, including the ones the authority scores as a loss. will's related case is carried as his hypothesis and not as a fact: perish counters resolve in speed order, so the slowest body faints last and its side would win. #115 landed the speed-ordered residual walk and its own status cell already notes `battle.ts:2604` awards a double ko to the last faint — engine is deriving the perish half now, and nothing in this row asserts it. what would decide the fix: a faint-order field written at every faint site in the engine (`battleresult` cannot acquire the rule without one), then `w3-simultaneous` promoted from reporting to asserting equality against `battle.winner`, with the perish-counter board as the second scenario once engine's derivation lands. instrument owed: a faint-order field written at every faint site in the engine, and `w3-simultaneous` promoted from reporting a known-open verdict to asserting that our result equals the authority’s `battle.winner`.

open.title: THE `-boost field 3` CLASS IS 9 OF THE CURRENT 96 WHOLE-GAME DIVERGENCES AND THE ARTIFACT CAN NAME A MECHANISM FOR ONLY
open.full: the `-boost field 3` class is 9 of the current 96 whole-game divergences and the artifact can name a mechanism for only 2 of them — filed 2026-08-23 by measure with no verdict. read, not re-run, off `data/game-differential.json`: release `59bb68aa89a9`, generated 2026-08-22t22:50:24z, 777 games / 96 diverged / 0 threw, census pin `80e648f34d56`, team pool `b2b61ec40281`. nine causes, each `n=1`, and every one is a magnitude-2 raise on the same slot with a different stat — `\|-boost\|p2a\|atk\|2 <> \|-boost\|p2a\|spe\|2`, `\|-boost\|p1a\|spa\|2 <> \|-boost\|p1a\|atk\|2`, and seven more of that shape. board-material: a +2 on the wrong stat is a different damage roll, a different turn order, or both, for the rest of the game. there is no `-unboost` class in this artifact at all, so the drop half of #351's observation does not appear on this sample. the class name describes the comparator, not the defect, and here that matters: one mechanism is named, seven are unnamed, and the instrument cannot name them. `first_divergences` samples 60 of the 96 games and holds 2 of these 9; in both, our line is `\|-boost\|p2a: scovillain\|spe\|2\|[from] ability: moody`. those two are #351's row and are not re-filed here. the other seven carry no mechanism anywhere in the file — a whole-file scan finds the string `moody` exactly twice, both in those two sampled lines. the reason is structural: `classify()` in `engine/game_differential.js` (`:3902` when read at 2026-08-23t01:40z; that file is under active engine edit — grep the symbol) builds the cause from the normalised line, and the `stat-attribution` entry of `equiv` strips `[from]`/`[of]` from every `-boost` and `-unboost`, 9,631 lines collapsed on this run. that rule is correct for the comparison — a stat line's meaning is (body, stat, direction, amount), and it ships with a red demonstration in both directions — and it is lossy for triage. right instrument, wrong question asked of it. at least two legal mechanisms produce exactly this shape, derived from the format rather than recalled: `moody`, whose legal carriers filtered to the regulation are exactly glalie and scovillain (367 in the abilities column of `data/regulation-usage.json`, clean corpus 17,563 games / 424,933 clicks), and acupressure — `isnonstandard: null`, *"raises a random stat of the user or an ally by 2"*, 42 clicks — which can also raise an ally, a shape moody cannot produce. a third class needs no random draw at all: a deterministic +2 move whose stat we map wrongly. so this class must not be worked as one defect. #351's caveat rides all of it: `game_differential.js` wraps three authority methods to derive a die address (`hitstepaccuracy`, `secondaries`, `getdamage`) and neither a residual ability draw nor a move's own random-stat draw executes in any of them, so whether the two engines even share the draw is not established by this run either. what would decide it: publish the attribution beside the cause — the normaliser can keep stripping it from the comparison while the artifact records what it stripped — and then the seven can be counted before anything is staged. a stat-selection probe means nothing until the class is split. instrument owed: the stripped `[from]` attribution published beside each cause in the artifact, so the nine can be split by mechanism before anything is staged. extended 2026-08-23 onto the settled artifact — the headline count above is not rewritten, it is superseded by a different sample. on release `c66976713feb` (961 games / 95 diverged / 0 threw, generated 2026-08-23t02:40:37z, triage `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-remaining-56.md`, `ea26208`) the `-boost field 3` class is 6, not 9, in five causes (one with `n=2`); the `-unboost` half this row recorded as absent is back as exactly one cause (`\|-unboost\|p1a\|spa\|1 <> \|-unboost\|p1a\|spe\|1`, moody's drop shape, which is #351's original observation); attribution recoverable from the file is 1 of the 6 and no more — a whole-file scan finds `moody` once and `acupressure` zero times; and the candidate split is now bounded from the pinned pool rather than argued — in `data/team-pool-frozen`, `acupressure` appears in one line each of `games.bo3.jsonl` and `games.ots.jsonl` (the same set) against `moody` at 813 + 204, so acupressure can explain at most 1 of the 6, and only if that team was drawn and the coverage driver clicked it. the five that cannot be attributed die on the instrument's dump cap, now filed as #375.

open.title: THE 22 DAMAGING `self` MOVES FAIL THROUGH A DOOR THAT HAS NEVER BEEN MEASURED, AND THE DECLARATION LIVED ONLY IN A CHANG
open.full: the 22 damaging `self` moves fail through a door that has never been measured, and the declaration lived only in a changelog — filed 2026-08-23 by measure, no verdict. #343 staged the one heal-primary status member (a failed roost, where we emit the `-fail` and then also the `-singleturn` and ground a body the authority leaves flying) and that pass declared the rest open rather than sweeping them in — correct, the scope of a fix is the scope that was probed. but the declaration existed only in changelog 5.74.0 and in no register row, which is the same failure as a figure that lives only in prose: nothing could print it, so nothing could act on it. membership derived from the format tonight, filtered to the regulation, not typed: 25 legal moves carry a `self` effect; 3 are status — baton pass, roost, shed tail — and exactly one of those is heal-primary (roost, `self.heal` true); 22 are damaging. ten carry `self.boosts` (close combat, superpower, hammer arm, ice hammer, headlong rush, draco meteor, leaf storm, overheat, make it rain, armor cannon), eleven `self.volatilestatus` (hyper beam, giga impact, outrage, thrash, petal dance, raging fury, uproar, blast burn, hydro cannon, frenzy plant, rock wrecker), one `self.onhit` (burn up). this is not a tail: 32,135 clicks of 424,933 in the clean corpus — 7.6% — and close combat alone is 18,600, with draco meteor 3,291, make it rain 2,811, overheat 1,879 and hyper beam 1,708. the door is the one #343 found: `runmoveeffects` writes `damage[i] = false` on a refused hit, `spreadmovehit` sets `targets[i] = false`, and step 4 `selfdrops` skips a false target — so for each of the 22 the open question is whether our self-rider fires on a hit the authority refused (a protect, a type immunity, a miss, a substitute). for the ten boost members that is a stat stage that does or does not exist; for the eleven volatile members it is whether the user is locked or recharging, which decides the whole of the following turn. nothing here claims they are wrong. the failure path has not been measured on any of the 22, on either engine, and no `defect` token is filed — an unprobed member is not a defect, and calling it one would corrupt the open-defect clause exactly as much as missing a real one. what would decide it: one staged pair per `self` shape rather than per move — close combat into a protect asserting the defence drop on both engines or on neither; hyper beam into a ghost asserting `mustrecharge` on both or on neither, which is the board #161 records wire 43 getting backwards once already; burn up into a target that refuses it for the `onhit` shape. three probes cover 22 members, and the shapes are derived, not listed. instrument owed: one staged pair per `self` shape — boosts, volatilestatus, onhit — asserting the self-rider fires on both engines or on neither when the authority refused the hit.

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE DIFFERENTIAL MIRRORS A FORCED SWITCH BY SPECIES NAME, SO IT CANNOT EXPRESS A RENAMED BODY OR ONE ALREADY ON THE FIEL
open.full: the differential mirrors a forced switch by species name, so it cannot express a renamed body or one already on the field — one instrument defect wearing three faces. filed 2026-08-23 by measure. `mirrorforcedswitch` in `engine/game_differential.js` (`:3743` when read at 2026-08-23t01:40z; that file is under active engine edit and had moved to `:3754` by 02:00 — grep the symbol, and it is exported) turns medicham2's replacement into a showdown choice with `roster.findindex((q, n) => !claimed.has(n) && !q.isactive && !q.fainted && id(q.species.id) === id(body.name))`. a miss writes `cannot`, which becomes `mirrorimpossible` and then, at the call site, `endreason = "the boards parted — medicham2's placement cannot be expressed to showdown"` at `:3533`. the message already distinguishes the two ways to miss: *"does not have under that name"* — the body was renamed (transform, forme change) — and *"has but cannot switch in (fainted/active)"* — the body is already on the field. neither is expressible by a name-keyed lookup, and both are the instrument, not the engine. measured on the current artifact (`data/game-differential.json`, release `59bb68aa89a9`, 777 games, 2026-08-22t22:50:24z): `declared_gaps.forced_switch_unmirrorable` = 11, against 959 slots mirrored and 7 legitimately passed, first instance *"p1: slot 1 holds froslass, which showdown has but cannot switch in (fainted/active)"*. the middle arm ends 2 of 777 games on it, `top-tie-first` 2 and `bottom-tie-first` 5 — and one of those end reasons names `froslassmega`, the renamed face sitting in the published record. every game that ends this way is a game whose remaining turns were never compared. three staged scenarios are this one mechanism and were proved to be, not assumed: `imposter-copies-the-body-opposite`, `hungerswitch-flips-every-turn` and `roar-drags-whoever-is-standing-there` in `tests/staged_board.js` return the identical short verdict at the identical turn with the identical `endreason` under all four arms, with `err=null`, `statediv=null` and the engines agreeing on every board, byte-identical on releases `18b227eee69f` and `39631097fcc7`. not the arm, not the dice, not the engine. and nothing gates them: `tests/staged_board.js` is not `test-*.js` so `tests/run-all.js` does not discover it, while seven `test-*.js` files require it as a library — `test-assert-mode`, `test-forme-assert`, `test-middle-stall-address`, `test-perish-song`, `test-roster-arm-pin`, `test-switch-back-renamed`, `test-volatile-duration` — and `tests/test-forced-switch-mirror.js` drives the exported helper directly. one fix, nine instruments. #346 is closed and is not this row: it fixed the fallback's lack of memory of what the other slot had just taken on a double ko. this is the key itself, and #346 must not be read as covering it. what would decide it: mirror on the roster index medicham2 chose rather than on a name, then stage a transform and a forme change through a forced switch and assert the game does not stop. sources `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-wrong-arm-callers.md` and `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-drag-and-fail.md`. instrument owed: a clause that fails while `declared_gaps.forced_switch_unmirrorable` is non-zero, plus a staged transform and a staged forme change driven through a forced switch.

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: `tests/test-precharge-order.js` PUBLISHED "83 CHECKS" MEASURED ON AN ARM IT NEVER NAMED, AND 21 OTHER CALLERS ARE IN THE
open.full: `tests/test-precharge-order.js` published "83 checks" measured on an arm it never named, and 21 other callers are in the same state with 7 already cleared — filed 2026-08-23 by measure. `primary_arm` on the live driver is `middle` (read off it, not assumed), so a caller that omits `arm` silently gets live dice. `test-precharge-order.js` was screened under three arms and it moves: under `bottom-tie-first` four of its arms produce more protocol — 11→12, 14→16, 12→13, 10→11 lines — because secondaries fire and crits land that the middle arm did not draw. its verdict does not flip today, because both engines share the arm and agree either way; what is weaker is the claim. *"the two protocol streams do not part"* means less on a board where fewer things happened, and `docs/engine.md:1596` and `:1650` publish "five arms, 83 checks" measured exactly there. the population is 22, not the 27 first reported, derived by parsing each `playgame` call site's balanced argument list instead of grepping for the string `arm:`: three files pass the arm as an es6 shorthand (`{ script, arm }`, no colon) and were accused wrongly, and two never call the driver's `playgame` at all — `replaygame` contains it as a substring. and it is bigger in the other direction: 4 more reach it indirectly through `tests/staged_board.js`'s exported `runone(sc, patchedsrc)`, which takes no arm parameter at all, and 7 more are the driver's own self-proofs — `planted_divergence_proof`, `directed` and `knock_off_roadmap_80` are published blocks of `data/game-differential.json` riding them, and a plant that has to beat live dice is a weaker red than one on a corner. 14 of the 22 publish a figure; 8 were screened and 7 are byte-identical across `middle`, `top-tie-first` and `bottom-tie-first` — inert with evidence, which is the noise floor the one positive rests on. will's rule governs the repair — fix one at a time, re-measure, withdraw only what moves. seven figures have already been cleared rather than withdrawn on suspicion, which is the point of screening before retracting. a correction is owed to `docs/engine.md`, which publishes 27 in two places; engine owns that ledger. this row does not withdraw the 83. it has not been re-measured on a named arm, so what is established is that the instrument is arm-dependent — not what the number becomes. source `docs/_reports/2026-08-22-wrong-arm-callers.md`. instrument owed: a check that every `playgame` call site names an arm, so an unpinned caller fails by name instead of being audited by hand once a quarter.

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE 5.74.0 RETRACTION'S MECHANISM IS NOT SUPPORTED BY EITHER ARTIFACT: THE TEAM-STORE FIELD HAS EXISTED SINCE 2026-08-07
open.full: the 5.74.0 retraction's mechanism is not supported by either artifact: the team-store field has existed since 2026-08-07 and both runs declare the same frozen pool. filed 2026-08-23 by measure, with no verdict on the remainder. changelog 5.74.0 revised its divergence-rate-over-usable from 9.7% to 11.69% and gave two reasons: that `--team-store data\team-pool-frozen` *"did not take"*, and that "`data/game-differential.json` records no team-store field at all". the second is false. `steer_stamp.team_store_pinned_to = team_store \|\| null` in `engine/game_differential.js` (`:4849` when read at 2026-08-23t01:40z; the file is under active engine edit — grep the symbol) writes it unconditionally in the swarm block, under its own comment *"said out loud either way … an unpinned run that looks like a pinned one is the whole problem"*, and `git log -s` puts it in `b168490`, 2026-08-07 16:34 — fifteen days before the entry saying it does not exist. and the first is contradicted by the record. read out of git rather than re-run: the earlier artifact (`b26c2d4`, generated 2026-08-22t21:17:11z, 961 games / 95 diverged) carries `steering.team_store_pinned_to = "data\\\\team-pool-frozen"` and `steering.team_pool_teams = 8778`; the corrected one (`head`, 22:50:24z, 777 / 96) carries `"data/team-pool-frozen"` and the same 8778. `team_store` is the sole input to `swarm.buildswarm(..., { storedir })`, and `data/team-pool-frozen/` is a 2026-08-12 snapshot whose `games.bo3.jsonl` is 109,006,606 bytes against the live store's 167,972,026 — a live pool cannot yield the frozen pool's team count, so both runs read the frozen pool. what actually differs is `team_pool_picked` (1,968 against 1,597) and therefore `team_pool_digest` (`0d103fb9fa87` against `b2b61ec40281`), and `buildswarm` is asked for `max(games * 2, 18)` teams — i.e. the two runs requested different sample sizes. and the requested count is recoverable from the record, though neither artifact stores it. there is no `games_requested`, no argv and no flag block in either file — the same gap this row is about, one level up. but `buildswarm` computes `per = max(1, floor(max(games * 2, 18) / cfg.length))`, both runs carry 9 configs, and both publish `picked` per config: seven of the nine sit exactly on the cap, at 266 for `b26c2d4` and 213 for `head`. inverting that puts `--games` in [1197, 1201] for the earlier run and [959, 962] for the later one — so the two runs asked for materially different sizes, roughly 1200 against roughly 960, and 1200 and 960 are the only round numbers in those intervals. `coverage_stop` is `null` in both and the source says that field is *"null on a fixed-count run"*, so both took an explicit count and neither was `--until-covered`. the driver clamps, and it clamps per config rather than to the whole pool — the picker is `for (i = 0; i < matching.length && picked.length < per; i += step)`, and the record shows `omit-protect` at 99/99 and `omit-priority` at 7/7 in both runs. identical starvation is a third independent sign that the two read the same pool. so neither run got the count it asked for: about 1200 requested against 961 played (80.1%), and about 960 against 777 (80.9%). the shortfall is per-config starvation inside the frozen pool, present in both runs and in the same proportion — it is not a live store. what remains unknown and is not guessed: which exact integer was passed, and why the second run asked for the smaller one. nothing in the record carries a command line, and nothing was re-run to find out. neither figure is withdrawn by this row and neither may be entered in a retraction registry on its account: 11.69% is a rate on 777 games and 9.7% is a rate on 961, both on the frozen pool — two samples, not a pinned one and an unpinned one. what this row disputes is the cause that was published beside them, and nothing else. the real defect is that nothing reads the field. the only reader of `team_store_pinned_to` anywhere under `engine/` or `tests/` is `engine/replay_one.js:240`, and it reads the dump artifact rather than this one; no gate, no provenance clause and no `status.js` line compares a published claim's asserted pool against the artifact's declared pool or its `team_pool_digest`. a receipt nobody presents is not a receipt — which is the true form of what 5.74.0 was reaching for, and it is why a wrong pin would still be invisible today. #288 is the general row (a corpus snapshot id beside the release id in every artifact that reads a game file) and stays open; this is the specific case where the id already exists and is unread. what would decide it: a provenance clause that fails when a published rate names a pool the artifact does not declare, plus one re-measure of the 961/777 gap at a single requested game count. instrument owed: a provenance clause that fails when a published rate names a pool the artifact’s own `steering.team_store_pinned_to` and `team_pool_digest` do not declare.

open.title: `tests/test-state-differential.js` WAS RED AND THEN GREEN ON THE SAME TREE IN ONE EVENING — OBSERVED 2026-08-22, CAUSE U
open.full: `tests/test-state-differential.js` was red and then green on the same tree in one evening — observed 2026-08-22, cause unknown, no mechanism claimed. two independent passes, hours apart, same evening. the first (`docs/_reports/2026-08-22-wrong-arm-callers.md`) recorded exit 1 on all three arms — `injected 86, 3 / 3 failures, exit 1/1/1`, arm-independent but for a pool-cache line — and printed the three clauses: *"the proof ran 1 plants and 42 are declared — cannot plant — the clean game's very first board already differs, so there is no agreeing board to plant into"*; *"no switch-in ever reordered showdown's `side.pokemon` in this sample, so part 3 tested nothing"*; *"no game in this sample held weather across two boundaries, so part 5 tested nothing"*. the second (`docs/_reports/2026-08-22-runner-blind-spot.md`) recorded it green, exit 0, in those words: *"same tree, same evening, different answer."* no mechanism is claimed and none is invented here. one candidate is on the record and is explicitly not this row's verdict: the first report observed of a neighbouring gate that its message *"varies between runs because the team pool is drawn live from the store"*, which ops appends to — and two of the three clauses above are fixture-reachability complaints that a moved pool could plausibly flip. the third is not a fixture complaint at all (*the clean game's very first board already differs*), so a single explanation is not even available. untested either way. why it is filed rather than fixed tonight: an engine agent was live in `engine/medicham2-browser.js` across both passes and `tests/run-all.js` is being edited now, so any verdict taken now describes a moving tree. per claude.md a red gate is fixed in the session that saw it or waived by will by name — which makes *"which of the two answers is the gate's"* the thing that has to be settled first, and it is not a status. a gate that answers twice is worse than one that answers red, because both answers are quotable and neither can be checked. what would decide it: three runs on a settled tree at one pinned release, `--team-store data/team-pool-frozen` and a pinned census, with all three verdicts recorded. if they still differ, the subject is the gate's own fixture search and not the engine. instrument owed: three runs of this gate on a settled tree at one pinned release, one pinned census and `--team-store data/team-pool-frozen`, with all three verdicts recorded.

open.title: `engine/register_reality.js --list` SAYS IT RUNS NOTHING AND IT STILL OVERWRITES THE VERDICT ARTIFACT, DESTROYING EVERY
open.full: `engine/register_reality.js --list` says it runs nothing and it still overwrites the verdict artifact, destroying every verdict in it — tripped and self-reported 2026-08-23 by measure. the file's own header advertises `node engine/register_reality.js --list # coverage only; runs nothing`, and that is true of the instruments — every row printed `--list: not run` and no gate executed. it is not true of the artifact. the run ends `wrote data/register-reality.json`, and it replaced the settled 2026-08-22t01:55:12.569z artifact — `marked: 31` rows over `distinct_commands_run: 22`, 0 stale rows, 2 premature close (`tests/probe_red_demo.js`, `engine/gate_offfield_target.js`) and 1 instrument unrunnable — with one carrying no verdicts at all: 271 insertions and 142 deletions against head. recovered only because the file is tracked. `git checkout -- data/register-reality.json` restored it byte for byte and the working tree is clean of it; nothing was lost. had it been untracked it would have been unrecoverable, which is this repository's standing rule about deletion arriving through a door labelled read-only. the blast radius is a gate, not a file. `opendefectclause` in `engine/quarantine.js` reads this artifact to decide which open register rows are backed by a red instrument; every row it cannot find a verdict for falls into `debt` and can no longer hold the gate shut. an artifact wiped to all-`not run` therefore makes the clause print *"no open row names an instrument that is red"* for exactly the reason that should have made it loudest — which is the same shape as the three-key mismatch (`rows`/`verdicts` against `results`, `command` against `cmd`, `exit` against `green`) that this very clause records having survived unnoticed until 2026-08-18. a wipe is quieter than that was, because the key names still match. filed by the agent that caused it, on a read of the header that was accurate and incomplete. what would decide the fix: `--list` and `--json` write nothing, or write to a separate path, and the write site is guarded rather than the mode documented. instrument owed: a self-test asserting that a coverage-only invocation leaves `data/register-reality.json` byte-identical, in the style of the `--selftest` already in that file

open.title: THE DERIVED RETRACTION REGISTRY MATCHES ON A ROUNDED VALUE, SO ONE RETRACTED FIGURE ACCUSED 52 DOCUMENT LINES THAT SAY A
open.full: the derived retraction registry matches on a rounded value, so one retracted figure accused 52 document lines that say a different number — measured 2026-08-23 by measure, and it is live at baseline today. `retractionviolations` in `engine/docs_scan.js` accepts a hit when `number(e.value.tofixed(f.dp)) === f.value`. that tolerance was built for a real case — a document writing `63%` for a retracted `63.2%` is restating it — and it has no bound, so `(9.7).tofixed(0)` is `"10"` and a retracted `9.7%` matches every bare `10%` in the repository. measured: when one register row caused `9.7%` to enter the registry, that single entry produced 56 violations, of which 52 were a bare `10%` — a 93% false-positive rate on one entry, across `docs/engine.md`, `docs/glossary.md`, `docs/literature-v2.md`, `docs/miltank.md`, `docs/abra-whitepaper.md` and `docs/card-review-2026-08-22.md`, hitting *"flare blitz's 10% burn"*, *"top 10% in singles"*, *"the 0-10% or 90-100% bin"* and *"~10% of its useful size"*. this is not about that one figure and it is not new — it is firing at baseline right now. with that entry removed the clause sits exactly at its baseline of 10 keys, and 12 of the 17 surviving raw violations are rounding collisions rather than exact matches: `docs/backlog.md:215` *"we produce the single most common set 48% of the time"* and `docs/archive/session-2026-08-02.md:113` *"sucker punch's 48% failure prices the missing opponent model"* are both accused of restating the retracted mirror figure 47.5%, and neither is about it. a second, independent half: `isdistinctive` admits any percent. it is `f => f.pct \|\| f.value >= 1000`, so a two-significant-figure percentage qualifies — and `docs/engine.md` carries the literal cell `\| into a bright powder holder (100 x 0.9 = 90) \| 10.3% \| 9.7% \|`, an accuracy, which any retracted `9.7%` rate would accuse forever. the registry's own header already makes this exact argument and then exempts percents from it: it records that a bare `17` once flagged ninety lines and concludes *"a registry that fires on every occurrence of a small integer is worse than no registry, because it is the thing people switch off."* a percent with two significant figures is a small integer wearing a unit. and the sharpest half: the extractor cannot tell a figure that is retracted from a figure named in a sentence about a retraction. rule 2 registers `<determiner> <number>` on any line containing `retract`, so a row whose finding is that a figure was not withdrawn is read as withdrawing it. that is what happened here: #367 states in terms that neither of its two rates is withdrawn, and the derivation entered one of them as retracted anyway. the row was reworded so it can only be read one way — which fixed the symptom and not this — and the baseline was deliberately not touched, because adding entries to `data/docs-currency-baseline.json` to quiet a false positive is the laundering that file's own rule forbids. this is #148 in a clause that is genuinely valuable when it fires correctly, which is what makes it worth fixing rather than loosening: the same derivation is what caught the deck's `63.2%` restated as fact after the white paper withdrew it in writing, and an over-firing gate is the one people learn to ignore. what would decide the fix is three cases and not a preferred implementation, because the shape decision is the open part: a retracted `63.2%` must still match a document writing `63%`; a retracted `9.7%` must not match a bare `10%`; a retracted `47.5%` must not match a sucker punch `48%` failure rate. the current rule satisfies only the first. instrument owed: a red demonstration pair per matching rule in `engine/docs_scan.js` on synthetic documents, in the style of the `equal`/`distinct` pairs the differential's own normaliser already carries, plus a distinctiveness floor for percents stated as a rule rather than as a magnitude

open.title: SHOWDOWN REFUSES A MOVE AND WE EXECUTE IT — 8 OF THE 47 NON-`event-missing` DIVERGENCES, EVERY MEMBER BOARD-MATERIAL, TH
open.full:
showdown refuses a move and we execute it — 8 of the 47 non-`event-missing` divergences, every member board-material, three sub-causes on one signature. filed 2026-08-23 by measure. read, never re-run, off `git show head:data/game-differential.json` (commit `192d917`): release `c66976713feb`, showdown `20ad99ffc9a5`, census pin `80e648f34d56`, team store pinned to `data/team-pool-frozen` (8,778 teams, 1,968 picked), 961 games / 95 diverged / 0 threw, generated 2026-08-23t02:40:37z. triage: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-remaining-56.md` (`ea26208`). the signature: the authority writes `\|-fail\|slot` and we write the move's effect, and in both sampled cases the authority's `\|move\|` line carries `\|\|[still]`. that pair — `this.battle.add('-fail', pokemon); this.battle.attrlastmove('[still]');` — is at `sim/battle-actions.ts:594-596`, the branch where `singleevent('try') && singleevent('preparehit') && runevent('preparehit')` returned an explicit `false`, and again at `:645-647` for an all-false `tryhit`, so the family narrows to those two gates without naming one of them. filed as one row with its sub-causes named, not as three rows: one signature, one place in the resolution order, and three rows would put three register entries on one fix.

(a) a stalling move that is not a shield never reaches the stall gate — 2 of 8, confirmed and source-cited. `unrelated event mismatch :: \|-fail\|p1b <> \|-singleturn\|p1b\|endure` and the same shape on `p2a`. `data/moves.ts:4816-4818` — `endure.onpreparehit(pokemon) { return !!this.queue.willact() && this.runevent('stallmove', pokemon); }` — is byte-identical to `protect`'s at `:13974-13976`; champions overrides `protect` (pp 5, `data/mods/champions/moves.ts:755`) and does not override `endure` at all. ours gates on the chooser's action kind rather than on the move being a stalling move — `it.a.kind==='protect'` — and `protectmoves` holds protect, detect, spikyshield, kingsshield, banefulbunker, burningbulwark, silktrap and maxguard, with endure absent from it, so both the `willact()` scan and the stall counter are skipped. *(both engine sites were verified at `engine/medicham2-browser.js:14901` and `:3891` by the coordinator on 2026-08-23 and are deliberately not re-read in this row: that file is under active engine edit tonight, so grep the symbols `protectmoves` and `_shieldpending`, never these line numbers.)* #232 closed on a family of six sharing one counter — endure among them — and five of the six reach the gate; #178 removed endure from `shieldsuser` for the right reason (it blocks nothing) and this gate is keyed on the same road. a fix for (a) is sitting uncommitted and unmeasured in the working tree from an agent that was stopped mid-task, so this sub-cause is not untouched — and nothing has yet measured whether that edit closes it or moves the divergence elsewhere.

(b) a trapping move re-applied to an already-trapped body — 2 of 8, mechanism confirmed from the format, instance a hypothesis. `\|-fail\|p2a <> \|-activate\|p1a\|trapped` and `\|-fail\|p1b <> \|-activate\|p2a\|trapped`. `meanlook` and `block` are both `onhit(target, source, move) { return target.addvolatile("trapped", source, move, "trapper"); }`, and `addvolatile` returns false on a repeat, so the second use fails; the `trapped` condition's `onstart(target) { this.add("-activate", target, "trapped"); }` is exactly the line we emit, so our announcement is right and the refusal is what is missing. this engine implements the repeat refusal per volatile (`applyattract`'s own comment: *"addvolatile refuses a repeat: no onrestart"*), never globally. a coverage-seeking driver re-clicks, which is why it surfaces here at all.

(c) four refusals that cannot be attributed at all — 4 of 8, unattributable by construction rather than unknown-cause. `\|-fail\|p2b <> \|-supereffective\|p1b\|1`, `\|-fail\|p2a <> \|-resisted\|p1a\|1`, `\|-fail\|p1a <> \|-damage\|p2a\|0 fnt`, `\|-fail\|p2b <> \|-damage\|p1a\|h/h`. all four carry `mentions: []` and `max_uses: undefined`, and none is among the 60 sampled `first_divergences`, so the file holds no species, no move and no preceding context for any of them. two damage a body the authority never damaged, one of those to a faint. the reason is the instrument's dump cap, filed as #375 — these do not become workable by thinking harder about them, and calling them unknown-cause would misname whose problem they are. what would decide (a) and (b): two bodies, one switches and the other clicks endure with nothing move-like left in the queue — assert `-fail` and no `-singleturn`, then endure on consecutive turns and assert the stall roll is consumed; and mean look twice into the same body — assert the second is `-fail` with no second `-activate`, with the same two clicks separated by a switch-out as the control that must succeed. endure is 5 corpus clicks; the fix is the keying, not the move.

open.title: A TARGET THE AUTHORITY HAD ALREADY REMOVED FROM ITS ARRAY WAS STILL DRAGGED BY THE DAMAGING PHAZE, SO A DIFFERENT BODY S
open.full: a target the authority had already removed from its array was still dragged by the damaging phaze, so a different body stood in the slot for the rest of the game — landed 2026-08-23 by engine, registered 2026-08-23 by measure. board-material. the authority zeroes its `targets` array all the way down (`sim/battle-actions.ts:1063` a substitute-eaten hit becomes `null`, `:1080` a `damage[i] === false` becomes `false`, `:1353` the forceswitch walk skips both); this engine’s damaging `forcesswitch` loop walked `targets` with only the protect filter applied. measured on the staged board before a byte moved: dragon tail into a pure-fairy clefable — both engines write `-immune`, and this one then wrote `\|drag\|p2a: weavile`. from that turn on the slot held a different species, at different hp, with different types and a different ability, and the refused body had lost its calm mind boosts to a switch-out that never happened (`clefable.boosts.spa/spd` 0 / 0 here against 1 / 1 on the authority). the fix is class-shaped and the probe is not, and that is said rather than glossed: the loop now walks the survivor set the step driver itself walks (`if (r.out) continue`), and `r.out` is written at six sites — type immunity, move-class immunity, invulnerability, an absorbing ability, the accuracy miss, and the substitute — so a seventh refusal added later is honoured with no edit here; the probe stages the type-immunity member only. new counter `medseen.forcedswitchtargetremoved`, because a guard that fires silently and a guard nothing reached look identical from outside. red then green with the control cleared on the same click at a non-immune target. what is owed is the pool reading: an immune or missed damaging phaze is uncommon, so the expectation stated before any run is that the lab moves and the pinned pool may not, and no usage figure is asserted. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-phaze-empty-bench.md` §5

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: "WHAT DOES THIS EXIT CODE MEAN" IS DECIDED IN TWO FILES, AND THE OPEN-DEFECT CLAUSE NOW SAYS SOMETHING FALSE ABOUT THE R
open.full: "what does this exit code mean" is decided in two files, and the open-defect clause now says something false about the rows it buckets — measured 2026-08-23 by measure, not fixed. `tests/run-all.js` has always treated exit 2 as *"i could not run, not i failed"* for every script it runs, generically and in those words; `engine/register_reality.js` treated the same code as a red verdict until 2026-08-23 (#379). two files deciding one fact, disagreeing, both continuing to work — and they still each own a copy. three things are owed and none was done, each for a stated reason. (1) `opendefectclause` prints *"open row(s) name an instrument that would not run"* over a bucket that now also holds instruments which ran and declared cannot-answer: the bucket is right and the sentence is false. (2) an open row whose instrument refused probably ought to make the clause `ok: false, cannot_answer: true`, exactly as `orderprobeclause` already does in the same file on the same reasoning — a clause that cannot be computed fails — so the gate stays shut for the honest reason rather than on a fictitious red; as it stands such a row moves to `unrunnable` and stops holding the clause at all. (3) the classifier should be one implementation both callers use. why not now: (1) and (2) are edits to `engine/quarantine.js`, which the pass that found this was forbidden to run, and an unverified edit to the file that computes the medicham gate is worse than the wording; (3) needs either an edit to `tests/run-all.js` (engine was live in `tests/`) or making `engine/register_reality.js` requirable, which today would write its artifact on require. note for whoever takes (3): `run-all.js` fails on exit 3 and `gate_fail_and_silent.js` uses exit 3 for regression — that stays red only because the gate now declares `abra-exit 3 verdict-red`. also unreached and left alone: `register_reality.js`’s `if (row.closed && !green)` is a real `!green` collapse, currently shadowed by the `green === null` branch above it. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-cannot-answer-vs-red.md`

open.title: THE REGISTER’S EVIDENCE BASE, MEASURED: FIVE ROWS CARRY A `VERIFIED BY` NO RUNNER CAN LAUNCH, AND THIRTY-FIVE OPEN ROWS
open.full: the register’s evidence base, measured: five rows carry a `verified by` no runner can launch, and thirty-five open rows assert breakage with nothing at all deciding them — measured 2026-08-23 by measure. derived over `docs/roadmap.md` with `quarantine.roadmaprowisclosed` and `roadmaprowsaysbroken`, the one closed-detector, on the register as it stood after this pass’s own edits. (1) five markers are instructions to a human wearing an instrument’s clothes. `engine/register_reality.js`’s `safe` pattern accepts only `node <engine|tests|build>/<file>.js [--flags]`, deliberately, so that no marker can be shell-executed. #316, #318, #319, #320 and #322 all carry `showdown_path=... node tests/...` with a literal ellipsis and, on #316, a literal `<id>`; every one files as instrument unrunnable, which is neither agreement nor evidence. two of the five are open and assert breakage (#318, #319), so they hold a gate shut on a claim no process has checked since it was typed. the repair is a decision, not a patch: either the runner learns to supply `showdown_path` from the environment it already has (it is set for every other instrument in the chain) and to expand `<id>` from `data/engine-release.json`, or these rows carry `instrument owed` instead and stop presenting a command as a verdict. the first is better and it must not be done by relaxing `safe` into a shell, which is the hazard that pattern exists to prevent. (2) thirty-five open rows assert breakage, hold the open-defect clause shut, and carry neither a `verified by` nor an `instrument owed`. of 49 open rows asserting breakage, 6 are marked and 8 declare a debt; the remaining 35 are prose that gates the project. that is not an accusation that they are wrong — it is the statement that nothing can tell. `data/register-reality.json` reaches 35 rows in total out of 295 register rows, so 88% of the register has never been checked against the world by anything but a reader. instrument owed: a runner that can launch an instrument needing `showdown_path`, and a coverage figure — marked rows over open-asserting-breakage rows — printed on every register-reality run so it can be ratcheted upward rather than rediscovered

open.title: `engine/move_result_state.js` COMPARES THE ONE PIECE OF STATE THAT DECIDED TWO SILENT DEFECTS, AND IT IS READ BY ONE PRO
open.full: `engine/move_result_state.js` compares the one piece of state that decided two silent defects, and it is read by one probe and by nothing at scale — built 2026-08-23 by engine, registered by measure. it reads `movethisturnresult` / `movelastturnresult` off the authority and `_mvres` / `_mvreslast` off medicham2 at the same turn boundary `engine/board_state.js` already uses, keeps the four values apart (`true` / `false` / `null` / `undefined`) rather than collapsing them — three of the field’s four consumers test `=== false` but `data/abilities.ts:5176` tests `!== undefined`, so a null/undefined collapse would silence exactly that one — and encodes anything outside the four as `unexpected(...)`. `--selftest` is 18 clauses driven through the shipping functions. on its first run it caught two state defects nothing in this repository could see, on arms whose boards were identical and one of whose protocol was byte-identical, both deciding stomping tantrum’s base power the following turn (#377). it is not wired into `engine/board_state.js`, deliberately: promoting it to a compared board field changes what every whole-game run counts, and the pass that built it could not size that. the cost of leaving it is the absence it was built to end, one level up — every whole-game divergence triaged as narration-only today is triaged without this field being compared, and the two defects above are the receipt that a byte-identical protocol proves nothing about it. instrument owed: either the field promoted into `engine/board_state.js`, or a declared `not_compared` entry there naming this row as its reason, plus a re-baselined whole-game count measured under the promotion rather than compared across it. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-announce-failure-class.md` §3

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: ABOUT SEVENTY OF THIS ENGINE’S ~84 `mvFail` SITES WRITE A BARE `-fail` WHERE THE AUTHORITY NEVER WRITES ONE, AND THE WHO
open.full: about seventy of this engine’s ~84 `mvfail` sites write a bare `-fail` where the authority never writes one, and the whole-game differential cannot count it by construction — measured 2026-08-23 by engine, no verdict, filed by measure so it is not re-discovered. derived rather than noticed: `grep "'-fail'" sim/battle-actions.ts` returns exactly twelve sites and every one pairs the `-fail` with an `attrlastmove` — `[still]` in ten, `[notarget]` in two — so there is no site anywhere in the authority that writes a bare `-fail` with the `\|move\|` line left intact. here `mvfail(mon)` is `{ mon._mvres = false; tr.fail(mon); }` with no `attrstill`, and about 70 of its call sites do not wrap it in one (11 do). it is invisible to the instrument and the instrument is right: `engine/game_differential.js`’s `move-target-field` equivalence is `f => (f[1] === 'move' ? f.slice(0, 4) : f)`, which drops field 4 and everything after it, including `[still]`. that rule is argued at length in that file (showdown names one nominal target plus `[spread]`, we name our own user) and it is not a silencer being abused — but the consequence is that this asymmetry has no instrument counting it and no known cost. it is not claimed harmless. it is claimed unmeasured, and the reason it is written down is that it looks like a seventy-site defect from outside and an evening was nearly spent on it. also why `tests/probe_fail_and_silent.js` reads 6 staged / 0 parted on the live tree: its field-repeat family genuinely agrees. what would decide it: a comparison that keeps field 4 for the `[still]` token alone, which is a measure decision about what the differential counts and not an engine change. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-announce-failure-class.md` §2b
