open.full: big root’s drain multiplier rounds differently from the authority and the error compounds across turns — measured 2026-08-23 by measure from the roster, filed for engine. `data/roster.items.json`, release `c36782953dee`, generated 2026-08-23t06:05:47z: `bigroot` is one of the item stage’s two fired-and-boards-differ rows, and every parted leaf is the healer’s hp — `kangaskhan party.hp showdown 693 ours 692` at turn 2, then 714 against 712 at turn 3. the gap grows, which is the interesting half: one hp, then two, so it is a per-tick rounding rule rather than a one-off. read: `data/items.ts:488-494` — the item is `ontryhealpriority: 1` with `ontryheal(damage, target, source, effect)` returning `this.chainmodify([5324, 4096])`, i.e. the authority applies 5324/4096 through its chained-modifier rounding rather than a plain multiply-and-floor. `data/mods/champions/items.ts` carries no `bigroot` key, so champions does not override it. and the effect list is five, not one — `['drain', 'leechseed', 'ingrain', 'aquaring', 'strengthsap']` at `:490` — so a fix aimed at drain alone closes one of five doors. adjacent but not the same as #339, which is the spread drain healing once over a summed total where the authority rounds per target; this is the multiplier’s own rounding and the two can be wrong independently. what would decide it: one staged big root drain whose pre-multiplier heal is chosen so that 5324/4096 and 1.3 round apart, asserted to the point against the authority, with a no-big-root control that must agree before and after; and the same body run across the other four heal sources so the class is not closed on one of them

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE ONE TOOL BUILT TO PRINT WHAT THE REGISTER CANNOT SEE ABOUT ITSELF IS FED BY A SINGLE ARTIFACT THAT IS 11.4 DAYS OLD,
open.full: the one tool built to print what the register cannot see about itself is fed by a single artifact that is 11.4 days old, so it prints `unregistered: 0` and that zero carries no information — measured 2026-08-23 by measure. `engine/open_work.js`’s whole justification is that *a register cannot audit itself*, and its unregistered half is the stronger of its two signals because it is measured rather than filed. run 2026-08-23: `measured_disagreements: 0, unregistered: 0`. the reason is in its own output — the only instrument it reads is `data/interaction-matrix.json`, generated 2026-08-11t22:00:06z, and it prints the warning itself: *"11.4 days old. anything read out of it describes the engine of that day, not this one."* it is doing exactly what it was built to do and the answer is still empty, which is worse than a red: a zero from a blind instrument reads identically to a zero from a clear one. measured against it the same day, the reports in `docs/_reports/` filed nine defects with no register row on 2026-08-22 and at least four more on 2026-08-23 (#377, #378, #382, #383 among them), every one of which unregistered reported as zero. the fix is not to regenerate the matrix — that makes one number current and leaves the tool reading one instrument. it is that unregistered must read the artifacts that actually measure this engine today: `data/game-differential.json`’s causes, the three `data/roster.*.json` stages, and `data/all-mechanics-fire.json`, each matched against the register by subject and each stamped with its own age. instrument owed: those four sources wired into `open_work.js`’s measured half, and a refusal — not a zero — when every source it reads is older than the engine

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: THE WHOLE-GAME HEADLINE SILENTLY CHANGED QUANTITY IN AUGUST AND NOTHING LABELS WHICH ONE IT IS, SO THE REGISTER’S OWN TR
open.full: the whole-game headline silently changed quantity in august and nothing labels which one it is, so the register’s own trend line compares two different measurements — measured 2026-08-23 by measure. `wholegameclause` published a raw rate (`diverged / games`) until the declared-divergence exemption landed 2026-08-18, and has published an undeclared rate (`(diverged - declared - decision_cleared) / games`) since. both are correct and neither is named in the sentence it prints: the string is `<n> of <games> = <pct>% diverge`, with the raw figure appearing only inside a parenthetical and only when something was subtracted. #218 therefore carries 39.6% (raw, 2026-08-12), 69.9% (undeclared, 2026-08-18) and 8.0% (undeclared, 2026-08-23) in one cell as if they were one series, and the raw-to-raw pair — 39.6% against 8.5% — has to be reconstructed by hand from a field the sentence does not print. and the artifact offers three more numbers the headline is not. the same run carries `arms[].diverged` at middle 82, top-tie-first 68 and bottom-tie-first 77 of 961; the headline reads 77 because 82 minus 5 declared is 77. a coordinator read that collision as the gate quoting a corner by omission and ordered a correction and a defect row on the strength of it. refuted by driving the shipping function on perturbed copies of the artifact: the headline is invariant to both arm figures and moves only with the top-level `diverged` and with the declared set (#218). no arm-selection defect exists and this row is not one — it is registered because the near-miss cost a correction cycle, and because the same collision will recur every time raw minus declared lands on one of the other two arms. what would fix it: the clause names its quantity in the sentence (`undeclared`), prints the raw rate beside it unconditionally rather than only when something was subtracted, and prints the arm it describes by id; and the artifact carries the published headline as its own field so a reader never has to reconstruct which of five numbers the gate meant. instrument owed: an assertion that the published headline string names its quantity and its arm, in the style of the composition-vs-headline check #292 already added to this clause

open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A RATCHET THAT REPUBLISHES ITS OWN ARTIFACT ON A RED RUN LAUNDERS THE REGRESSION IT JUST CAUGHT — `tests/test-unmodelled
open.full: a ratchet that republishes its own artifact on a red run launders the regression it just caught — `tests/test-unmodelled-clicks.js`, found 2026-08-23 by measure while sweeping the class behind #390. at `head` the file's `fs.writefilesync(out, …)` sits outside every conditional and carries `generated: new date().toisostring()`, so `data/unmodelled-clicks.json` is rewritten on every invocation including a failing one. the demonstration, recorded in the fixing agent's own header: remove `healbell` from the baseline so the live set appears to have grown — run 1 fails `the set did not grow … new: healbell`, exit 1, and writes the grown set; run 2, the run a person naturally does after seeing red, reads `3 -> 3`, exit 0, and `healbell` is baseline forever. nothing else changed between the two runs. this is claude.md's founding failure inside the instrument rather than the engine — a capability absent and everything reporting success — and it is the same shape as the torn read that produced `344 attributed games` where the settled artifact had 450. it is the only sibling the class sweep found: of the six `tests/test-*.js` that write into `data/` with no flag, four are generators and `test-json-nan-guard` writes only when its count falls. not closed here, deliberately. a green-only write is in the working tree, written by another agent tonight, uncommitted, and i did not run it — the file is on this brief's do-not-touch list. instrument owed: the two-run demonstration above, re-run against the fix, with the artifact hash shown identical across the red run the class is wider than this file, and a gate for it was built the same night. `tests/test-red-run-writes.js` (another agent, 2026-08-23) asserts the property structurally rather than enumerating known-bad files — three bugs in this repository have come from a ratchet whose detector was a list — and its own header reports five more instances found by reading, one of which is `tests/test-game-diff.js` publishing its artifact after its comparator had failed its own planted-divergence proof: an instrument declaring itself trustworthy immediately after failing the test of its trustworthiness. it also records that four instruments already carried an ad-hoc write-detecting regex (`test-rollout-gates`, `test-site-data-fresh`, `test-publish-guard`, `test-register-reality-readonly`) — the machinery was present four times and enforced nowhere. no `verified by` marker is placed yet: that file is untracked at filing time and measure has not run it; the marker belongs on this row the moment it is committed and has been run once. the gate landed and is committed; the row stays open because measure has not verified it and the floor still names a launderer — 2026-08-24. `tests/test-unmodelled-clicks.js` now carries a green-only write (`write_policy: "written only by a run that passed (or by an explicit --accept)"`) and is committed. four more instances were confirmed one at a time and fixed — `test-tag-consumed.js` (laundering demonstrated on the verbatim ratchet logic: `regressed (was live)` → `still dead` on the second run), `test-game-diff.js` (now exits at the planted-divergence proof, before a game is played; its header had claimed this for months and it was false), `test-forme-assert.js` and `test-switch-back-renamed.js`. `tests/test-red-run-writes.js` asserts the property — a column-0 `data/` write with a later failure signal — over 387 files rather than enumerating known-bad ones, proves its own detector against 2 plants and 3 controls every run, and was shown red on a planted new offender. the enumeration handed over was itself wrong in the direction that matters: it called `tests/test-mechanics.js` the milder class and it is the worst instance in the tree — a full self-baselining ratchet on `data/mechanics-census.json`, the artifact that steers `all_mechanics_fire.js`, that `quarantine.js` reads for a medicham gate clause, and that the whole-game differential pins as `steering.input_digest`. it was fixed separately (the census floor may fall and may never rise, demonstrated two-run before and after) but `tests/test-mechanics.js` is still inside `accepted` in `tests/test-red-run-writes.js` with tier `launders`, and the floor may only shrink by somebody removing it. that removal, plus one measure run of the gate, is what closes this row. not closed on another agent’s report. accounts: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-red-run-writes.md`, `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-red-run-writes-class.md`, `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-census-launders.md`. verified by: `node tests/test-red-run-writes.js`

gengar` 69-82 (ours 90-106, x1.30 sheer force), `kangaskhanmega fakeout -> pinsir` 37-45 (ours 44-55, the bonded packet), `gyaradosmega earthquake -> rotomwash` 0-0 (ours 136-160, levitate broken by with an `onmodifymove` / `onpreparehit` / `onmodifypriority` handler; across all legal abilities there are 22 such carriers. a related structural blindness, stated so it is not mistaken for agreement: the harness never runs `onpreparehit` either, so protean rows agree for the wrong reason — a green row that asks nothing. instrument owed: run `modifymove` in the harness (or exclude these carriers from the comparison and say so in the artifact), then re-measure at seed 20260804

open.title: A CASTFORM-SNOWY BODY IS NEVER RECONCILED TO AN EMPTY SKY, AND WHETHER THAT IS THE HARNESS OR THE ENGINE RESTS ON A READ

`mc.mons` holds all four today. the blocker named in the comment is gone and the premise should stop being cited. which scoreboard, declared before the run: castform is 0.08% of teams (28 of 36,696), so expect the pinned pool not to move — 39% of the published damage residual for 0.08% of the metagame. instrument owed: the init probe above

open.title: THE DAMAGE DIFFERENTIAL PUBLISHES 40 ROWS OF HOWEVER MANY IT FOUND, SO A TAIL OF 16 HAD TO BE RECONSTRUCTED BY HAND BEFO
open.full: the damage differential publishes 40 rows of however many it found, so a tail of 16 had to be reconstructed by hand before anyone could group it — measured 2026-08-23 by measure. `tests/test-engine-diff.js:954` writes `worst: bad.slice(0, 40)` over a list sorted by move usage descending, and every `arms` list is capped at 40 the same way (`:975`) — the union of all sixteen arm lists is the same 40 triples as the midpoint's, so the arms do not recover the tail either. at `disagreed: 56` that hid 16 rows, all with move `uses` <= 1507, and recovering them required replaying the harness's lcg (seed 20260804, whose only in-loop consumer is `pick`) and re-deriving each family by the harness's own rules — a reconstruction that reproduced 39 of the 40 published rows and is therefore near-exact rather than exact. the cost was not academic: the hidden 16 contained 8 of the 15 mimikyu-busted rows (#392) and 6 of the 11 sheer force rows, so the artifact under-reported the engine defect's size by more than half. today's re-run (`disagreed: 41`) hides only 1, so the cap is currently almost harmless — which is exactly when it is cheapest to raise. what would fix it: raise or remove the cap, or publish a family tally beside the truncated list so the count is readable without a replay. individual rows can already be confirmed one at a time with `--case att,move,def` (`:762`), and the run is deterministic, so nothing is lost — only hidden. instrument owed: the cap raised, or a per-family count written into the artifact

open.title: THE WHOLE-GAME 82 GROUP INTO 31 MECHANISMS, AND NO MEASUREMENT IN THAT RUN SAYS WHETHER ANY OF THEM IS BOARD-MATERIAL —
open.full: the whole-game 82 group into 31 mechanisms, and no measurement in that run says whether any of them is board-material — measured 2026-08-23 by measure, index row. source: `data/game-differential.json`, release `c36782953dee`, census `8c778268919e` `matches_live: true`, pool `data\team-pool-frozen` digest `0d103fb9fa87`, generated 2026-08-23t06:10:58z — the run was pinned exactly as claimed. the arm matters and the headline is not the primary one: `arms` read middle 82 (`pins.primary`), top-tie-first 68, bottom-tie-first 77, and the commit body's `77 of 961 = 8.0%` is the bottom corner minus nothing; the primary arm is 82 of 961 = 8.5%, or 8.34% over the 959 usable once the 2 mid-void games are removed, which is the only rate the artifact itself computes (see #387 for why the quantity is unlabelled). this row groups the middle arm's 82, because `classes[].causes[]` is the middle arm's table and nothing else in the artifact is broken out per arm at cause level. the single most important fact here: `state_mode: false`, `end_state_mode: false`, `state: null`, `end_state: null` — this was a protocol run, no board was compared at any turn boundary and no end board was compared, so by will's standing rule (*a divergence is narration-only when something measured it as narration-only*) the board-material split cannot be read off it at all, and `data/state-ladder.json` may not be substituted (16 days old, no `engine_release`, and it predates the artifact's own declared `baseline_reset`). until `node engine/game_differential.js --games 961 --end-state --release c36782953dee --team-store data/team-pool-frozen --write` runs, "board-material zero" has no denominator — and even a clean end-state run does not clear the `-fail` family, which needs `engine/move_result_state.js` (#382) because `board_state.js` compares no move-result field. coverage, honestly: 82 of 82 attributed at cause-string level; 64 of 82 (78%) backed by evidence (61 cards in `first_divergences`, +2 mega `detailschange`, +2 `order_probe`); 18 read from the cause string alone and every claim about those is inferred. the two rows most worth carding are `\|-fail\| <> \|-damage\|…0fnt` — if the shape holds, a move the authority failed is killing something here, which would be the most serious single finding in the group; they are not carded and it is not claimed (see #371, #383). the groups, with counts of 82: substitute-vs-intimidate 1 (fixed, #388); `-fail` announce 7 (#371, #383); eager `\|faint\|` 6 +1 perish variant (#331); weather-upkeep missing 5 (#352 holds the derived `!field.wsup` gate defect and explicitly does not claim to explain these five); zero-magnitude boost at the +/-6 cap 5 (#289 is closed and does not cover these — see #398); supreme overlord `fallenundefined` 5 (#321); simultaneous switch order 5 (#353); spread drain interleave 4, every instance matcha gotcha (#339); ability-activate announce 3 (telepathy #360, toxic debris #374); wrong body targeted 3 (#335); two-side residual order 2 (#355); silent `-end` of a real volatile 2 (#345); forecast absent 2 and symbiosis / sand spit / protean / regenerator / psychic terrain 1 each (#397); semi-invulnerable turn not respected 2 (#400); spread flinch 2 (#335); exact speed ties 2 (this reading is withdrawn 2026-08-24 — it is a real turn-order defect: `order_probe` measured `speed_gap: 0`, `same_priority: true`, and both tie devices are pinned in this harness, so a tie must resolve identically and these do not — #376); berry vs self-damage 2 (#372); mega `detailschange` order 2 (#373); future sight damage off by 1-2 hp 2 (#401); substitute hp 1 (#358); copycat 1; spurious second `-activate … sitrusberry` 1; moody 8 (instrument, #351); off-field body 1 (already declared, `declared_gaps.trace_body_off_field`). the cross-references above were matched by subject and are not a row-by-row audit — 342 register rows were not individually adjudicated against 31 mechanisms tonight, and that gap is exactly what #386 says `open_work.js` must learn to do. what the sampling structurally leaves out: the middle arm stops at the first divergent line in 81 of 82 games, so these are the 31 mechanisms that fire earliest, not the 31 that exist; `forced_switch_unmirrorable: 4` means up to 4 games carry an instrument-manufactured constraint (none surfaced as a cause, but the switch-ordering group is the one exposed to it, #365); and 2 games are void with `outrage` among the unshared addresses, which is a live risk to the outrage retargeting row specifically. instrument owed: the `--end-state` run above, before any fixing effort is ranked superseded in part 2026-08-24, and the index is not rewritten because it is a dated measurement. read the register, not this list, for anything below. seven of the mechanisms counted above are now closed — regenerator, forecast and symbiosis (#397), the substitute break (#358, and it was narration, not the "substitute hp" this list calls it), future sight (#401, and the mechanism was the span-vs-index draw and not the snapshot), the semi-invulnerable status move (half of #400) and the zero-magnitude boost (#398). and one entry was wrong in the direction that matters: the exact speed ties were listed here as not a defect, which is corrected above — that reading would have subtracted a live turn-order defect

open.title: SIX SWITCH-IN / ON-HIT EFFECTS DO NOT FIRE AT ALL IN A REAL GAME, EVERY ONE BOARD-MATERIAL BY STRUCTURE, AND EVERY ONE A
open.full: six switch-in / on-hit effects do not fire at all in a real game, every one board-material by structure, and every one already carrying a populated tag row — 7 of the whole-game 82, filed 2026-08-23 by measure. read off `data/game-differential.json` (release `c36782953dee`, 2026-08-23t06:10:58z); none of the six has a champions override, so the mainline handler is the authority. forecast (2 games, 15 uses): the authority writes `-formechange … castform-rainy \|[msg]\|[from] ability: forecast` in rain and the forme carries a different type — board-material without argument; the tag `formefollowsweather` already holds the full `byweather` / `typesbyweather` map, and #204 landed the missing bodies (see also #394). regenerator (1 game, 1,855 uses — the highest here): `-heal … 170/170 \|[from] ability: regenerator\|[silent]` on switch-out; `[silent]` but hp-bearing, which is exactly why a blanket "`[silent]` is narration" normalisation rule must never be written. psychic terrain (1 game): the authority blocks a prankster-boosted thunder wave into a grounded annihilape and we let the paralysis land — a status that should not exist. symbiosis (1, 69 uses): neither the `-activate` nor the item transfer happens; tag `passesitemtoally` (see #175). sand spit (1, 34 uses): the weather is not set; tag `punishesattacker` with `setsweather: "sandstorm"` already populated (see #329). protean (1, 571 uses): the type does not change on a meowscarada; tag `typebecomesmovetype` with `onceperswitchin: true` (see #356, which is the mega-forme half of the same subject and is marked under re-derivation). so the work is wiring, not modelling — six independent probes, six populated tag rows. pick up regenerator first on usage and psychic terrain first on consequence. a caveat the filer owes: `grep -ci` on `medicham2-browser.js` returns 0 for `sandspit` and non-zero for four of the others — that is weak evidence and is labelled as such, because this engine matches on tag shape and not on names, precisely so a new ability is picked up without editing it. a zero name-count is a hint, not a finding. instrument owed: a census probe per member, each red before the wire, each with the control arm named narrowed 2026-08-23 — three of the six are closed and the group’s wording was wrong for one of them. regenerator: closed — and *"does not fire at all"* was never true of it. the heal fired and only the announcement was absent, removed on purpose in #223 on a read of mainline where `data/mods/champions/abilities.ts:77-84` adds the line. probed by `tests/probe_regenerator_line.js` (red 2 / green 0). forecast: closed — the field-driven forme now follows a sky that was already there when the body arrived; the sync had two moments and arriving was not one of them. 2 board-material games. symbiosis: closed — the handler is `onallyafteruseitem` and `pokemon#useitem` raises `afteruseitem`, so every item spend is a trigger; this engine had hung it on `consumeberry`, its one berry door, and had declared the shortfall by name in `medfails.symbiosisnonberrysites`. 1 board-material game (a white herb). all three verified by the cause diff on release `3e00ea2575a9`, where those exact causes leave `by_cause` and nothing else moves by a single game. accounts: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-mechanics-by-reach.md`, `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-board-material-remainder.md`. three remain and the row stays open on them: psychic terrain (a prankster-boosted thunder wave lands a paralysis the authority blocks — first on consequence), sand spit (the weather is not set) and protean (the type does not change; see #356 for the mega-forme half). instrument owed: a census probe per remaining member, each red before the wire, each with its control arm named

open.title: THE ONE TOOL THAT RENDERS DIVERGENCE CARDS FOR A HUMAN READS A TWO-DAY-OLD DUMP AND SAYS SO NOWHERE ON THE PAGE — MEASUR
open.full: the one tool that renders divergence cards for a human reads a two-day-old dump and says so nowhere on the page — measured 2026-08-23 by measure. `engine/divergence_cards.js` reads `data/divergence-turns.json`, which is stamped 2026-08-22t03:05:53z, release `6a05dd9ad60d`, `of_diverged: 378`, arms `{middle:133, top-tie-first:120, bottom-tie-first:125}` — the 39.6%-era run. the current differential is release `c36782953dee` at 2026-08-23t06:10z with middle 82. running the tool today produces a readable, well-formed html page of the wrong run with no staleness warning anywhere on it; its causes include `-unboost: a different body` and an `ordering` case involving `[from]drought` / `hospitality`, neither of which is in today's 82. this is precisely the shape claude.md warns about — a rendering that computes nothing, over a file nobody regenerated, indistinguishable from a fresh result — and it is the same class as #386 (a tool reporting confidently off one aged input) and the web rule that a rendered figure must trace to an artifact or read not measured. will's own card review runs through this page, so a stale render is not cosmetic: it sends a human reading cards at mechanisms that no longer diverge. why it goes stale silently: the dump is only written alongside `--write` and only when `--dump-games` is given a count, so an ordinary differential run leaves it untouched while updating everything around it. what would fix it: the renderer refuses — or banners — when the dump's `engine_release` differs from `data/game-differential.json`'s, and the next differential run is given `--dump-games 200 --dump-out data/divergence-turns.json --write`. instrument owed: that release comparison, at the top of the page and in the exit code

open.title: A SEMI-INVULNERABLE BODY IS HIT ANYWAY, AND A CLOSED ROW SITS OVER IT — 2 OF THE WHOLE-GAME 82, BOARD-MATERIAL BY STRUCT
open.full: a semi-invulnerable body is hit anyway, and a closed row sits over it — 2 of the whole-game 82, board-material by structure, filed 2026-08-23 by measure. `data/game-differential.json` (release `c36782953dee`, 2026-08-23t06:10:58z) carries two: decorate into a dragapult in the phantom force turn — the authority writes `-miss` and we write `-boost atk 2`, so a stat exists on the board here that does not exist there — and a locked phantom force that announces and deals nothing. #123 is closed and does not cover these: it settled the semi-invulnerability exception list (which moves reach an invulnerable body anyway), not whether the invulnerable turn is respected by an ordinary move or whether the second turn of the lock resolves. anyone grepping the register for semi-invulnerability lands on a row marked closed, which is why this is filed separately. phantom force is 698 uses. likely sites: the invulnerability check on the target, and the locked-move second turn. no verdict on the mechanism — both are read from cause strings plus their cards, and neither has been staged. instrument owed: a staged pair — decorate into a body in the phantom force turn (control: the same decorate into the same body out of it), and a two-turn phantom force asserting damage on turn 2 half closed 2026-08-23 by engine; the row stays open on its second member. (a) closed — a status move now misses a semi-invulnerable body. `hitstepinvulnerabilityevent` is step zero of `tryspreadmovehit` (`sim/battle-actions.ts:556, 621`) and that path is taken by every move; this engine implemented it as `_stepinvuln` inside the attack branch only, so roughly forty non-attack kinds resolved in branches below it. staged before a line changed, decorate / charm / will-o-wisp / taunt into a mid-phantom-force dragapult were byte-identical across the knob on every member — which is what an unwired gate looks like. one gate at the common commit site, `a.kind === 'attack'` deliberately skipped so nothing about the damaging path moves, with the authority’s own three exemptions (helping hand, a poison-type’s toxic, `guaranteedagainst`) as probe arms that must not miss. both events emitted (`[miss]` attribute and the `-miss` line), because emitting only one trades a board divergence for a narration one. probe: `tests/test-mechanics.js` `move/semiinvulnerable`; counter `medseen.statusmissedinvuln`. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-board-material-remainder.md` §5. (b) still open — the locked phantom force that announces and deals nothing on its second turn. untouched by the above, never staged, no instrument. instrument owed: a two-turn phantom force asserting damage on turn 2, control being the same pair with the lock broken

open.title: TWO PUBLISHED SEED-PREVALENCE FIGURES ARE WITHHELD — THE GENERATOR'S SPECIES LOOKUP DROPPED EVERY FORME — 2026-08-23, ME
open.full: two published seed-prevalence figures are withheld — the generator's species lookup dropped every forme — 2026-08-23, measure. `engine/rollout_seed_prevalence.js:95` read `mc.mons[base(sp)]`, and `base()` ends in `norm()`, which strips the hyphen `mc.mons` keys every forme with. so `rotom-wash` asked the table for `rotomwash`, got nothing, and was handed an empty dataset moveset — which the caller compares against the sheet's declared four and scores as *"the moves differ"*. a miss can only push `movesdiffer` up, so the bias is one-directional. measured over `data/games.bo3.jsonl`: 47 of 256 store species names, 10,980 of 144,260 brought bodies (7.61%); at the sheet-body level 19,236 of 231,924 bodies hit it and 7,177 (3.095% of all bodies) flip true → false once the row is found — top flippers floette-eternal 3,022, arcanine-hisui 1,919, lycanroc-dusk 1,059. withheld, not annotated (claude.md: *"a caption is not a quarantine"*), from `docs/search.md` r14 (the section headline, the one-line verdict, the prevalence table's `#248 moveset` and `any` rows, and the two r14 cells in the argmax-paired reach column), from `docs/miltank.md` §3.9, from this row's #248 closure text, and from `docs/medicham-sprint-notes.md`: `pct_248_bench_moves_differ` and `pct_any` of `data/rollout-seed-prevalence.json`. scope is bounded and measured, not assumed: `datasetmoves` is called at exactly one site in the generator and feeds only `movesdiffer`; `pct_any` is an or containing it. the other four rates — `17.655`, `17.053`, `13.089`, `0.061` — are computed independently and stand. no corrected value is estimated: the direction is known, the magnitude is not, and a body-level flip rate does not translate one-for-one to a decision point that ors over the whole live bench. the four rows closed on this batch (#247, #248, #249, #250) do not rest on the withheld figure and are not reopened — each closed on `tests/test-rollout-seed.js` shown red first with its own control, the prevalence figures were published as ceilings on reach beside them (`docs/search.md`: *"a ceiling on reach, not a count of flipped argmaxes"*), and the actual effect was measured separately and independently at 61/131 paired argmax flips under common random numbers (#278). #247's and #249's quoted shares are among the four unaffected. restored by a pinned re-run, not an unpinned one: `head -n 14102 data/games.bo3.jsonl > data/_seed-prev-pin.jsonl && node engine/rollout_seed_prevalence.js --store data/_seed-prev-pin.jsonl`. the store has grown 14,102 → 19,401 games since 2026-08-14, so an unpinned run is a different question; a correct pin must return `decisionpoints: 190378` exactly, which the bug cannot have touched. the lookup itself is already fixed and goes through `engine/mc_key.js` — verified by: `node tests/test-mc-key.js` scope narrowed 2026-08-24 by measure — the `verified by` on this row does not decide its open half, and the register was overstating because of it. `engine/register_reality.js` ran `node tests/test-mc-key.js`, read exit 0, and filed this row as the only stale row in the file — an open row whose instrument is green. that is correct and it is not evidence the row should close: the marker decides the lookup fix, which is landed and gated, and it is structurally incapable of deciding the withheld figures, which are restored only by the pinned re-run this row already specifies (`head -n 14102 data/games.bo3.jsonl > data/_seed-prev-pin.jsonl`, and a correct pin must return `decisionpoints: 190378` exactly). the two figures remain withheld, not annotated, and the re-run has not been done. instrument owed for the open half: nothing in the repository fails while those two figures are absent

open.title: `engine/position_features.js:249` READS A LIVE STONE-HOLDER’S DECLARED ABILITY WHERE `engine/board.js:3520` RESOLVES IT
open.full: `engine/position_features.js:249` reads a live stone-holder’s declared ability where `engine/board.js:3520` resolves it — one fact, two implementations. found 2026-08-23 by the runtime tripwire, which the retired count ratchet was green on. `priorityrefusedabove()` in `position_features.js` builds its defender list with `b.norm(f.mon.ability \|\| e.ability \|\| '')`; the identical function in `board.js` uses `effability(f.mon, dex)`. this is claude.md’s facts-are-global rule broken — a fact about the game living inside feature code and diverging. exposure is zero today and is re-derived on every run rather than asserted once: the value is consumed only by the `blocksmove{what:'priority'}` bar (`armortail`, `queenlymajesty`) and 0 legal megas gain or lose a `blocksmove` ability; the gate’s `guard()` goes red by name the day one does. fix: thread the dex into `priorityrefusedabove` and call `b.effability(f.mon, dex)`, then delete the `runtime_allowed` entry. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-23-identity-gate-permanent.md`. verified by: `node tests/test-effective-identity.js`

(`sim/battle.ts:429-460`) resolves a tie with a selection sort whose swaps move untied bodies past the tied pair, and a plain stable sort cannot produce that order. there are four places this engine sorts on speed: the move queue was fixed in 3.74.0, the entry pass was fixed 2026-08-23, and `engine/medicham2-browser.js:16787` (`_run.sort(…)`, the mega phase) and `:5487` (`residualorder`) still do not. the mega site is board-material — which body evolves first can decide which side spends its one mega — and the residual site is narration. both mega rows in the pinned pool are exact ties (starmie adamant 167 against charizard timid 167; two adamant/brave mawile at 112), so the class is already showing them; counts are small either way, 2 mega rows and 2 tailwind rows of 961. decision needed from will, and it is card 3 of `docs/_reports/2026-08-24-ordering-cards.md`: both remaining sites in one batch, or one at a time — they share a mechanism but land in completely different parts of the turn, and the standing rule is small batches. see #220 for the residual’s earlier slot-order-versus-speed history, which this does not restate re-scoped 2026-08-24 by measure to its remainder — the mega half landed the same night and the residual half did not. engine took the mega phase on its own rather than waiting on the batching ruling; its account is `docs/_reports/2026-08-24-mega-order.md`. the mechanism this row proposed was only half of it, and that is the part worth keeping. the authority's two `megaevo` actions sit at queue order 104, so they are the first group `speedsort` places and no swap made for a faster move can reach them — they keep the push order `addchoice` gave them (`sim/battle-queue.ts:306` pushes, it does not insert). this engine has no megaevo action at all and read the order off `acts`, which `sortturnorder` had already sorted for the moves, so the move sort's swaps had reversed the tied pair before the mega phase ever looked at it. so it was not only the algorithm, it was the list being sorted. `data/mechanics-census.json` (2026-08-24t20:59z) carries `item/megastone` *"a mega-phase speed tie keeps the queue order, not the move order"* live. measure did not re-verify that pass's game counts and says so: the engine run was still in flight at the time of this edit (`data/all-mechanics-fire.json` was being rewritten), so its pool figures are engine's own and the close belongs to engine once the tree settles. what remains in this row is the residual sort alone (`engine/medicham2-browser.js:5487`, `residualorder`) — narration, 2 tailwind rows of 961, and the same handler-list gap #355 and #440 both sit on. card 3 is therefore narrowed rather than answered: the batching question is moot for the mega site, and the question left is only whether the residual sort is worth taking now or waits for the handler list and the mega half is committed — measure, 2026-08-24, an hour after the paragraph above. engine committed it as `0a78640` (*the mega phase reads the authority's queue, and a tied pair had been reversed by the move sort*), `970a1c4` and `87d3a17`, and the tree settled at release `b35e96a0e7c7`. what measure has verified on the settled artifacts is the probe and not the pool arithmetic: the census carries the mega-phase tie probe live, and `data/game-differential.json` at that open.section: Solving — DUSK, and the retrograde idea
open.title: A ROLLOUT HAS NO COIN TO FLIP ON AN ENTRY TIE, SO IT TAKES ONE BRANCH DETERMINISTICALLY — FILED 2026-08-24 BY ENGINE, AN
open.full: a rollout has no coin to flip on an entry tie, so it takes one branch deterministically — filed 2026-08-24 by engine, and it is loud rather than silent. the entry tie is now decided by the shared `tie` die exactly as the move queue’s is. but a caller that hands `battleinit` no rng — every rollout, every census probe, miltank’s search — has no die, so the tied group keeps the order the selection sort handed it. `medfails.entryordertienodie` counts every occurrence, which is why this is a row rather than a hole. it is not a correctness defect against the authority: the differential pins the die to a constant on both sides anyway, so the measured whole-game number does not move either way. it is a search-quality question. decision needed from will, and it is card 4 of `docs/_reports/2026-08-24-ordering-cards.md`: leave rollouts deterministic on a tie (cheap, reproducible, biased to one branch), or give `battleinit` a die and accept that every existing seeded baseline in the repository shifts will ruled 2026-08-24, and the ruling splits the row in two. no die for rollouts — but a rollout must recognise that a tie is a tie and plan both branches rather than silently taking one and calling it the future. that is two pieces of work with two owners. the engine half is live: make the tie visible where it resolves, so a caller can see that the order it received was one branch of a coin rather than a fact. the search half is paused and is filed only, not queued — miltank is not being invested in while medicham is being corrected, so "plan both branches" is recorded here so it is not lost, and no work is scheduled against it. the cost the row named does not arise: no existing seeded baseline shifts, because no die is being added.

open.full: a move trap survives on our board after the authority has released it, and both narration streams agree — found 2026-08-24 by engine while closing the bounced-move line, filed by measure. the magic bounce scenario parts on the board at turn 4: `p2a feraligatr vol.trapped` reads showdown 0 / us 1, with the two protocol streams in agreement — so it is a state defect that the protocol arm structurally cannot see and only the board arm reports. it was already carried in the published artifact as `verdict: state`, so it is not a regression; open.title: A SINGLE-GAME REPLAY IS NOT REPRODUCIBLE IN ISOLATION, SO EVERY ISOLATED DEBUGGING SESSION IN THIS REPO IS QUIETLY UNREL
open.full: a single-game replay is not reproducible in isolation, so every isolated debugging session in this repo is quietly unreliable — found 2026-08-24 by engine, filed by measure. replaying one diverging pair on its own gives a different game from the same pair played in sequence inside the 961-game run, and the difference is not small: it changes which turn the game diverges on, and sometimes whether it diverges at all. measured twice inside one batch — the phazing game diverged at turn 3 as the 11th game in a process and at turn 1 played alone, on a mega-order speed tie between two identical aerodactyls; the redirect game diverged at turn 11 in sequence and at turn 10 on a different cause alone. the cause is named: the tie key and the mid-battle address log are process-scoped in a way the per-game reset does not fully clear, so a game's dice depend on how many games ran before it. it was shown not to be any one batch's doing — reproduced with `engine/medicham2-browser.js` reverted to head in the same isolated position. the consequence is the part that matters: a single-game replay is a fine way to read a divergence and a bad way to prove one was fixed; only the full run played in the same order on both arms is an attribution. nothing published has been shown wrong because of it — the standing figures all come from the sequenced run — but every `replay_one.js` session is affected. what would decide it: play one pair alone and at position n of a run with both engines' per-game reset instrumented and assert the first divergence is identical; then reset the tie key and the address log per game and assert it again. instrument owed

open.title: `tests/test-resolution-order.js` DIES OOM AT NODE'S DEFAULT HEAP, AND HAS BEEN RED FOR LONGER THAN ANY ONE BATCH — FOUND
open.full: `tests/test-resolution-order.js` dies oom at node's default heap, and has been red for longer than any one batch — found 2026-08-26 by engine. the file exits 134 with `fatal error: reached heap limit allocation failed` after printing ~17 `release store overridden` lines. it is not this batch's, proved rather than argued: `git show head:engine/medicham2-browser.js` was put in place and the file re-run — same exit 134, same message — and it also ooms with the batch's own behaviour knob switched off. the engine is fine: at `--max-old-space-size=6144` it passes, 26 arms staged, 1 known-open (the declared multi-hit granularity arm), 0 failing. the cause is named and not fixed: the file opens a release per arm and each snapshot loads the frozen engine plus its lazily-read data files, so ~26 of them are resident at once. why it matters beyond the red: every gate in this repo is read as an exit code, `tests/run-all.js` spawns children without a heap flag, and an instrument that dies on memory is indistinguishable at the exit code from an instrument that found a defect — which is this project's signature failure wearing the other hat. what would decide it: open one release for the whole file (the arms already share an id) or release each snapshot after its arm, then re-run at the default heap and assert exit 0 with the same 26/1/0 line. the runner half is closed 2026-08-27 by measure and the leak is not, and the two are deliberately not merged. this row named two defects in one paragraph: a per-arm snapshot leak in the check, and *"`tests/run-all.js` spawns children without a heap flag, and an instrument that dies on memory is indistinguishable at the exit code from an instrument that found a defect"*. the second is the runner's and is fixed: a check declares `abra-heap: <mb>` in its own header, `plan()` derives it and passes `--max-old-space-size` before the script path, and `--list` prints the honoured value so the derivation can be seen to have fired. it is derived from the child rather than tabled in the runner for the reason the ci job list was replaced — a table of costs goes stale and the staleness surfaces as exit 134 on a machine nobody is watching. and an oom still fails: it is annotated `out of heap`, never downgraded to a skip, because a crash filed as "did not run" is the same laundering as a crash filed as a verdict. verified by capturing the real argv of all 165 children with `spawnsync` stubbed — exactly one carries the flag — and by measuring that the flag moves the ceiling 2,240 mb → 6,336 mb in that position and does nothing at all after the script path. the leak is untouched and this row stays open on it: nothing was done to the 26 resident snapshots, and measure did not re-run the file (it plays games and engine held the play layer), so the 26/1/0 line is engine's measurement of 2026-08-26 and not a fresh one. instrument owed

open.full: the party is keyed by the displayed species, so a transformed body overwrites the one it copied -- measured 2026-08-26 by engine and held, because the re-key moves the sample. `duplicate_species_in_party` has read 20 on every pinned 961-game run and nothing acted on it. it is not a cosmetic tally: `partymap`'s second row overwrites the first, so one body is compared against the other engine's other body and the survivor is decided by whichever of them `sf.team` / `side.pokemon` lists last. one of the two remaining board-parted games is this -- `baseline ...2636042531 vs ...2635567733`, turn 3, `p2.party.garchomp` reading `hp/maxhp 123 vs 183`, `item lifeorb vs choicescarf`, `boosts.atk -2 vs 0`: one engine's row is a transformed ditto and the other's is the real garchomp it copied. the brief and #463's closing line both said both remaining games were this cause. they are not -- the other, `-damage: a different body` at turn 2, is a genuine spread-target divergence and survives the re-key untouched, so closing the party key takes board-material to one, not to zero. the sample answer, which is the point of the card: the ordered game list did not move (961 of 961, same pairs, same order) and 109 of 961 trajectories did. the list criterion is necessary and not sufficient and it gives the comfortable answer here -- under `--games n` the scheduler takes a fixed prefix of `pairscached`, so the pair list cannot move whatever the credit does; `data/whole-game-baseline.json` re-stamped at 18 of 961 = 1.9%, no `--force`. `party.species` and `party.types` are in the end-state worklist for the first time -- a transform one engine holds and the authority does not, on a row that had no stable name to be reported under before. the card's own prediction held: `-damage: a different body` at turn 2 survived the re-key untouched, so closing the key did not take board-material to zero. two things broke on the re-key and one was silent. the six bench plants built their expected path from `id(m.name)`, so `tests/test-state-differential.js` went 12 fails -- `caught=true`, `localised=false`, row `p2.party.lopunny.item` against a plant wanting `lopunnymega` -- attributed to this batch rather than assumed by re-running under `medi_party_key_display=1`, which was green; open.title: A DIVERGENCE PROPOSED AS `INCOMPARABLE` IS A SHARED-STREAM ADDRESS BUG, AND THE VOID GAME IT RIDES ON CANNOT BE SUBTRACT
open.full: a divergence proposed as `incomparable` is a shared-stream address bug, and the void game it rides on cannot be subtracted from the clause — refused and filed 2026-08-27 by measure. two findings, one game. (a) the declaration was refused. `-damage: a different body :: |-damage|p2a|h/h <> |-damage|p2b|h/h` (`...2635122796 vs ...2634861011`, turn 2) follows `|move|p1b: garchomp|outrage|p2a: staraptor` and medicham2 hit p2b. outrage is `randomnormal` (derived from the format), so the target is a draw — but it is a draw on a stream this harness shares. the authority falls `sim/battle.ts:2461` -> `:2484 getrandomtarget` -> `sim/side.ts:367 randomfoe()` -> `sim/prng.ts:136 this.random(items.length)`, and `battle.prng.random` is replaced at `engine/game_differential.js:3009`; medicham2 draws the generic `any` stream at `engine/medicham2-browser.js:20046`. same seed constant 20260813 on both sides, same fnv-1a, same `math.floor(u*2)` over foe lists in the same slot order — if the addresses matched, both engines would pick the same body deterministically. the address is ours and it is wrong: showdown resolves the target at `sim/battle-actions.ts:223`, above `setactivemove` at `:245`, with both fields nulled by `sim/battle.ts:2828 clearactivemove()` — `20260813|2|any|-|-|0` against this engine's `20260813|2|any|outrage|p20|0`, written at `:19878-19880` above the wire 144 draw at `:20043`. that is byte for byte the moody diagram, the fifth plausible "nothing to fix" in five days, and `midclearactivemove()` at `:19800` already fixes this class — it just runs before the write. the repair is engine's: address the `randomtarget` re-roll where the authority takes it, with a `medi_*` knob restoring the leak. predicted whole-game 13 -> 12 and board-material 4 -> 3 by a fix, not by an exemption; not measured. (b) a voided game is counted as a disagreement and the one-line fix is wrong. the arm voided this game (`mid_void.by_reason.low-identity 1`, `diverged 1`, every unshared address an `outrage` one) and `wholegameclause` still reads `j.diverged` 18 over `j.games` 961 — 13 published where the arm's own `usable_games 960` / `diverged_among_usable 17` supports 12. reading the void-adjusted pair is not the fix: `declaredgames` is accumulated by cause attribution over `classes[].causes[].n`, which still counts the void game, so the moment a void game's cause is itself declared the clause double-subtracts — 17-6=11 where the truth is 12, off by one in the direction that makes the gate look greener. `data/game-differential.json` records a count of void games and never which cause diverged on one; the repair is a `void_n` field beside `n` in `engine/game_differential.js`, which measure did not own in this batch. nothing moved this batch: `--whole-game` byte-identical at 1,810 bytes before and after, 13 of 961 both times, board-material 4 of 961, `--selftest` 109 passed 0 failed, `git diff engine/medicham2-browser.js` empty and `data/game-differential.json` unmodified against head.

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE MOVES QUEUE — the roster's moves stage, measured for the first time at 3.79.0 and worked down since. 52 → 40 → 32 →
open.full: the moves queue — the roster's moves stage, measured for the first time at 3.79.0 and worked down since. 52 → 40 → 32 → 25 → 23 fired-and-boards-differ, plus 24 did-not-fire and 91 could-not-stage, against 362 matching. 3.94.0 closed clanging scales and scale shot: showdown keeps the user's own stat change in two fields (`self.boosts` and `selfboost.boosts`) and the builder read one — the six moves using `self` all read match, which is exactly why it looked closed. 3.93.0 closed the partial-trap family — seven rows on one fact. bind, fire spin, infestation, sand tomb, snap trap, whirlpool and wrap each read `showdown 4 / ours 3` then `3 / 2`; identical deltas across seven independent rows is one fact, not seven bugs. `partialtrap: {turns:'4-5'}` was typed by hand and is the felt duration, while the compared quantity is showdown's `partiallytrapped` counter, which starts at 5 and is decremented in the residual of the turn the trap lands. the volatile-duration defect a third time (perish song, then #111's family) — it survived both because this counter lives in `_trap` and not `_vol`. now derived from the condition itself (duration, the `random(5,7)` range, the grip claw branch, `onstart`'s `bounddivisor`) and failing closed. red shown on the frozen pre-fix release. whole-game differential unmoved at 65/107. remaining clusters by corpus weight, which is not the order they look biggest in — `encore` alone is 6,102 uses, 55% of what is left, while the whole lock-in family is 101: 13 `move/plain-attack` (of which outrage/petaldance/ragingfury/thrash/uproar are one lock-in family), 4 remaining `move/volatile`, 9 `move/generic-status`, 6 `move/boosts-target`, 3 `move/multihit` (triple axel, scale shot, dragon darts — three different mechanics), 3 `move/fixed-damage`

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: TWO USAGE COUNTS EXIST AND NEITHER KNOWS ABOUT THE OTHER — but the engine queue is NOT where it bites. `data/meta-usage.
open.full: two usage counts exist and neither knows about the other — but the engine queue is not where it bites. `data/meta-usage.json` (what chomp reads) filters hard: collected 39,792 → after_bot_filter 13,263 → behavioural bots 10,480 → forfeits → min turns → full bring → 7,123 clean. `data/tags.json` (which every "n uses" in this project is quoted from) reads `loadcorpus({scope:'all'})` across `games.bo3` + `games.ots` + `games.ladder` — 11,429 games, 137,148 sheet entries, no bot filter and no quality filter. corrected 2026-08-10 by will, and the correction is the important half: *"it doesnt really matter because its not like bots can break the rules, the moves, mons, and items they use we still need to have in medicham right"*. exactly right. a bot cannot click an illegal move, so every entity it uses is one medicham must handle anyway — and the medicham gate demands zero differ and zero did-not-fire, so the count changes the order of work and never the destination. the unfiltered count is arguably the correct one for an engine queue: it measures exposure. where it does still bite is the opponent model — what a human will bring and click — which is what the bot filter exists for and what chomp consumes. so this is a measure item about `meta-usage.json`, not an engine item about the queue. *(an earlier draft of this row claimed three sources disagreeing 13x, citing a scan of `games.ladder.jsonl` alone that found 15 iron ball rows against tags.json's 139. that scan was wrong — ladder alone carries sheets on 1.7% of sides because the sheets live in the bo3 and ots files. the 139 is sound. retracted.)*

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: `new Battle()` VALIDATES NOTHING — a probe could measure a mechanic this format does not contain. Will: *"why dont we us
open.full: `new battle()` validates nothing — a probe could measure a mechanic this format does not contain. will: *"why dont we use showdowns teams validator that is universal truth"*. now it does. `engine/champions_sim.checklegal` asks the `teamvalidator` — the authority adr-002 names, through the instance `packteam` already builds — and splits its complaints into banned (the format does not contain this; always fatal) and pairing (this species cannot hold this; a legitimate isolation, declarable in writing). it catches strictly more than an `isnonstandard` check: *"meganium can't learn flamethrower"* is a legal move on a species that cannot have it, and that set was hand-staged on 2026-08-08. caught two defects in its own harness on the first run — `tackle` is `past` and every inert slot carried it, and the padding species were named from memory and included one not in the format. the sweep that followed (3.92.0) settled the blast radius: the `.item`/`.ability` assignment surface across 238 files is clean (one hit, `noability`, the blank sentinel), so the hazard this item was written about never actually fired — but move literals hit five sites, two of them defects. `test-priority-block.js` silenced three slots with splash, which has no `mc.moves` row at all, so the silencing worked through absence rather than through the move doing nothing; and `test-dead-volatile.js` guarded on `.exists`, which is true for a banned move, so the guard could never fire and the case always ran on thousand arrows. tightening that guard would have moved the hole rather than closing it, so the subject is derived from the format (smack down). still open: `staged_board.js` and `game_differential.js` (`buildpair`)

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE ROSTER SCRIPT LANGUAGE HAS NO SWITCH ACTION, AND `board_state.js` DOES NOT COMPARE TRAPPING AT ALL. Will, 2026-08-10
open.full: the roster script language has no switch action, and `board_state.js` does not compare trapping at all. will, 2026-08-10: *"we need to test the switch blocking like shadow tag, block, and the trapping moves, so we need to be able to switch in the test"*. the roster says it in its own source at `tests/roster.js:1814`. two layers, and they must not be confused: the engine switches fine — measured, `{kind:'switch', to: body}` through `battleturn`, and a partial trap correctly refused it while the untrapped control left freely — but the roster drives through the differential's script language, which cannot express the action, and even if it could the comparator has no field for trapping. that is why `block` reads inert: nobody ever tried to leave. covers the hard-trap moves (block, mean look, spider web, anchor shot, thousand waves), the partial-trap family's switch-prevention half (chip damage was closed at 3.93.0; the trapping half has never been compared), and the trapping abilities

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE WEATHER-CONDITIONAL MOVE FAMILY, SWEPT. Nine moves in this format change behaviour with the sky. Verified CORRECT an
open.full: the weather-conditional move family, swept. nine moves in this format change behaviour with the sky. verified correct and now on record rather than assumed: thunder and hurricane are never-miss in rain and 50 in sun; blizzard is never-miss in snow and untouched by sun; solar beam and solar blade closed under the precondition layer. broken: `growth` does not double in sun (sd +2/+2, ours +1/+1) — it read match for months and went red the moment its precondition was real, which is the sharpest argument for the precondition work there is. open: only growth. a later sweep at release `f727f7fdee4f` closed the rest and this line is corrected rather than left standing: `weatherscaled` has eleven members and five payload shapes, growth is the sole member carrying a `boosts` payload, weather ball now reads match (#96's fix took), and the other nine — including electro shot, which this item wrongly called untested — are all green under `move/needs-the-sky-it-names`. the remaining untested weather surface is on the ability side: `solarpower`, `raindish` and `icebody` all read control-not-quiet. `dig` appears in a naive weather scan and is a false positive — its weather mention is `onimmunity` (underground bodies take no sandstorm or hail chip), a different mechanic, recorded here so the next sweep does not re-find it as a bug

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: FIVE TAG SIGNATURES ARE CARRIED BY MOVES THE ENGINE TREATS DIFFERENTLY — so something other than the tag is deciding, an
open.full: five tag signatures are carried by moves the engine treats differently — so something other than the tag is deciding, and 105,709 uses sit on those signatures. generalised from #126 rather than left as one anecdote: every move in `data/tags.json` was resolved through `playeraction` on the frozen release and grouped by its sorted tag list. five groups split on the resolved kind, and a split can only mean a name match (forbidden here) or a tag missing the param that should separate them (#71). ranked: 96,406 `protect`+`detect` -> `protect` but `endure` -> `affect`, the highest-usage signature in the format carrying three behaviours — and `protectmoves` is an exported name list, which is the mechanism; 4,924 `wideguard` -> a branch, `quickguard` -> nothing (#126); 3,721 `roost`/`recover`/`slackoff`/`softboiled` -> `heal` while `wish` and `rest` -> nothing, because the tag says *heals self* and cannot express delayed or also-sleeps; 524 `beatup`/`hex`/`storedpower` -> `attack`, `spitup` -> nothing; 134 `bellydrum`/`tidyup` -> `statcode`, `acupressure` -> nothing. the last three overlap #125's dead list and groups a/b of the 13-row diagnosis, so the fix is shared. the check itself is the deliverable — it is cheap, it is derived, and it should be a gate: a signature whose members resolve to different kinds is either a name match or an under-specified tag, and both are defects by this repo's own rules

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: 'GOOD ENOUGH' IS A USAGE-WEIGHTED THRESHOLD, NOT A ROW COUNT — and by that measure the engine is already at 99.24%. Will
open.full: 'good enough' is a usage-weighted threshold, not a row count — and by that measure the engine is already at 99.24%. will, 2026-08-10: *'we do have to ask ourelves at what point is the engine good enough and has enough used features that it can perform its end goal'*. measured against the corpus rather than argued: 553,910 total move clicks; 781 (0.14%) land on a move that resolves to a whole no-op turn; 3,888 (0.70%) land on a move the roster says disagrees with the authority; the union is 4,208 = 0.76%. so 99.24% of real clicks land on a move with no known defect, and the game differential is 150/150 clean on real replayed games. the gate is a coverage standard and has been read as a sufficiency standard. its 45 open move rows are deliberately-staged edge cases, which is precisely why they survived — they barely occur. the honest test of sufficiency is roadmap #68: scale the differential from 150 games to 1,000+ real stored games. if it stays clean there, the remaining rows are polish and can run beside search work rather than blocking it, and the #99 quarantine can lift on a measured condition instead of a feeling. note the standing counter-evidence, which cuts the same way: `docs/measure.md` §0 carries a tight null at n=8,883 on the hypothesis that correctness fixes move the leaf at all

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE OPTIMIZATION PASS — hand MEDICHAM to Fable 5 and say make it faster, but only behind a correctness gate a stopwatch
open.full: the optimization pass — hand medicham to fable 5 and say make it faster, but only behind a correctness gate a stopwatch cannot fake. will, 2026-08-10: *'once we think medicham is good enough i plan to run some optimization programs to speed it up'* / *'handing it over to feeble 5 and saying make this go faster'*. dispatchable directly — the model is selectable per agent. the hazard is that 'faster' and 'different' are indistinguishable to a benchmark. an optimizer that shaves 30% by skipping a branch produces a beautiful number and a broken engine, and every existing test can still pass because those tests cover mechanics the branch never touches. so the pass runs three instruments, not one: `tests/bench-medicham.js` for the score (built 2026-08-10, pinned fixture, best-of-5, refuses to record a baseline under load — first reading 0.4341 ms/turn); the 500-move x 4-turn whole-board digest sweep for the verdict (2,000 cells; wire 147 used it to show only 11 moved, and that is the shape every optimization must reproduce at zero); and `tests/test-damage-stages.js` at 1728/1728 exact so arithmetic shortcuts cannot drift. sequencing, which decides how much work this is: the classifier cascade is both the most likely optimization target and the thing the remaining ~20 wires append to. restructure it first and the queued fixes land in the restructured version; do the wires first and the optimizer rewrites code that was just written

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE COST OF A FEATURE DEPENDS ENTIRELY ON WHICH PATH IT SITS IN, and the first measurement of that was taken 2026-08-10.
open.full: the cost of a feature depends entirely on which path it sits in, and the first measurement of that was taken 2026-08-10. will: *'how many of these features will slow down the engine? cause if it costs nothing to have harvest in there, then sure we can, but if there is a time cost to it then maybe we otta reconsider'* — the right question, and the answer splits cleanly. hot path — runs on every click of every rollout: the damage chain and the ~40-branch classifier cascade. tonight's five wires cost +6.2% (0.776 -> 0.825 ms/turn, interleaved a/b across frozen releases under load), and the per-hit damage loop is almost certainly all of it, being the only wire that touched damage. cold path — fires once per turn on a trigger, and is effectively free: harvest, cud chew, cheek pouch, quick guard, the heal family. so harvest specifically: yes, free. the thing to actually guard is compounding — 6% per five wires, twenty more wires, and the engine is ~25% slower to serve 0.76% of clicks. that trade stops being worth it well before the queue empties, which is the argument for #76's ratchet firing on every wire rather than at the end

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: A FEW MILLION SELF-PLAY GAMES TO PROVE THE SAMPLER FIRES AT THE RATE WE DECLARED — Will's idea, and the right tool for t
open.full: a few million self-play games to prove the sampler fires at the rate we declared — will's idea, and the right tool for the question it actually answers. *'once we feel our engine is good we can have it play a few million games and then determine if our rate for accuracy and secondary effects is right'*, then, on the distinction: *'correct run the million games after we determine'*. so: #132 first (is the declared number right — free, exact), then this (does the code fire at it — statistical). this catches the failure a probe structurally cannot: a probe forces the outcome to test the mechanic, so a secondary declared at 30% that a bug makes fire at 0% or 100% passes every probe and every roster row. that is claude.md's founding failure — a capability absent while everything reports success — in the one place the existing instruments are blind. cost is not a constraint: at the measured 0.4341 ms/turn and a mean 3.6-turn rollout, a million games is roughly half an hour. compare observed firing rates against the declared chances with a confidence interval per move, and expect the answer to be boring — the value is the one that is not

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE STORE REACHES FOUR FACTS AND THROWS THEM AWAY — and #68 needs every one of them. Will, reading the replay design: *'
open.full: the store reaches four facts and throws them away — and #68 needs every one of them. will, reading the replay design: *'i think multi hit moves say how many times they hit in the chat'*, *'life orb in the chat too'*, *'same with focus sash'*. all correct. `engine/durable-ingest.js` parses 30 protocol lines and drops these four: `|-hitcount|` (never read — so the differential skips 630 multi-hit rows as incomparable when the real hit count was on the wire); `|cant|` (never read — a flinched, paralysed, asleep, frozen or recharging body is simply an absent `m` event, indistinguishable from each other, 0 games in 52,089 carry a flinch marker); the `[from]` clause on chip damage — the parser tests for it to decide the damage is residual and then discards the text, so burn, sandstorm, life orb and rocky helmet all land as a bare `{t:'hp'}` with no source, and its own comment names them; `|-enditem|`, read only to infer what item a body held, never emitted as a turn event, so 'the focus sash triggered this turn' is gone. the store's event vocabulary is `b f fs hp m mega s w x`. this contradicts the project's founding principle — *store raw, analyze on top, every fact we might ever want* — at the parser. four regex arms; the raw replays can be re-pulled so no history is lost. ops work, touches no engine, and it makes #68 able to attribute a divergence instead of reporting an unexplained hp drop

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE SCENARIO CATALOGUE — one test SHAPE per mechanic, covering every move, ability, item and species. 920 entities carry
open.full: the scenario catalogue — one test shape per mechanic, covering every move, ability, item and species. 920 entities carry 217 distinct tags, so 217 shapes cover all of them and an entity added tomorrow inherits its shape without an edit; plus 357 legal species as one `structural` shape that needs no battle, only a comparison against the format. ten archetypes, and the archetype decides which instrument can ask the question — `chance` tags are marked so nobody builds a one-board test for a coin. two fields make it work and both are will's: `faces`, the adversary's action as distinct from the subject's precondition (*"wide guard needs a spread move against it, its pointless to test if it doesnt face that"*), without which a shape passes by doing nothing — and it explains the could-not-stage pile; and a property tested through its reactor (*"have contact hit rough skin to check"*), which resolves the `contact` flag's 166 moves in one shape. built by `engine/scenario_catalogue.js`, written to `data/scenario-catalogue.json`

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE PP FACT HAS TWO READERS UNTIL ENGINE ADOPTS THE SHARED ONE. `medicham2-browser.js`'s `ppMax` / `ppLeft` / `ppDeduct`
open.full: the pp fact has two readers until engine adopts the shared one. `medicham2-browser.js`'s `ppmax` / `ppleft` / `ppdeduct` / `ppallout` / `pppressureextra` are file-local — on neither `module.exports` nor `root` — so `board.js` cannot call them, and #145 had to put the fact in `engine/pp.js` rather than copy it. that is claude.md's *"two files that both decide choice scarf is x1.5"* hazard, live. it is guarded rather than declared: `tests/test-pp-fact.js` plays real turns and asserts that the number medicham writes into its own `_pp` equals the number `pp.js` gives, across every maxpp tier in the format. the ask is one edit in engine's file — have those five delegate to `engine/pp.js`, or export them and let `pp.js` become a thin adapter — so that one implementation remains. two further items found while wiring. `board.js` writes `b._pp` by name, which ought to be an engine-supplied setter rather than a string literal in a consumer. and `docs/_outbox/pp-and-moldbreaker-notes.md` states that `floor(base*0.8)+4` fits 500 of 500 rows: it fits 499, because struggle carries `noppboosts` and stays at 1/1 where the formula gives 4. nothing downstream is wrong — the number is read, never computed — but the claim would have to break before the artifact did

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: TWO SHIPPED COMMITS CITE ROADMAP NUMBERS THAT WERE NEVER REGISTERED, AND A LATER AGENT REUSED THEM. Commits `0a28580` (4
open.full: two shipped commits cite roadmap numbers that were never registered, and a later agent reused them. commits `0a28580` (4.1.0) and `e7d672a` (4.2.0) name "roadmap #145" and "roadmap #146" in their messages and in `docs/medicham-sprint-notes.md`. neither number existed in §5 — head's register stopped at #143. the search agent then correctly took #145 and #146 as the next free numbers for the pp work, so those two numbers now mean two different things depending on whether you read a commit message or the register. the findings are re-registered here as #147 (grounded axis) and #148 (sixth gate clause); the commit messages cannot be rewritten and are left alone, which is why this row exists. `tests/test-roadmap-register.js` did not catch it and is not wrong to have missed it — it checks that every item a division ledger schedules is named in §5, and these citations were in a commit message and the sprint notes, neither of which it reads. widening it to those two sources is the fix; until then a number in a commit message is not a registered number

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: `status.js` STAMPS UTC WHILE EVERY DATED ARTIFACT USES LOCAL, SO ANY RUN AFTER 20:00 EDT IS DATED TOMORROW. Measured 202
open.full: `status.js` stamps utc while every dated artifact uses local, so any run after 20:00 edt is dated tomorrow. measured 2026-08-10 20:43 edt: `engine/medicham2-browser.js` has mtime `2026-08-10 20:41:29 -0400` and `docs/search.md`'s generated block renders it as `2026-08-11 00:40`. a changelog entry written in the same session was stamped `[4.4.0] — 2026-08-11` against a real date of the 10th and had to be corrected by hand. this is small and it is exactly the class this repository keeps paying for: an artifact that looks newer than it is, feeding a staleness comparison that then reads backwards. `engine/provenance.js` already had to stop comparing mtimes for this family of reason. fix: one date function, local, called by everything that stamps — the facts are global rule applied to the clock

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: `data/status.js`'s GRAPH ROW NAMES THE WRONG BUILDER, WHICH IS WHY #153 WAS INVISIBLE. `engine/provenance.js` attributes
open.full: `data/status.js`'s graph row names the wrong builder, which is why #153 was invisible. `engine/provenance.js` attributes it to `engine/build-status.js`, which reads `policy-eval.json` and friends and is clear. the file's own header says it is generated by `build/build_status.js`, which reads two withheld artifacts — so the row that would have made `data/status.js` quarantined was never computed. two builders with almost the same name, one stale, and the graph followed the stale one. neither file may be deleted on this reasoning alone and web may not touch either; what is owed is a decision about which builder is live and a re-classification. related: `data/games.h2h-joint-trained.jsonl` and `data/games.h2h-tags2.jsonl` have no row at all, so doduo's and mew's evidence lines resolve to *unclassified* — the site withholds them on the ground that unclassified is not cleared, and that withholding expires by itself the day either file gets a row that clears.

open.section: Measurement integrity
open.title: THE CANONICAL SPEED BENCHMARK HAS NEVER HAD SIX BODIES, AND ITS STORED NUMBER WAS INVALID THE DAY IT WAS RECORDED — TYPE
open.full: the canonical speed benchmark has never had six bodies, and its stored number was invalid the day it was recorded — typed literal repaired 2026-08-27 by measure, re-record owed. `tests/bench-medicham.js` pinned `roster = [... 'amoonguss']`, a species that is `isnonstandard: 'past'` here and that `data/engine-data.js` has never carried — zero key hits on every commit that touched the file back to 2026-07-23, including `9a060821` on the day the benchmark was written. at the baseline commit `5884fd23` `buildmon` was `const m = monrow(name); if (!m) return null;`, and every game draws all six roster indices exactly once, so all 120 games ran with a null body on one side; `turns: 450` against a 120x12 cap is the fingerprint. `data/medicham-bench.json`'s 0.4614 ms/turn is withdrawn — it timed five bodies and a hole. today `monkey` throws (`engine/lookup.js`, armed 2026-08-02) so the file cannot run at all: the benchmark roadmap #76/#61 exists to provide has been dead and silent. repaired: the slot now holds toxapex, derived rather than picked — the highest team-rate legal, mc-carried, buildmon-safe body whose built set is majority-status, retains a damaging move and sits in the sub-56 speed tier amoonguss occupied (3.63% of teams / 1,554 games; regenerator, leftovers, infestation / toxic / wide guard / baneful bunker; `checklegal` legal, as are the other five). two guards added, both aimed at the exact failure: `mk()` throws on a null body instead of playing a hole, and the comparison refuses when `base.roster` differs from `roster` — the artifact has always carried the roster and nothing compared it, so the file's own "changing this list invalidates every stored number" was prose. owed: `node tests/bench-medicham.js --record` on a quiet machine. this batch may not play a game. until it is run there is no speed baseline for medicham and no optimization may claim a delta. report: `docs/_reports/2026-08-27-typed-literals.md`

open.title: `g.sets` DUPLICATES EVERY MOVE THAT WAS BOTH DECLARED AND CLICKED, ON 97.96% OF THE CORPUS MAG IS FITTED ON — FILED 2026
open.full: `g.sets` duplicates every move that was both declared and clicked, on 97.96% of the corpus mag is fitted on — filed 2026-08-27 by measure, not fixed (engine/ops). on an open-sheet game the revealed set merges the sheet's move spelling with the log's spelling without normalising. printed rather than described, `gen9championsvgc2026regmbbo3-2653849509`: `g.sets.kangaskhan.moves = ["fakeout","lastresort","fake out","last resort"]` against a declared sheet of `["fakeout","lastresort"]`. measured: 84,761 of 263,859 bo3 revealed sets (32.12%) repeat a move id, in 20,370 of 20,795 games (97.96%); 90,531 sets carry more than four revealed moves, up to thirteen. `games.ots.jsonl` 16,695 of 52,964 sets (31.52%) in 99.23% of games. the control is exact: on the closed-sheet ladder the defect appears in 1,410 games and 1,410 of 1,410 carry a sheet, 0 do not, against 1,432 sheeted games in the store — so the sheet-merge path is the cause and nothing else is. it is not a legality bug and it shows up as one: it produces 200 of `games.bo3.jsonl`'s 221 `teamvalidator` move complaints and 43 of `games.ots.jsonl`'s 46, which is why the illusion signature reads 9.05% there against 86.8% on the ladder. the store stays raw — the repair is in the reveal path in `engine/durable-ingest.js`, not a rewrite of stored lines, and `engine/durable-ingest.js` is not measure's. until it lands, no measurement may read `g.sets[x].moves` on an open-sheet game as a moveset. whether the duplicate reaches mag's features is unmeasured and is downstream of the fix. report: `docs/_reports/2026-08-27-bo3-unjudged.md`
