open.full: the last board-material game is an unshared die, not a rule - filed 2026-08-27 by engine, not a defect in medicham and not engine's to fix. `seed ...2635122796 vs ...2634861011` t2: `p2.party.staraptor.hp` medicham 160 / showdown 87 and `p2.party.incineroar.hp` 106 / 170 - the classifier calls it `-damage: a different body` and the two engines aimed one outrage at two different foes. the harness sent no target, and that is correct: `chooseaction` and `scripted` deliberately name none for the `randomnormal` family, and showdown then ignores any targetloc it was given - `if (move.target !== 'randomnormal' && this.validtargetloc(...))` in `battle#gettarget` falls straight through to `getrandomtarget`. each engine draws the target from its own prng, and the arm's shared streams are `acc / crit / sec / dmg / stall`: there is no sixth category for a target draw. neither engine is wrong. the instrument already knows and says so in the same run: `void (instrument desync): 1 of 961`, `mid_void.by_reason['low-identity'] = 1`, and every unshared address shape in the artifact is `outrage` (`acc/crit/dmg outrage [sd only]` 2 each, `[me only]` 1 each; `unshared_address_field_rollup: { target differs: 3, turn differs: 3 }`). why it is not fixed here: sharing the draw means a sixth arm category in `engine/game_differential.js`, which is the instrument and not the play layer, and adding one changes every arm's dice and therefore every published rate. same shape as the exact speed tie - showdown picks one, we pick the other - and it is will's call whether the instrument grows the category or the game stays declared. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-27-last-four.md` measured 2026-08-27 by engine after will ruled "fix the address" (option b, explicitly over declaring it incomparable). the landing was conditioned on a collision proof and the proof came back the other way, so nothing was landed and board-material is unmoved at 1 of 961. `tests/probe_random_target_address.js`, release `7f7de860723b`, arm middle, 961 games, pinned pool and census. the authority's blank `any` bucket is eleven call sites, not one, read off the real stack rather than reasoned about: of 1,332 blank-bucket draws only 137 (10%) are the `runmove` -> `gettarget` -> `getrandomtarget` draw the fix is about. the largest is `battle#getactionspeed` (380), which calls `gettarget` on every move action every turn just to hand `modifypriority` a target (`sim/battle.ts:2641`) and falls through to `getrandomtarget` for a randomnormal move exactly as `runmove` does; then `battlequeue.addchoice` (203), `insertchoice` (164) and the residual `fieldevent` sample (274). none of those four is a draw this engine makes at all, so 291 of 668 base addresses (43.6%) carry more than one draw, deepest 12, and the authority's target draw sits at nth 1..11 and never 0 while ours would be near 0 (our own blank bucket: 603 draws, 429 bases, deepest 3). the two engines would share a base and not an address. it would have worked anyway, 136 of 137 (99.3%) against a 65.0% coin floor — and that is a weakness in the hash rather than a shared die. fnv-1a ends `h = (h ^ c) * 0x01000193`, so the trailing index translates the value modulo 1 instead of mixing it: swept over 2,000 bases a one-digit index moves it by at most 0.0352 and a two-digit index by 0.4999. on the 137 real draws the circular step is at most 0.1622 and the closest any multi-candidate value came to a boundary was 0.0129, so one draw flipped — `baseline ...bo3-2654515998 vs -2654545512`, `20260813\|5\|any\|-\|-\|10`, authority picks 0 and blanked-at-0 picks 1. that is the collision, in a real game, on the pinned pool. what landing would have done, measured: `--focus 2635122796` prints the only random-target draw in the board-material game — `20260813\|2\|any\|-\|-\

open.title: EIGHT COMMENTS NAMED A SOURCE FILE THAT IS NOT THERE — SIX CORRECTED 2026-08-27 BY MEASURE, TWO OWED BY ENGINE. A commen
open.full: eight comments named a source file that is not there — six corrected 2026-08-27 by measure, two owed by engine. a comment naming a repo `.js`/`.py`/`.html` file asserts that file exists. of 2,822 such references in `engine/`, `tests/` and `build/`, eight named something absent and did not say so (a negation within 200 characters clears it). this row as first filed said "not measure's to fix" and that was wrong about six of the eight — they sat in files measure owns; the misrouting is recorded rather than edited away. corrected, each repointed at what is actually true rather than deleted: `build/build_mag_data.js` said *"web/magnemite.html carries a self-check against a fixture generated here"* — 32 days, the worst; no such page has ever existed, the room is `roommagnemite()` and the check is `magselfcheck()`, both in `web/index.html`, and it detects a bundle-vs-engine vintage mismatch rather than two scorers diverging (the page stopped re-implementing `featuresfor` and calls `board.js` live, so the sentence was wrong twice). `engine/prior_player.js` *"see tests/test-policy-parity.js"* — 34 days, the oldest; no such test, and `setpurepriors()` in `engine/medicham2-browser.js` is the real switch and has no caller, so the like-for-like comparison has never been run. `engine/lookup.js` *"tests/test-lookup-contract.js reads this"* — 25 days (first written 2026-08-02, not the 21 days first reported); no such test, and `misses()` has no reader at all. `engine/million_run.js` *"engine/status_residual.js asserts it"* — 16 days; the identity guard is real and is the `if (dump_status)` block in that same file, which refuses to write on a mismatch. `engine/speed_vs_pokeenv.js` *"arm a lives in engine/bench_pokeenv.py"* — 16 days, printed to the operator at run time and written into `data/speed-vs-pokeenv.json`'s `what` field as a third arm that does not exist; arm a is unwritten and both now say so. `engine/quarantine.js` named `web/scoreboard.js` where `data/scoreboard.js` was meant — 13 days. still open, both in engine's files: `engine/game_differential.js` names `tests/rate_runner.js` (15 days; the instrument that derives its trials from statistical power is `engine/million_run.js`) and `engine/medicham2-browser.js` names `tests/test-engine-contract.js` (34 days; `tests/test-engine-consistency.js` is the file that holds the two engines together). re-derived on every run of `node tests/test-claim-truth.js`, which reports 2 of 2,822, down from 8. no engine byte moved and no game was played. account: `docs/_reports/2026-08-27-false-claims.md`

open.title: position against THREE comparables, because the field is not empty and none of them is playing our game. VGC-Bench (AAMA
open.full: position against three comparables, because the field is not empty and none of them is playing our game. vgc-bench (aamas 2026) — whose archive we already consume, and dropped from the fit for staleness (four days, mid-june, seven weeks old); `engine/corpus_shift.js` exists to measure the metagame distance and has never written an artifact. future sight ai — closed-source showdown bot, reportedly top 5% of the most popular format, matches revealed attributes to the most common set, ships a win-probability browser extension; also settles a naming question, since "future sight" is taken and this project names everything after pokémon. the pokeagent challenge (arxiv 2603.15563, neurips 2025, 100+ teams, two tracks) — by far the strongest reference of the three and not yet read. add sarantinos (arxiv 2212.13338, cambridge) as the closest published method: gen 7 random battles singles, peaked 33rd in the world, regret-minimisation opponent prediction, fills unknown properties from usage statistics, and explicitly rejects monte carlo sampling as too sample-inefficient — which is what miltank's leaf does. it also names our #29 independently: its first "biggest challenge" is keeping the team balanced, with a worked example that is the sack, and it asserts *"an ai agent cannot achieve this just by looking ahead with minmax or monte carlo tree search."* finally, its elo caveat is load-bearing for will's stated goal: comparing human and ai ratings is invalid unless they played each other — laddering with alakazam is exactly that, so the plan is sound and should say why
